items.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF
items.spec: Replace Morgan features with all RDKit Descriptors (Descriptors.descList) computed per molecule, with nan/inf replaced by 0 and values clipped to +-1e6. Keep the RandomForest (max_features 0.3). Caco-2 depends on TPSA, logP, HBD and similar, which fingerprints capture poorly.

items.title: Descriptors + count Morgan concat
items.spec: Concatenate RDKit 2D descriptors (cleaned) with a Morgan count fingerprint (radius 2, 1024 bits, count simulation) and fit the RF on the combined matrix.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors
items.spec: Use RDKit descriptors with LGBMRegressor (n_estimators 400, lr 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10, reg_lambda 1, n_jobs 8, random_state seed).

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Fit CatBoostRegressor (iterations 800, depth 6, lr 0.04, loss MAE or RMSE, thread_count 8, random_seed seed, verbose 0) on cleaned RDKit descriptors.

items.title: MAE objective
items.spec: With a gradient boosting model, switch the loss to L1 or Huber (Huber alpha about 0.5) since the metric is MAE and the targets have outliers. Alternatively use RF criterion absolute_error.

items.title: Small physchem descriptor set
items.spec: Use a hand-picked set of about 15 descriptors: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, RingCount, NumAromaticRings, HeavyAtomCount, LabuteASA, charge counts, and the fraction of N+O atoms. Use ExtraTrees or RF on them. Less noise on 728 samples.

items.title: ExtraTrees on descriptors
items.spec: Replace the RF with ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.5, min_samples_leaf 2) on descriptors, possibly concatenated with Morgan counts.

items.title: RF+LGBM+CatBoost ensemble
items.spec: Average the predictions of an RF, an LGBM and a CatBoost model, all on descriptors plus Morgan counts. Use equal weights.

items.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Compute a Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) with numpy and fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1). Consider averaging it with the tree models.

items.title: Gaussian process Tanimoto
items.spec: Use kernel ridge regression with a Tanimoto kernel on count Morgan fingerprints (alpha about 0.3), with the target mean-centered. Return the predictions, and blend 50/50 with the RF.

items.title: MACCS keys addition
items.spec: Add 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys) to the features, concatenated with Morgan or descriptors, for the RF.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion counts
items.spec: Add hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 1024, counts) to the feature set. Fit an RF.

items.title: Feature-based Morgan (FCFP)
items.spec: Use Morgan with a feature-invariant atom generator (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen), radius 3, count-based, 1024 bits, in place of the ECFP bits. This gives pharmacophore-level generalization across scaffolds.

items.title: RF hyperparameter tune
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=2, MAX_FEATURES=0.2 and N_TREES=500 on the current features. Smoother averaging may help when the test scaffolds are unseen.

items.title: Feature selection by variance/correlation
items.spec: Drop constant features and features with fewer than 5 non-zero molecules in the training set, and drop one of each descriptor pair with |corr|>0.95. Then fit the RF.

items.title: Ridge on descriptors
items.spec: Standardize the descriptors (clip to the 1st-99th percentile of train, then StandardScaler) and fit RidgeCV or Lasso. Blend it with the RF at 0.3 weight to add a linear trend.

items.title: Residual stacking
items.spec: Fit ridge on the standardized descriptors, then fit an RF or LGBM on the residuals, using Morgan counts plus descriptors. Prediction is ridge + RF residual.

items.title: Target winsorizing
items.spec: Clip train_y to its 2nd-98th percentile before fitting, which reduces the influence of outliers on MAE.

items.title: Median-based forest aggregation
items.spec: Take the median of the per-tree predictions of the RF (stack estimators_ predictions) instead of the mean. This suits the MAE metric.

items.title: XGBoost on mixed features
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor (hist, 500 trees, depth 4, lr 0.03, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.4, objective reg:pseudohubererror or absolute error) on descriptors plus MACCS.

items.title: MLP on descriptors
items.spec: Use a sklearn MLPRegressor (128,64 hidden, alpha 1e-2, early stopping) on standardized, quantile-transformed descriptors. Bag 5 seeds and blend with the trees.

items.title: Seed bagging of boosters
items.spec: Train 5 LGBM models with different seeds and subsample settings and average them, to reduce variance on the small data.

items.title: Crippen/Gasteiger partial-charge features
items.spec: Add features from Gasteiger charges: the sum of charges on polar atoms, the max and min charge, and the PEOE_VSA and SlogP_VSA descriptors (already in descList). Also add polar surface area variants (TPSA with S and P). Use these with the RF.

items.title: Count-based Morgan with log1p
items.spec: Use Morgan counts (radius 2, 2048 bits, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) transformed with log1p instead of bits, and use them with the RF.

items.title: Rule-based flags
items.spec: Add flags: Lipinski violations, Veber rule (TPSA>140, rotatable bonds>10), carboxylic acid, basic amine, quaternary N, and number of charged groups (via SMARTS). Append them to the descriptors. They capture efflux and permeability heuristics.

items.title: Salt stripping and canonicalization
items.spec: Before featurizing, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges (Uncharger). Apply it consistently to train and test.

items.title: Internal-CV stacked blend weights
items.spec: Within fit_predict, compute 5-fold out-of-fold predictions for 3 base models (RF-descriptors, LGBM, SVR Tanimoto). Fit a non-negative linear regression on them to set the blend weights, then predict.

items.title: kNN Tanimoto blend
items.spec: Add a KNeighborsRegressor with a Tanimoto-like metric (jaccard on bits, k=5, distance weighted) and blend it at 0.2 weight with the main model.

items.title: Descriptor + Morgan LGBM with feature_fraction low
items.spec: Use LGBM on descriptors plus 1024 Morgan counts with colsample_bytree 0.2, extra_trees=True, lr 0.02 and 800 trees, num_leaves 8, min_child_samples 8.

items.title: Quantile-transform descriptors for SVR RBF
items.spec: Apply a QuantileTransformer (normal output) to the descriptors, drop constant columns, and fit SVR(RBF, C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'). Average it with the RF.

items.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF
items.spec: Replace Morgan features with all RDKit Descriptors.descList values (nan_to_num, clip to +-1e6, float32). Keep the RandomForest. Descriptors such as TPSA, logP, HBD and MolWt are strongly tied to Caco-2 permeability.

items.title: Descriptors plus count Morgan concat
items.spec: Concatenate RDKit 2D descriptors with Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Use the RF with max_features=0.3.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors
items.spec: Use RDKit descriptors as features and replace the RF with LGBMRegressor (n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1).

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use RDKit descriptors as features and fit CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, loss_function='MAE', random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8).

items.title: ExtraTrees on descriptors
items.spec: Use RDKit descriptors with ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.5, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed).

items.title: Small curated descriptor set
items.spec: Use about 15 hand-picked descriptors: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, RingCount, NumAromaticRings, HeavyAtomCount, LabuteASA, and charge counts. Fit a GBM or RF on them. This tests whether low-dimensional features generalize better to unseen scaffolds.

items.title: MAE/Huber objective
items.spec: Train the GBM or RF with an MAE-like objective: LightGBM objective='huber' (alpha=0.5), or RF criterion='absolute_error'. The loss is MAE, so this may help.

items.title: Ensemble RF + LGBM + CatBoost average
items.spec: Average the predictions of an RF, an LGBM and a CatBoost model, all on descriptors + Morgan counts. Equal weights.

items.title: MACCS keys addition
items.spec: Add MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the descriptor features. Fit RF or GBM.

items.title: Atom pair / topological torsion counts
items.spec: Use count-based atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048) combined with descriptors. Fit RF.

items.title: Morgan feature invariants (FCFP)
items.spec: Use a Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 2, counts, concatenated with descriptors.

items.title: Ridge/SVR on scaled descriptors
items.spec: Standardize the descriptors (clip to +-5 sd after scaling), then fit SVR(C=3, epsilon=0.1, rbf kernel). Smooth models can extrapolate to new scaffolds better.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR/KRR
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (minmax kernel). Fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5) or kernel ridge.

items.title: Gaussian process on descriptors
items.spec: Fit a GaussianProcessRegressor with a Matern kernel + WhiteKernel on standardized selected descriptors (top 30 by RF importance inside fit_predict).

items.title: Feature selection by RF importance
items.spec: In fit_predict, fit a quick RF on descriptors + fingerprints, keep the top 150 features by importance, then refit the final model on those. Remove constant features first.

items.title: Stacking RF + SVR + GBM
items.spec: Use sklearn StackingRegressor with RF, SVR (scaled descriptors) and LGBM as base models and RidgeCV as the final estimator, cv=5.

items.title: RF hyperparameter tune
items.spec: On the descriptor features, set min_samples_leaf=2, max_features=0.33, n_estimators=600. Try max_samples=0.8.

items.title: LGBM stronger regularization
items.spec: LightGBM with num_leaves=7, min_child_samples=15, reg_lambda=5, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=800, extra_trees=True, colsample_bytree=0.3.

items.title: XGBoost on descriptors
items.spec: XGBRegressor(n_estimators=600, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.4, min_child_weight=3, reg_lambda=3, objective='reg:absoluteerror', n_jobs=8, random_state=seed).

items.title: Seed-bagged GBM
items.spec: Fit 5 LGBM models with different seeds (seed+i) and bagging/colsample randomness, and average them to cut variance.

items.title: Crippen/EState/VSA fragment features
items.spec: Add the EState fingerprint counts (rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol counts and sums) to the descriptors. Use a GBM.

items.title: Neutralize and desalt molecules
items.spec: Before featurization, take the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize it (Uncharger). Use with descriptors.

items.title: Target winsorizing
items.spec: Clip the training targets to the 2nd–98th percentile before fitting, to reduce the effect of outliers on tree splits.

items.title: Median-of-trees RF prediction
items.spec: Take the median over per-tree predictions of the RF (model.estimators_) instead of the mean, since the metric is MAE.

items.title: Pharmacophore 2D Gobbi / Pharm2D fingerprint
items.spec: Add counts of H-bond donor/acceptor pair distances using rdkit Pharm2D Gobbi_Pharm2D fingerprint (folded to 1024), concatenated with descriptors.

items.title: Polar surface and ionization SMARTS counts
items.spec: Add SMARTS counts for carboxylic acid, basic amine, quaternary N, sulfonamide, amide, phenol, and Lipinski violations, plus descriptors. These are flags relevant to permeability and efflux.

items.title: kNN-residual correction
items.spec: Fit a GBM, then fit a kNN (k=5, Tanimoto/Jaccard on Morgan bits) on out-of-bag residuals and add a shrunken correction (0.5) to the predictions.

items.title: MLP on scaled descriptors ensemble
items.spec: Use sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden (128,64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping, max_iter=500) on quantile-transformed descriptors. Average 5 seeds and blend 50/50 with the LGBM.

items.title: Rank-average blend of tree and kernel models
items.spec: Fit an LGBM on descriptors and an SVR on Tanimoto kernel counts. Average their predictions with weights 0.6/0.4.

items.title: Drop highly correlated descriptors
items.spec: Remove descriptors with abs Pearson correlation above 0.95 to an earlier column and zero-variance ones, computed on the training set. Then fit the GBM.

items.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF
items.spec: Replace Morgan features with all RDKit Descriptors.descList values (nan_to_num, clip to ±1e6) computed per molecule. Keep the RandomForest (max_features 0.3). Descriptors like TPSA, logP, HBD capture permeability well.

items.title: Descriptors concatenated with count Morgan
items.spec: Concatenate RDKit descriptors with Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Fit the RF on the combined matrix.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors
items.spec: Use RDKit descriptors as features and LGBMRegressor (n_estimators 500, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10, verbose -1, random_state seed, n_jobs 8) instead of RF.

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use RDKit descriptors with CatBoostRegressor (iterations 800, depth 6, learning_rate 0.03, loss MAE or RMSE, random_seed seed, thread_count 8, verbose 0).

items.title: MAE objective for GBM
items.spec: With descriptor features and LightGBM, use objective 'huber' or 'l1' since the metric is MAE and the targets may have outliers. Compare to L2.

items.title: Small curated physchem feature set
items.spec: Use only about 15 descriptors: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, RingCount, NumAromaticRings, HeavyAtomCount, LabuteASA, charge counts, and the Crippen MR. Fit an ExtraTrees or RF model to cut noise from the 200 descriptors.

items.title: Extra Trees instead of RF
items.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1) on the current or descriptor features.

items.title: Ensemble RF + LightGBM + CatBoost
items.spec: Average predictions from an RF, an LGBM and a CatBoost model, all trained on descriptors plus Morgan counts. Use the mean or median.

items.title: SVR with RBF kernel on scaled descriptors
items.spec: Standardize the descriptors, using a QuantileTransformer or clipping, and fit SVR(C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale'). Predict with it.

items.title: Tanimoto kernel SVR/KRR
items.spec: Compute a Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count or bit fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). Fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5) or KernelRidge. Build the kernel with numpy matrix ops.

items.title: Gaussian process on Tanimoto + descriptors
items.spec: Use a kernel that sums the Tanimoto kernel and an RBF kernel on scaled key descriptors. Fit KernelRidge with alpha about 0.1, tuned by an inner validation.

items.title: MACCS keys added
items.spec: Add the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the feature set alongside descriptors and fit the RF.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints
items.spec: Use the rdFingerprintGenerator atom pair and topological torsion count fingerprints (fpSize 1024 each), concatenated with the descriptors. Fit LightGBM or RF.

items.title: Morgan with feature invariants (FCFP)
items.spec: Use a Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 3, count-based, 1024 bits, to capture pharmacophore-like features. Use with RF.

items.title: RF hyperparameter tune
items.spec: Set MAX_FEATURES to 0.5, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 2, N_TREES to 500 on the descriptor+Morgan features. Check whether smoother trees help on unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Drop low-variance and correlated features
items.spec: After computing the descriptors, drop features with zero variance in the training set and prune one of each pair with abs correlation above 0.95. Then fit the model.

items.title: Winsorize target
items.spec: Clip train_y to its 2nd–98th percentile before fitting, to reduce the effect of outliers on the fit. Predictions stay unclipped.

items.title: Feature selection by importance
items.spec: Fit a quick RF on all features, keep the top 100 by importance, and refit the final model on them. Do this only inside fit_predict using training data.

items.title: Stacking with ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Build out-of-fold predictions from RF, LGBM, SVR and CatBoost with 5-fold CV on the training set. Fit a non-negative linear regression on them and use it for the test predictions.

items.title: Multi-seed bagging
items.spec: Train the chosen model with 5 different seeds derived from seed (seed*10+i) and average. Use subsample or colsample to introduce diversity.

items.title: MLP on scaled descriptors
items.spec: Use sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden 256-64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping, adam) on quantile-transformed descriptors. Average 5 seeds.

items.title: XGBoost with shallow trees
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor (max_depth 4, n_estimators 600, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.7, colsample_bytree 0.4, reg_lambda 5, objective reg:absoluteerror) on descriptors plus MACCS.

items.title: Gasteiger charge / PEOE and EState features
items.spec: Add the VSA descriptors, such as PEOE_VSA, SlogP_VSA and SMR_VSA, and the EState fingerprint counts (Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol) to the features. Fit LightGBM.

items.title: Polar surface and H-bond emphasis features
items.spec: Add hand-made features: TPSA/MolWt, HBD+HBA, logP−0.01*TPSA, the count of carboxylic acids, basic amines and quaternary N via SMARTS patterns. They capture efflux and ionization effects. Append them to the descriptors and fit the model.

items.title: Canonical largest fragment / salt stripping
items.spec: Before featurizing, take the largest fragment using rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser and neutralize charges with Uncharger. Apply to train and test alike.

items.title: Sample weights by scaffold frequency
items.spec: Weight each training sample by 1/sqrt(count of its Murcko scaffold in the training set), and pass it to the fit. This reduces the dominance of large scaffold clusters, and the folds are scaffold-split.

items.title: kNN-Tanimoto blend
items.spec: Compute a kNN regressor (k=7, similarity-weighted) on the Morgan Tanimoto similarity. Blend 0.3 with the descriptor GBM prediction at 0.7.

items.title: Random-forest with quantile-median leaf prediction
items.spec: Take the median of the per-tree predictions instead of the mean, since the loss is MAE. Use model.estimators_ to compute it.

items.title: Rank-average target transform
items.spec: Standardize the targets (z-score) before fitting and invert the transform afterwards. This matters for SVR, MLP and GP and has little effect on trees. Apply it to the SVR/KRR model.

items.title: LightGBM DART with extra_trees
items.spec: Use LGBMRegressor with extra_trees=True, num_leaves 8, n_estimators 1000, learning_rate 0.02, colsample_bytree 0.3, reg_lambda 10 on the descriptors plus counts. This is a strongly regularized GBM for small data.

items.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors to fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, besides the Morgan bits, compute a block of RDKit descriptors per molecule (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, RingCount, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, NumAromaticRings). Replace NaN and inf with 0 and hstack them onto the fingerprint matrix before fitting the same RandomForestRegressor.

items.title: Full RDKit descriptor set with random forest
items.spec: Compute all values from Descriptors.descList for each molecule, clip each column to the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles of the training set, set NaN to 0, and concatenate with the Morgan bits. Keep the random forest unchanged.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same Morgan generator so each feature holds the occurrence count of a substructure rather than a 0/1 flag. The forest and its settings stay the same.

items.title: Larger radius with more bits
items.spec: Set RADIUS to 3 and N_BITS to 4096 so larger substructures are represented and bit collisions drop. Fit the same random forest on the resulting dense matrix.

items.title: Feature-invariant Morgan fingerprints (FCFP)
items.spec: Build the Morgan generator with the feature atom invariants so atoms are grouped by pharmacophore class (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than element identity. Keep radius 2, 2048 bits, and the same forest.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion fingerprints added
items.spec: Compute hashed atom-pair fingerprints and topological-torsion fingerprints (2048 bits each, count-based) with rdFingerprintGenerator, concatenate them with the Morgan bits, and fit the same random forest.

items.title: MACCS keys added
items.spec: Compute the 167 MACCS structural keys with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule and concatenate them to the Morgan bits before fitting the random forest.

items.title: LightGBM regressor with MAE objective
items.spec: Replace the random forest with LightGBM using objective regression_l1 (MAE), learning rate 0.05, around 600 trees, num_leaves 31, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, and random_state set to seed. Use the Morgan bit matrix as input.

items.title: CatBoost regressor on fingerprints
items.spec: Replace the random forest with CatBoostRegressor using loss_function MAE or Huber, depth 6, about 1000 iterations, learning rate 0.05, random_seed set to seed, and verbose off. Fit on the Morgan bit matrix.

items.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor with objective reg:absoluteerror, max_depth 5, learning rate 0.05, 600 estimators, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3, and random_state set to seed, fitted on the Morgan bit matrix.

items.title: Random forest and gradient boosting blend
items.spec: Train the existing random forest and a LightGBM regressor with L1 objective on the same features, then return the simple average of their test predictions.

items.title: Random forest with larger leaves for regularization
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 3 and MAX_FEATURES to sqrt of the feature count so each tree is smoother and less prone to fitting noisy labels. Keep everything else the same.

items.title: Random forest with more trees and smaller feature subsets
items.spec: Raise N_TREES to 1000 to reduce variance and set MAX_FEATURES to 0.1 to decorrelate trees. Keep the rest of the random forest unchanged.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (MinMax or Jaccard) kernel matrix between binary Morgan fingerprints for train-train and test-train pairs, then fit sklearn SVR with kernel set to precomputed, C around 5, and epsilon 0.1. Return predictions for the test molecules.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel Gaussian process or kernel ridge
items.spec: Use the same precomputed Tanimoto kernel as a kernel ridge regressor (sklearn KernelRidge with kernel precomputed and alpha around 0.3). Predict the test set from the test-train kernel. Use a fixed regularization value and no hyperparameter search.

items.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto regression as ensemble member
items.spec: For each test molecule, find the k=5 most similar training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits and predict the similarity-weighted mean of their labels. Average this with the random forest output.

items.title: Curated physchem features with gradient boosting
items.spec: Use a small set of about 15 chemistry-driven features: TPSA, MolLogP, MolWt, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, formal charge, counts of carboxylic acid, basic amine, and phenol groups, plus the number of rings. Fit a LightGBM L1 regressor on these features only.

items.title: Ionization-state features
items.spec: Count ionizable groups with SMARTS patterns for carboxylic acids, aliphatic amines, quaternary nitrogens, sulfonic acids, and tetrazoles. Append these counts and their sum to the Morgan bits before the random forest, since charge state strongly affects passive permeability.

items.title: Largest-fragment standardization before featurization
items.spec: Before computing fingerprints, strip salts and counterions by keeping the largest covalent fragment of each SMILES (Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with sanitizeFrags), neutralize charges when possible, and handle parse failures by falling back to the original string. Keep the model unchanged.

items.title: Log-transform or winsorize training targets
items.spec: Clip training labels to the 1st and 99th percentiles of train_y before fitting, which limits the influence of extreme measurements on MAE. Fit the same random forest and return predictions unchanged.

items.title: Median of tree predictions instead of mean
items.spec: After fitting the random forest, collect the per-tree predictions for each test molecule (model.estimators_) and return the median rather than the mean. The median is a closer match to the MAE objective and is more robust to outlier leaves.

items.title: Stacking with out-of-fold predictions
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold inner split on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from a random forest, a LightGBM L1 model, and a kernel model. Train a ridge regressor on these stacked predictions and apply it to the test-set predictions of the base models.

items.title: Small MLP on fingerprints
items.spec: Train sklearn MLPRegressor on the Morgan bit matrix with hidden layers of 512 and 128 units, ReLU activation, alpha 1e-3 for L2 regularization, early stopping with a 10 percent validation split, and random_state set to seed. Standardize targets before fitting and invert the transform on predictions.

items.title: Ridge regression on standardized descriptors as blend member
items.spec: Build a standardized feature matrix from RDKit descriptors and Morgan bits, fit RidgeCV with alphas in logspace from -2 to 3, and average its predictions with those from the random forest using equal weights.

items.title: Subsampled bagging ensemble of gradient boosters
items.spec: Train 5 LightGBM L1 models, each on a different random 80 percent subsample of the training molecules and each with a different seed derived from the seed argument, and average their test predictions. This reduces variance without changing the base learner.

items.title: Learning-rate schedule with early stopping for boosting
items.spec: Hold out 10 percent of training molecules as validation. Train LightGBM L1 with a decaying learning rate (lower it by half every 200 rounds) and early stopping after 50 rounds of no improvement on the validation MAE. Refit on the full training set with the chosen number of rounds.

items.title: Inner hyperparameter search selecting a model per fit
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, split off a validation portion of the training molecules, evaluate 4 random-forest settings (max_features in 0.1, 0.3, sqrt; min_samples_leaf in 1, 3), choose the one with lowest validation MAE, refit on all training data, and predict the test set.

items.title: Bootstrap fraction and max-samples tuning
items.spec: Set the random forest max_samples to 0.7 so each tree sees a smaller bootstrap sample, which adds diversity and regularization. Keep other settings the same and set bootstrap to True.

items.title: Random-subspace ensemble over fingerprint types
items.spec: Train several random forests on the Morgan bits, the MACCS keys, and the RDKit descriptor block separately, each with a different seed, then average their predictions. Use equal weights.

items.title: Multi-SMILES augmentation for training
items.spec: For each training molecule, generate 3 randomized SMILES strings with Chem.MolToSmiles(doRandom=True) using a seed derived from the seed argument, compute features for each, and train the random forest on all copies with the same label. At prediction time, average the predictions over the canonical and randomized SMILES of each test molecule.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace the bit-vector Morgan featurization with Morgan count fingerprints: use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048) and call GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy, so each bit holds the number of times the substructure occurs. Keep the RandomForestRegressor and all other settings unchanged.

items.title: Add RDKit physchem descriptors
items.spec: Append a small set of interpretable molecular descriptors to the fingerprint vector: molecular weight, Crippen logP, TPSA, H-bond donor count, H-bond acceptor count, rotatable bond count, aromatic ring count, heavy atom count, formal charge, and fraction sp3. Compute them with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors and rdMolDescriptors for each molecule, concatenate them to the Morgan bits, and keep the random forest unchanged. Permeability is strongly driven by these properties, so the trees can use them directly.

items.title: Full RDKit descriptor set
items.spec: Compute all RDKit 2D descriptors via rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList for every molecule, replace NaN and infinite values with 0, clip extreme values to the 0.1st and 99.9th percentiles of the training set, and concatenate the result with the Morgan fingerprint. Use the random forest as before. Compute the clipping bounds from train_smiles only, then apply them to test_smiles.

items.title: LightGBM with MAE objective
items.spec: Replace the random forest with LightGBM regression using objective='l1' (MAE), since the metric is mean absolute error. Use learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=5, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8 with bagging_freq=1, and n_estimators=600. Set random_state=seed and n_jobs=8. Train on the same Morgan bit features.

items.title: CatBoost on fingerprints
items.spec: Replace the random forest with CatBoostRegressor using loss_function='MAE', depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, iterations=800, and random_seed=seed, with verbose=0 and thread_count=8. Train it on the Morgan fingerprint bits. Ordered boosting on sparse binary features often generalizes well to unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Huber-loss gradient boosting
items.spec: Use sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor with loss='huber' and alpha=0.9, n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=4, subsample=0.8, and random_state=seed, trained on the Morgan bit features. Huber loss is less sensitive to the outlier permeability values in the training set than squared error, while staying close to MAE.

items.title: Extra-Trees instead of random forest
items.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for ExtraTreesRegressor with the same n_estimators, max_features, min_samples_leaf, and random_state. Extra-Trees chooses split thresholds at random, which adds more smoothing on high-dimensional sparse fingerprints and may generalize better to unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Random forest hyperparameter sweep
items.spec: Keep the random forest but change its regularization settings: min_samples_leaf=3, max_features='sqrt', and n_estimators=500. Larger leaves and fewer features per split smooth the model, which should help on scaffold-held-out folds where the training neighbors are less similar. No other changes.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity matrix between binary Morgan fingerprints, using K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)) on the 2048-bit vectors, and use it as a precomputed kernel for sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.05. Predict test molecules with the test-versus-train Tanimoto matrix. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecular property prediction.

items.title: Tanimoto Gaussian process / kernel ridge
items.spec: Use the Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bit vectors, as defined by sum(min)/sum(max), with sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.5) trained on the centered target: subtract the training mean from train_y before fitting and add it back to the predictions. The kernel is a smooth similarity measure that works well on small molecular datasets.

items.title: Similarity-weighted kNN regressor
items.spec: Predict each test molecule as a weighted average of the training labels of its k=7 nearest neighbors, using Tanimoto similarity on the Morgan bit vectors as the weight, with weights = similarity raised to the power 3. Use the Tanimoto matrix from the training set. This nonparametric baseline gives a different error pattern from the trees, so it is useful in an ensemble.

items.title: Average random forest and gradient boosting
items.spec: Train two models on the same Morgan features: the existing random forest and a LightGBM model with objective='l1' and learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=600, num_leaves=31. Return the simple average of their two predictions for the test molecules. Averaging models of different types usually reduces the error more than either model alone.

items.title: Stacked ensemble with ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Build out-of-fold predictions on the training set with an inner 4-fold KFold (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) for three base models: the random forest, LightGBM with objective='l1', and the Tanimoto kernel ridge model. Fit a non-negative linear regression (sklearn LinearRegression with positive=True) on the three out-of-fold prediction columns. Then refit each base model on all training data, and apply the learned weights to the test predictions.

items.title: Residual boosting on random forest
items.spec: Fit the random forest on the training data, compute out-of-fold residuals on the training set with a 5-fold inner KFold, then fit a LightGBM model (objective='l1', n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15) on the Morgan features plus the physicochemical descriptors to predict those residuals. The final prediction is the random forest prediction plus the residual model prediction on the test molecules.

items.title: Multi-radius Morgan count fingerprints
items.spec: Concatenate Morgan count fingerprints at radii 1, 2, and 3, each with 1024 bits, using GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, so the feature vector has 3072 columns. Keep the random forest. Multiple radii capture both local functional groups and larger substructures, which helps the model when the scaffolds differ between folds.

items.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP) fingerprints
items.spec: Use the feature-invariant Morgan variant: GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator set to rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius=2, fpSize=2048, and count fingerprints. FCFP groups atoms by pharmacophoric role (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than exact element, so it may generalize better across unseen scaffolds. Keep the random forest.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion fingerprints
items.spec: Compute atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize=2048) and topological torsion count fingerprints (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, fpSize=1024) for every molecule. Concatenate them with the Morgan bits and fit the random forest on the combined vector. Atom pairs and torsions encode topology beyond the local circular environments of Morgan.

items.title: MACCS keys added
items.spec: Add the 167-bit MACCS structural keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the Morgan bit features, concatenated into one feature vector. Keep the random forest. MACCS keys are a compact set of hand-chosen substructure flags that complement the hashed Morgan bits.

items.title: Reduced-graph (ErG) pharmacophore fingerprints
items.spec: Add the Extended Reduced Graph fingerprint from rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint for each molecule, a 315-dimensional pharmacophore-type descriptor. Concatenate it with the Morgan bit features and fit the random forest. ErG encodes shape and pharmacophore pattern in a way that is less tied to exact substructures, which may transfer better across scaffolds.

items.title: Crippen atom-contribution counts
items.spec: For each molecule, compute the Crippen atom-type contributions with rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs, sum the logP and molar-refractivity contributions per atom type to get counts of each Crippen type, and concatenate these per-type sums (about 110 values) with the Morgan features before fitting the random forest. This adds a physics-motivated lipophilicity signal that the bit fingerprint does not express directly.

items.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing
items.spec: Clean each SMILES before featurization: parse it, keep only the largest covalent fragment (rdkit.Chem.SaltRemover or by splitting on '.' and keeping the fragment with the most heavy atoms), neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and then compute the Morgan fingerprint. If parsing fails, fall back to the raw SMILES. Standardizing salts and charges removes noise that otherwise splits identical compounds into different fingerprints.

items.title: Winsorize training targets
items.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles, computed on the training labels only. Then fit the random forest on the clipped labels. Predictions for test molecules come from the model trained on the clipped targets. Clipping limits the pull of extreme measured values on the fitted trees, which can reduce MAE on the held-out folds.

items.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weights
items.spec: Compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold of each training molecule with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles. Give each training molecule a sample weight equal to 1 divided by the count of its scaffold within the training set, normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights to the random forest's fit call. This stops heavily represented scaffold families from dominating the trees, which matches the scaffold-held-out evaluation.

items.title: Bootstrap-median aggregation of trees
items.spec: Instead of averaging the random forest's tree predictions, take the median of the per-tree predictions for each test molecule, using np.median over model.estimators_. Because the metric is mean absolute error, a median estimate of the predictive distribution is the better point estimate. Keep the forest hyperparameters unchanged.

items.title: Shrink predictions toward the median
items.spec: After computing the random forest predictions on the test molecules, blend them toward the training median: final = 0.85 * prediction + 0.15 * median(train_y). Pick the shrinkage weight 0.85 using the 5-fold result on training folds only, not on test molecules. Shrinkage reduces variance on molecules that lie far from the training distribution.

items.title: Clip predictions to label range
items.spec: After prediction, clip the returned values to the interval [min(train_y), max(train_y)] computed from the training labels. This prevents extreme predictions for test molecules whose fingerprints are far from the training set, and it costs almost nothing in code. Keep the model unchanged.

items.title: Inner-CV random search over configs
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a small random search over 6 configurations drawn from: random forest min_samples_leaf in {1,2,4}, max_features in {0.1,0.3,'sqrt'}, and feature set in {Morgan bits, Morgan counts}. Score each configuration with an inner 3-fold KFold on train_smiles (shuffle=True, random_state=seed) using MAE. Refit the best configuration on all training data and predict the test molecules. Keep the total runtime below the 10-minute budget by using n_estimators=200 during the search.

items.title: Scaled MLP ensemble on descriptors
items.spec: Build the feature matrix from Morgan count fingerprints concatenated with the physicochemical descriptors, apply sklearn QuantileTransformer fit on the training set, and train an sklearn MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes=(256,128), alpha=1e-2 (L2 weight decay), early_stopping=True, learning_rate_init=1e-3, and max_iter=500. Average 5 networks with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4, and return their mean predictions.

items.title: Target standardization for trees
items.spec: Standardize train_y by subtracting its training mean and dividing by its training standard deviation before fitting. Fit the random forest on the standardized targets, then map the predictions back to the original scale by multiplying by the standard deviation and adding the mean. Random forest splits depend on the target scale only through the variance criterion, so standardization changes split choices slightly and can improve calibration when the label distribution is skewed.

items.title: Two-stage LightGBM with decaying learning rate
items.spec: Train LightGBM with objective='l1' on the Morgan features using a two-stage schedule: first fit 400 trees at learning_rate=0.05, then continue training for 400 more trees at learning_rate=0.01 by passing init_model to lgb.train. Use num_leaves=31, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8, and bagging_freq=1, with random seed set to seed. The lower late learning rate reduces overfitting to noisy training labels.

items.title: Morgan count fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, replace gen.GetFingerprintAsNumPy(...) with gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(...) and keep radius 2 and 2048 size. The random forest and all other settings stay the same. Counts carry more information than presence bits for repeated substructures.

items.title: Add RDKit 2D descriptor block
items.spec: Compute all values from rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList for each molecule (for example as a list of functions applied to the mol). Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip to +-1e6. Concatenate these float features with the Morgan count vector before fitting the random forest. Use the same fit_predict signature.

items.title: Compact physicochemical feature block
items.spec: Append about 10 interpretable features to the Morgan vector: Crippen MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, aromatic ring count, FractionCSP3, and SMARTS counts for carboxylic acids and basic amines. Permeability depends strongly on these properties, so a tree model can use them directly.

items.title: Multi-fingerprint concatenation
items.spec: Build three feature sets per molecule: Morgan radius-2 counts (2048), MACCS keys via rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys (167 bits), and atom-pair count fingerprints folded to 1024 bits. Concatenate them into one matrix and fit the same random forest.

items.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP-style) fingerprints
items.spec: Create the generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Use count fingerprints from it. Feature invariants (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) generalize better across unseen scaffolds than plain atom identities.

items.title: Larger radius and fingerprint size
items.spec: Change RADIUS to 3 and N_BITS to 4096 in the featurizer, and keep the rest of the pipeline the same. Larger radius encodes more of the local environment. The bigger vector is sparser, so the random forest's max_features setting should still be used.

items.title: Molecule standardization before featurizing
items.spec: In featurize, convert each SMILES to a mol, keep only the largest covalent fragment with rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, and neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Fall back to the unstandardized mol if sanitization fails. This removes counterions and salt forms that add noise to the fingerprints.

items.title: Winsorize training targets
items.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 1st and 99th percentiles, computed on train_y only. Fit the model on the clipped targets, and predict test molecules without any change. Outlier labels then have less influence on the fitted trees, which helps when the scoring metric is MAE.

items.title: LightGBM with L1 objective
items.spec: Replace the random forest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor(objective='l1', n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Use Morgan counts plus the physicochemical block as input. The L1 objective optimizes the median, which matches the MAE scoring.

items.title: LightGBM with Huber objective
items.spec: Use lightgbm.LGBMRegressor with objective='huber', alpha=1.0, n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=15, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed. Input is Morgan counts plus physicochemical features. Huber loss gives a robust fit to the squared-error region near the center and to the L1 tail.

items.title: CatBoost regressor
items.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, loss_function='MAE', random_seed=seed, verbose=False, thread_count=8) on Morgan count features plus physicochemical features. CatBoost's ordered boosting handles small datasets well, and the MAE loss matches the scoring.

items.title: XGBoost regressor
items.spec: Use xgboost.XGBRegressor(n_estimators=600, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3, reg_lambda=1.0, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on Morgan count features plus physicochemical features. Shallow trees with column subsampling reduce overfitting to scaffold-specific bits.

items.title: SVR with Tanimoto (MinMax) kernel
items.spec: Compute a precomputed kernel K(a,b)=sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)) on Morgan count vectors, using numpy broadcasting in chunks to stay within the memory limit. Fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on the train-train kernel and predict using the test-train kernel. Chemical similarity kernels usually work well for small molecular datasets.

items.title: Kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Build the MinMax (Tanimoto) kernel on Morgan count vectors, as in the SVR idea. Center train_y by subtracting its mean. Fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=a) for a chosen from {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by an inner 3-fold CV on the training set only, then add back the mean to the test predictions.

items.title: Weighted kNN with Tanimoto similarity
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules on Morgan bit vectors. Keep the k=7 most similar training molecules. Predict the similarity-weighted mean of their labels, with weights = similarity^2. This is a simple nonparametric baseline that often complements tree models.

items.title: Sklearn MLP on standardized features
items.spec: Standardize the physicochemical features with StandardScaler (fit on train only), then concatenate with Morgan bits. Standardize the target. Fit sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), alpha=1e-3, learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=500, random_state=seed). Inverse-transform the predictions.

items.title: ExtraTrees regressor
items.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) on the same Morgan features. Extra trees use random split thresholds, which smooth the predictions and can generalize better on unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Equal-weight blend of RF, LightGBM and SVR
items.spec: Fit the current random forest, a LightGBM L1 model on the same features, and the Tanimoto-kernel SVR. Return the simple mean of the three test predictions. Averaging models with different inductive biases usually reduces variance.

items.title: Stacked ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 5-fold inner CV on the training set to produce out-of-fold predictions from the random forest, LightGBM, and kNN models. Fit sklearn.linear_model.Ridge(alpha=1.0) on those OOF predictions. Refit the base models on all training data, and apply the ridge to their test predictions.

items.title: Residual two-stage model
items.spec: First fit a RidgeCV on standardized physicochemical features to predict train_y. Compute the residuals on the training set. Fit the random forest on Morgan features to predict those residuals. For test molecules, the prediction is the ridge output plus the forest output. A linear trend captured this way lets the forest focus on the structure-specific part.

items.title: Random forest leaf and feature settings
items.spec: Set min_samples_leaf=3, max_features='sqrt', and n_estimators=500 in the RandomForestRegressor. Keep Morgan bit features. Larger leaves smooth predictions and reduce variance for noisy labels.

items.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits
items.spec: Before fitting, compute the number of training molecules that have each bit set. Keep only bits set in at least 3 training molecules, using the same column mask on the test features. This removes sparse noise and speeds up the random forest. The mask must be computed inside fit_predict using train data only.

items.title: Clip predictions to training label range
items.spec: After prediction, clip the returned values to [min(train_y), max(train_y)]. Tree and kernel models can extrapolate poorly for test molecules with unusual properties, and clipping stops extreme outputs.

items.title: Murcko scaffold and ring count features
items.spec: Compute the generic Murcko scaffold with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold and hash it into a 256-bit vector of scaffold-atom-type features. Also add counts of ring systems and heavy atoms. Append these to the Morgan features. Scaffold-level signals can help with unseen skeletons when they correlate with permeability.

items.title: Density-based sample weighting
items.spec: For each training molecule, compute its mean Tanimoto similarity to its 10 nearest training neighbors. Use the inverse of that value, normalized to mean 1, as sample_weight in the random forest's fit call. This down-weights molecules in dense clusters so that the model covers the chemical space more evenly.

items.title: LightGBM with learning-rate schedule and early stopping
items.spec: Hold out a random 10% of the training set (using seed) for validation. Train LightGBM with objective='l1', learning_rate=0.05, and lgb.callbacks.reset_parameter to decay the learning rate by a factor of 0.995 each round, with early_stopping(50) on the validation set. Record the best iteration, then refit on all training data for that many rounds, scaled by 1.1.

items.title: MLP with L-BFGS solver and L2 penalty
items.spec: Use sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with solver='lbfgs', hidden_layer_sizes=(128,), alpha=1e-2, max_iter=1000, random_state=seed. Input is standardized physicochemical features concatenated with Morgan bits, and the target is standardized. L-BFGS is a full-batch quasi-Newton optimizer that converges well for datasets of this size.

items.title: Bagged LightGBM over row batches
items.spec: Train 5 LightGBM L1 regressors on random 60% row subsets of the training data, each with a different seed derived from the main seed. Average their test predictions. Each model sees a different batch of molecules, which reduces variance and is a form of bagging over batches.

items.title: Fingerprint bit-masking augmentation for RF
items.spec: Make two copies of the training set. In the second copy, randomly set 10% of the fingerprint bits to 0 using a seeded RNG. Stack both copies and fit the random forest on the augmented data with the same labels. The bit dropout makes the trees less dependent on any single substructure.

items.title: Median aggregation over random forest trees
items.spec: Instead of the mean, return the per-molecule median of the individual tree predictions: call model.estimators_, stack each tree's predict output on the test features, and take np.median along the tree axis. The median is more robust to outlier trees and aligns with the MAE objective.

items.title: RDKit descriptors + RF
items.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors (about 210 values, e.g. MolLogP, TPSA, MolMR) as extra features concatenated to the Morgan bits. Replace NaN/inf with 0 and clip extreme values. Keep the RF.

items.title: Crippen logP and descriptors only with GBM
items.spec: Drop fingerprints. Use RDKit 2D descriptors only and fit LightGBM (n_estimators 600, lr 0.03, num_leaves 31, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.5). Clean NaN/inf.

items.title: Morgan counts instead of bits
items.spec: Use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with radius 2, 2048 bits, then apply log1p. Keep the RF.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors + count fingerprints
items.spec: Concatenate RDKit descriptors with Morgan count fingerprints (1024 bits, radius 2). Fit LightGBM with 800 trees, lr 0.03, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_samples 10, L2 reg 1.

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors+counts
items.spec: Replace the RF with CatBoostRegressor (iterations 1500, depth 6, lr 0.05, loss MAE or RMSE, thread_count 8, random_seed seed) on descriptors plus Morgan counts. Check the time budget.

items.title: MAE/Huber objective
items.spec: Because the loss is MAE, switch the GBM objective to Huber (alpha about 0.9) or L1. If the RF is kept, use criterion absolute_error only if the time allows.

items.title: Ensemble RF + LightGBM + CatBoost
items.spec: Average the predictions of an RF, a LightGBM and a CatBoost, all on descriptors plus count fingerprints. Use equal weights.

items.title: MACCS keys added
items.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the features of the current model.

items.title: Atom-pair and topological torsion counts
items.spec: Add hashed atom-pair counts (1024 bits) and topological-torsion counts (1024 bits) from rdFingerprintGenerator, combined with the Morgan counts.

items.title: Larger Morgan radius 3 with feature invariants
items.spec: Add FCFP-style counts: GetMorganGenerator with radius 3 and atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), 1024 bits, concatenated to the ECFP features.

items.title: ExtraTrees swap
items.spec: Replace the RF with ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1) on the current features.

items.title: RF hyperparameter tuning
items.spec: Set MAX_FEATURES to 0.5, N_TREES to 500 and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 2, and check the effect on the MAE.

items.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (min/max) kernel on Morgan count vectors and fit sklearn SVR (kernel precomputed, C 5, epsilon 0.1). Predict with the test-train kernel.

items.title: Kernel ridge / GP with Tanimoto
items.spec: Use KernelRidge with a precomputed Tanimoto kernel on count fingerprints (alpha 0.5). Fit on y minus its mean.

items.title: Ensemble SVR-Tanimoto + GBM
items.spec: Average the Tanimoto SVR with LightGBM on descriptors. Different model families give diverse errors.

items.title: MLP on descriptors
items.spec: Standardize the RDKit descriptors with QuantileTransformer, then fit sklearn MLPRegressor (256,128, early stopping, alpha 1e-3). Average 5 seeds. Add the result to the ensemble.

items.title: XGBoost with hist
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor (hist, 800 trees, depth 6, lr 0.03, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.4, reg:pseudohubererror or squarederror) on descriptors plus counts.

items.title: Feature selection by variance
items.spec: Drop fingerprint columns that are on in fewer than 5 training molecules, and drop constant descriptors. This cuts noise and speeds up the fit.

items.title: Stacking with ridge
items.spec: Build out-of-fold predictions inside fit_predict with 5-fold KFold for RF, LGBM and SVR. Fit a non-negative linear meta-model on them.

items.title: Seed bagging
items.spec: Train 5 GBM models with different seeds and subsample 0.7, then average them. This lowers variance.

items.title: Winsorize target
items.spec: Clip the training targets to the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles before fitting, which gives robustness to outliers under an MAE metric.

items.title: Ionization-group features
items.spec: Add SMARTS-based counts for carboxylic acid, aliphatic amine, amidine, tetrazole, sulfonamide, phenol, quaternary N and similar groups, since logD depends on ionization. Append these to the features.

items.title: Fragment counts fr_ and EState
items.spec: Make sure the fr_* fragment counts and the EState VSA/ MQN descriptors are included: add rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_ and the Crippen contribution histograms (per-atom Crippen logP binned sums).

items.title: Canonicalize and strip salts
items.spec: Before featurizing, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges with Uncharger. Then compute the features.

items.title: Residual learning on Crippen logP
items.spec: Fit the model to the residual y minus a linear fit on MolLogP and TPSA. Add the linear prediction back at predict time.

items.title: Scaffold-aware inner early stopping
items.spec: Within fit_predict, hold out 10% of the train set by GroupKFold on Murcko scaffolds, to pick the number of LightGBM rounds with early stopping. Refit with that count.

items.title: LightGBM DART or extra_trees
items.spec: Use LightGBM with extra_trees=True, 1500 trees, lr 0.02, num_leaves 24, colsample 0.3, lambda_l2 5 on descriptors + counts for stronger regularization.

items.title: Graph-distance and shape descriptors
items.spec: Add the Chi, Kappa, BCUT2D, and Balaban/BertzCT descriptors, plus the PEOE_VSA, SMR_VSA and SlogP_VSA bins, via rdMolDescriptors. If the descriptors idea has already run, only add the 3D-free shape set.

items.title: Feature-bagged multi-fingerprint ensemble
items.spec: Train a separate RF on each of Morgan counts, atom pairs and MACCS+descriptors, then average the three. Weights are equal.

items.title: Rank-average blend with weights tuned
items.spec: Blend the SVR-Tanimoto, LGBM and CatBoost predictions with weights 0.3/0.3/0.4 (fixed, not fitted). Keep the code short and run it once to check the blend.

items.title: RDKit descriptors + RF
items.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors (about 200 values, nan_to_num, clip to +-1e6) concatenated to the Morgan bits as features for the random forest.

items.title: Count Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace binary Morgan bits with count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), radius 2, 2048 bits, keep RF.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors+counts
items.spec: Replace RF with LightGBM (n_estimators 800, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, colsample 0.3, subsample 0.8, objective l1 or huber) on RDKit descriptors plus count Morgan features.

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, 1500 iterations, lr 0.05, MAE or RMSE loss, thread_count 8) on RDKit descriptors plus count Morgan fingerprints.

items.title: XGBoost with MAE objective
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor with reg:absoluteerror or pseudohuber, 600 trees, depth 6, lr 0.03, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.8 on descriptors+count FP.

items.title: Crippen/logP-focused features
items.spec: Add Crippen MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, LabuteASA, HBD/HBA, rotatable bonds, and fraction sp3 as explicit features, and add Crippen atom-contribution bag (per-atom Crippen logP type counts via rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs bucketed) to the RF features.

items.title: Larger radius and bigger fingerprint
items.spec: Use Morgan radius 3, 4096 bits with counts; compare against radius 2.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion counts
items.spec: Add atom-pair count fingerprint (2048 bits) and topological torsion count fingerprint (1024) to the features.

items.title: MACCS keys addition
items.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the Morgan features.

items.title: Extra Trees ensemble
items.spec: Swap RF for ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1) on the same features.

items.title: RF tuning
items.spec: Tune RF: N_TREES 600, MAX_FEATURES 0.2, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF 2, max_samples 0.8 bootstrap fraction.

items.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Use sklearn SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) with Tanimoto (minmax) kernel computed from count Morgan fingerprints via numpy; predict with kernel between test and train.

items.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto
items.spec: Use KernelRidge with a precomputed Tanimoto kernel on binary Morgan radius 3 bits, alpha 0.3, with target centered by the train mean.

items.title: Gaussian process Tanimoto
items.spec: Implement GP regression manually: K=Tanimoto kernel plus noise 0.2 on diagonal, solve with scipy cholesky, predict mean; center targets.

items.title: MLP on descriptors
items.spec: Standardize (QuantileTransformer) descriptors and train sklearn MLPRegressor (512,256), alpha 1e-2, early stopping, averaged over 5 seeds.

items.title: Blend RF + LightGBM + SVR
items.spec: Average predictions of RF, LightGBM and Tanimoto SVR on shared features with equal weights.

items.title: Stacking with ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Build inner 5-fold out-of-fold predictions from RF, LGBM, CatBoost, and fit a non-negative linear regression on them; final predictions use the learned weights.

items.title: Huber/MAE loss in GBM
items.spec: Since metric is MAE, use LightGBM objective 'huber' (alpha 1.0) or 'l1' on current features and compare to l2.

items.title: Seed bagging
items.spec: Train 5 models with different seeds derived from seed (different subsample/colsample) and average predictions.

items.title: Feature selection by variance
items.spec: Drop fingerprint bits that are on in fewer than 5 training molecules (and near-constant descriptors) before fitting.

items.title: Functional group SMARTS counts
items.spec: Add fr_* fragment counts and counts of ionizable groups (carboxylic acid, amine, quaternary N, sulfonamide, phenol) via SMARTS as features, important for logD ionization.

items.title: Charged-state features
items.spec: Add features: number of acidic and basic groups by SMARTS, formal charge sum, and Gasteiger partial charge statistics (min, max, sum of abs).

items.title: Residual model on Crippen logP
items.spec: Compute Crippen MolLogP, fit target minus linear regression on logP as the residual with the GBM, add back at predict.

items.title: Scaffold-aware early stopping
items.spec: Inside fit_predict hold out 10% of train by Murcko scaffold groups to pick the number of LightGBM boosting rounds via early stopping, then refit on all with that count.

items.title: Target clipping/winsorizing
items.spec: Clip training targets to the 1st and 99th percentiles to reduce outlier influence before fitting.

items.title: Canonical tautomer/salt stripping
items.spec: Preprocess SMILES: keep largest fragment (rdMolStandardize LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges via Uncharger before featurizing.

items.title: Morgan feature-invariant variant
items.spec: Add FCFP (feature-invariants Morgan, radius 3, count, 1024 bits) alongside ECFP counts.

items.title: Avalon and ErG fingerprints
items.spec: Append Avalon count fingerprint (GetAvalonCountFP, 1024) and rdReducedGraphs ErG fingerprint to the features.

items.title: Sample weighting by scaffold size
items.spec: Weight training samples by 1/sqrt(size of their Murcko scaffold group) in the GBM fit to reduce dominance of large series.

items.title: Deeper CatBoost with strong regularization
items.spec: CatBoost depth 8, l2_leaf_reg 5, 2000 iterations, lr 0.03, rsm 0.2, loss RMSE on descriptors+counts, with random_strength 1.

items.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF
items.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors (Descriptors.descList) computed per molecule, replace inf/nan with 0 and clip extremes, and concatenate with the Morgan bits. Keep the RF. Descriptors like MolLogP carry strong logD signal.

items.title: Descriptors-only LightGBM
items.spec: Replace RF with LGBMRegressor (n_estimators 800, lr 0.03, num_leaves 31, colsample 0.5, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, n_jobs 8, random_state seed) on RDKit descriptors plus Crippen contributions only (no fingerprints).

items.title: Morgan counts instead of bits
items.spec: Use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with Morgan radius 2, 2048 bins, and apply log1p. Keep the RF. Counts retain multiplicity information.

items.title: Count fingerprint + descriptors into CatBoost
items.spec: Features: RDKit descriptors plus Morgan count fp (1024 bits, radius 2). Model: CatBoostRegressor(iterations 1500, depth 6, lr 0.05, loss MAE or RMSE, thread_count 8, random_seed seed, verbose 0).

items.title: Huber/MAE objective for GBM
items.spec: Since the metric is MAE, train LightGBM or XGBoost on descriptors+fp with objective huber (alpha ~1.0) or l1 and compare to the L2 objective.

items.title: Ensemble RF + LightGBM
items.spec: Fit both an RF on fingerprints+descriptors and a LightGBM on the same features; return the average of the predictions. Different model families usually decorrelate errors.

items.title: Add MACCS keys
items.spec: Concatenate MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the existing features. Useful for functional groups relevant to polarity and ionization.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints
items.spec: Add hashed atom pair count fingerprint (1024 bins) and topological torsion count (1024 bins) from rdFingerprintGenerator and concatenate them with the Morgan counts and descriptors for a GBM.

items.title: Feature-based Morgan (FCFP) addition
items.spec: Add Morgan fingerprints with the feature-invariant atom generator (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen), radius 3, 1024 bits, counts, in addition to the ECFP. Abstract pharmacophore-type features generalize better across unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Larger radius, more bits
items.spec: Use Morgan radius 3, 4096 bits counts with the RF, max_features 0.2. Test whether larger environments help.

items.title: Extra-trees ensemble
items.spec: Replace RF with ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1) on the fingerprints+descriptors. Smoother predictions can lower MAE.

items.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Compute Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count/bit fingerprints (via matrix ops, minmax for counts) and fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1). Average with the RF prediction.

items.title: Gaussian process / kernel ridge Tanimoto
items.spec: Use KernelRidge with a precomputed Tanimoto kernel on count fingerprints (alpha ~0.3) on centered targets. Kernel methods are strong on small molecular datasets.

items.title: MLP on descriptors, standardized
items.spec: Standardize descriptors with QuantileTransformer, then train a sklearn MLPRegressor (256,128, alpha 1e-3, early_stopping) averaged over 5 seeds; blend with a tree model.

items.title: Multi-seed bagging of GBM
items.spec: Train 5 LightGBM models with different seeds (seed+i) and subsampling, and average them to reduce variance.

items.title: RF min_samples_leaf and max_features tuning
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=2 and MAX_FEATURES=0.2 for the fingerprint RF, with 500 trees. Quick tuning check of the baseline.

items.title: Remove low-variance features
items.spec: Drop fingerprint bits that are on in fewer than 5 training molecules (computed on train only) before fitting. Reduces noise and speeds up the job.

items.title: Crippen/partial-charge and ionization features
items.spec: Add handcrafted features: counts of acidic groups (carboxylic acid, tetrazole, sulfonamide NH), basic amines (aliphatic amines, amidines, guanidines) via SMARTS, plus formal charge counts. logD depends strongly on ionization.

items.title: Gasteiger charge summaries
items.spec: Compute Gasteiger charges and add max, min, sum of positive, sum of negative charges, and the PEOE_VSA/SMR_VSA/SlogP_VSA descriptors if not present. Append to features.

items.title: XGBoost with deeper tuning
items.spec: XGBRegressor(n_estimators 1000, learning_rate 0.03, max_depth 6, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.4, min_child_weight 3, reg_lambda 2, tree_method hist, n_jobs 8) on descriptors plus count Morgan.

items.title: Stacking with ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Inside fit_predict get out-of-fold predictions (5-fold on train with GroupKFold-like split by scaffold) of RF, LightGBM, and SVR, then fit a non-negative linear regression for blending weights and apply it to test predictions.

items.title: Early stopping via inner validation
items.spec: Hold out 10% of the training set by scaffold, train LightGBM with lr 0.02 and up to 3000 rounds with early stopping on MAE, then predict with best iteration. Optionally refit on all data with that iteration count.

items.title: Lower learning rate, more rounds
items.spec: LightGBM with lr 0.01, 3000 trees, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, feature_fraction 0.3, lambda_l2 5. Slow shrinkage generally improves generalization.

items.title: Outlier target clipping
items.spec: Winsorize train_y at 0.5 and 99.5 percentiles before fitting, to reduce the influence of noisy extreme measurements, especially for L2 losses.

items.title: Sample weights by scaffold frequency
items.spec: Compute Murcko scaffold counts in the training set and weight each sample by 1/sqrt(count) in the model fit, so that big scaffold clusters don't dominate and the model generalizes to unseen skeletons.

items.title: Canonical tautomer / neutralization preprocess
items.spec: Standardize molecules before featurizing: largest fragment chooser and Uncharger (rdMolStandardize), so salts and charge forms don't produce artifacts. Compute logD-relevant features on the neutral form, optionally adding the charge state flag.

items.title: Simple graph-based message passing features (Weisfeiler-Lehman counts)
items.spec: Use Morgan unfolded counts: collect environments with radius up to 3 as a sparse dict from GetSparseCountFingerprint, keep those appearing in at least 3 training molecules, build a sparse matrix, and fit Ridge or LightGBM on it with descriptors.

items.title: Target as residual from Crippen logP
items.spec: Fit the model on y minus a linear fit to MolLogP (fit slope and intercept on train), then add back the linear prediction. The GBM/RF learns only the correction.

items.title: Blend RF, CatBoost, and SVR
items.spec: Average three diverse models: RF on Morgan bits, CatBoost on descriptors + counts, and Tanimoto SVR. Use weights 0.25/0.5/0.25 as a start. Keep the runtime under about 6 minutes.

items.title: Median-of-trees RF prediction
items.spec: With the RF, take the median of per-tree predictions instead of the mean, since the metric is MAE. Use np.median over [t.predict(X) for t in model.estimators_].

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace the bit-vector Morgan featurizer with a count fingerprint: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy, keeping radius 2 and 2048 size. Everything else (RandomForest settings, fit_predict signature) stays the same. Counts keep how many times each substructure occurs, which matters for logD because repeated polar groups push the value down.

items.title: Append RDKit 2D physchem descriptors
items.spec: In featurize, compute the full RDKit descriptor set with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors(mol) for each molecule (or Descriptors._descList), convert to a float array, replace NaN/inf with 0, and hstack it after the Morgan fingerprint columns. Descriptors such as MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD/HBA and aromatic ring counts carry most of the lipophilicity signal that a bit vector only captures indirectly. Fit the same RandomForest on the combined matrix.

items.title: Add Crippen logP as a feature
items.spec: Compute Crippen.MolLogP(mol) (from rdkit.Chem.Crippen) and MolMR for each molecule and append these two floats as extra columns to the fingerprint matrix. Crippen logP is a physically meaningful prior for octanol/water partitioning and is cheap to compute. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

items.title: Ionization-state SMARTS counts
items.spec: Add a small block of counts of ionizable groups that matter at pH 7.4 for logD: carboxylic acids, tetrazoles, acyl sulfonamides, phenols, aliphatic amines (primary, secondary, tertiary, not amides), amidines/guanidines, and quaternary nitrogens. Define each as an RDKit SMARTS pattern, count matches per molecule with mol.GetSubstructMatches, and hstack the counts to the features. Ionized acids and bases partition very differently from neutral species, so these counts should help the model.

items.title: MACCS keys added to fingerprint
items.spec: Compute rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol) (166 bits) per molecule, convert to a numpy array, and hstack it onto the Morgan features. MACCS keys encode broad pharmacophore-level features (rings, heteroatom types, functional groups) that complement the local circular environments of Morgan fingerprints.

items.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP-style) fingerprint
items.spec: Switch the Morgan generator to the functional-class variant: rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 2, 2048 bits. Atoms are then binned by pharmacophoric role (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than element identity, which generalises better across unseen scaffolds. Keep the RandomForest unchanged.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion fingerprints
items.spec: Build a second fingerprint per molecule using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048) and count it with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy, then hstack it to the Morgan counts. Atom pairs encode topological distance between atoms and capture overall molecular shape and size, which correlates with lipophilicity. Use the same RandomForest.

items.title: Larger Morgan radius and fold size
items.spec: Increase the Morgan radius from 2 to 3 and the bit count from 2048 to 4096 (or use unfolded counts via GetSparseCountFingerprint folded to 4096). Larger radius captures longer-range environments; more bits reduce collisions. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged. Check that memory stays well under 6 GB.

items.title: Canonicalise and deduplicate SMILES
items.spec: Before featurising, convert every training and test SMILES to canonical form with Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and drop any unparseable molecules by falling back to the original string. If the training set has duplicate canonical SMILES, average their target values and keep one row per unique molecule. This removes conflicting duplicate labels that bias tree fits and makes the training set cleaner.

items.title: LightGBM regressor on combined features
items.spec: Replace the RandomForest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor using objective='regression_l1' (MAE, matching the loss), n_estimators about 800, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed. Fit on the existing Morgan features. Gradient boosting usually beats a random forest on this kind of tabular fingerprint data.

items.title: CatBoost with MAE loss
items.spec: Replace the RandomForest with catboost.CatBoostRegressor(loss_function='MAE', iterations=1500, learning_rate 0.05, depth 6, rsm 0.3 (feature subsampling), random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8). CatBoost's symmetric trees are strong with noisy labels and its ordered boosting reduces overfitting on small datasets. Fit on the Morgan features and return predictions.

items.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective
items.spec: Use xgboost.XGBRegressor with objective='reg:absoluteerror', n_estimators 1000, learning_rate 0.03, max_depth 6, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3, tree_method='hist', n_jobs=8, random_state=seed. Train on the Morgan features. The absolute-error objective optimises the same metric the job scores.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity matrix between binary Morgan fingerprints of train and test molecules: K = (A·B) / (|A|+|B|-A·B) using numpy dot products. Fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on the train kernel, and predict using the test-by-train kernel. Standardise the target (subtract mean, divide by std) before fitting and invert after prediction. Chemically similar molecules have similar logD, and the Tanimoto kernel is the standard similarity measure for fingerprints.

items.title: Tanimoto kernel ridge / Gaussian process
items.spec: Use the same Tanimoto kernel matrix as the SVR idea (binary Morgan fingerprints, K = AB/(|A|+|B|-AB)). Fit kernel ridge regression by solving (K + lambda I) alpha = y_centered with lambda about 0.5 via numpy.linalg.solve, then predict test values as K_test @ alpha plus the target mean. Centre the target by its training mean first. This is a closed-form smooth similarity-based regressor that is quick on about 3000 molecules.

items.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto regressor
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between test and training fingerprints as in the SVR idea. For each test molecule take the k=7 most similar training molecules and predict a similarity-weighted median (or weighted mean with weights sim**3) of their labels. A kNN regressor is a simple, different-inductive-bias model that can be averaged with the tree models later.

items.title: MLP on fingerprints with standardised target
items.spec: Use sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), activation='relu', alpha=1e-3 (L2 penalty), learning_rate_init=1e-3, max_iter=300, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.1, random_state=seed. Standardise the input fingerprint matrix as float32 and standardise the target (mean and std), then invert the transform on predictions. A neural net over fingerprints can learn smooth multi-bit interactions that trees miss.

items.title: Blend of RandomForest, LightGBM and SVR
items.spec: Train three diverse models on the same features: the existing RandomForest, a LightGBM with regression_l1 objective, and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR (targets standardised). Return the simple average of their test predictions, or weight them 0.4/0.4/0.2. Averaging models with different inductive biases typically reduces error more than tuning any single model.

items.title: Stacking with a ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training data into 5 inner folds. For each inner fold, fit a RandomForest and a LightGBM model on the other folds and predict the held-out fold, building an out-of-fold prediction matrix. Fit a non-negative linear regression (sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression(positive=True)) of the training labels on these out-of-fold predictions. For the test set, refit both base models on all training data and combine their predictions with the learned weights.

items.title: Median of per-tree RandomForest predictions
items.spec: Keep the RandomForest but do not use the mean of its predictions. For test molecules, collect predictions from every fitted tree (np.stack([t.predict(X) for t in model.estimators_])) and return the median across trees.
