The median is more robust to outlier trees and aligns better with an MAE-based metric. No change to training.

items.title: Residual learning on Crippen logP
items.spec: Compute Crippen.MolLogP for each training molecule and fit a simple linear regression of the label on logP (y ≈ a*logP + b). Subtract this baseline from the training labels, fit the RandomForest (or LightGBM) on the residuals using the fingerprint features, then add the baseline back to the test predictions (baseline computed from the test molecules' logP). Modelling the residual lets the trees focus on structure-specific deviations from the physical prior.

items.title: Ensemble over multiple random seeds
items.spec: In fit_predict, train the RandomForest with several sub-seeds derived from the seed argument (for example seed, seed+1, seed+2, seed+3, seed+4), each with n_estimators=N_TREES//5, and average the test predictions across the sub-models. This reduces variance from random feature subsampling beyond what a single forest of the same total size achieves. Keep total tree count the same.

items.title: RandomForest hyperparameter sweep on leaf size and features
items.spec: Change the RandomForest settings: try min_samples_leaf=3 (or 5) instead of 1 to smooth predictions, and max_features='sqrt' (about 45 features) versus the current 0.3 (about 600). Keep n_estimators at 300 or raise to 500. Larger leaves regularise against noisy labels in a 3360-molecule dataset. Pick the setting that improves cross-validated MAE in the job.

items.title: Limit tree depth and use bootstrap subsampling
items.spec: Constrain the RandomForest with max_depth=20 and max_samples=0.7 (bootstrap fraction less than 1). Shallower trees and smaller bootstrap samples increase diversity between trees and reduce overfitting to individual scaffolds, which matter because the test folds contain unseen skeletons. Keep the other RandomForest settings.

items.title: Huber loss gradient boosting
items.spec: Use sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss='absolute_error' or, to smooth gradients, loss='quantile' with alpha 0.5 (median). Set max_iter 500, learning_rate 0.05, max_leaf_nodes 31, l2_regularization 1.0, min_samples_leaf 20, early_stopping=False, random_state=seed. Training on the Morgan features with an absolute-type loss targets the median, which is optimal for MAE, and the L2 penalty adds regularisation.

items.title: Inner early-stopping for LightGBM
items.spec: Hold out 10 percent of the training molecules (chosen with a seed-based random permutation) as an inner validation set. Train a LightGBM regression_l1 model with n_estimators up to 3000 and learning_rate 0.02, using callbacks lightgbm.early_stopping(100) on that validation set. Then refit on all training data using the best iteration count found (scaled by 1.1). This picks a tree count tailored to each fold rather than a fixed number.

items.title: Cosine learning-rate decay for MLP
items.spec: Implement the MLP training with a cosine learning-rate schedule: use a PyTorch-free approach by training sklearn MLPRegressor with solver='adam' and warm starts over several rounds, updating learning_rate_init manually each round as lr = 1e-3 * 0.5*(1+cos(pi*round/total_rounds)). Use 20 rounds of max_iter=10 each, warm_start=True. A decaying learning rate lets the network settle into a smoother minimum, improving generalisation on unseen skeletons.

items.title: Decaying shrinkage schedule for boosting
items.spec: Train LightGBM with regression_l1 but use a learning-rate schedule via the callback reset_parameter: start learning_rate at 0.05 and decay it geometrically to 0.01 over the 1000 boosting rounds (lr_t = 0.05 * (0.2)**(t/1000)). Early boosting steps move quickly and later steps fine-tune, which often gives a lower final error than a constant rate at the same tree count.

items.title: Minibatch-style bagging of gradient boosting
items.spec: Train 5 LightGBM regression_l1 models, each on a random 80 percent subsample of the training molecules (sampled with the seed-derived RNG), with different random_state values, then average their test predictions. This batch-level bagging decorrelates the models, reducing variance on the small dataset without changing the individual model's settings.

items.title: Mini-batch MLP ensemble
items.spec: Train an ensemble of 5 MLPRegressor models with hidden_layer_sizes=(256,), batch_size=64, solver='adam', alpha=1e-2, max_iter=200, early_stopping=True, each with a different random_state derived from seed. Standardise the target. Average the 5 predicted test vectors (after inverting the target standardisation). Small minibatches with multiple members yield a smoother, lower-variance estimate.

items.title: Sample weighting by label density
items.spec: Compute per-molecule weights as the inverse of the local density of the training label distribution (for example, bin the labels into 20 quantile bins and weight each molecule by 1/bin_count, normalised to mean 1). Pass these weights as sample_weight into the RandomForest or LightGBM fit. Rare logD extremes then get more influence, which helps tails that MAE penalises when predicted badly.

items.title: Remove low-variance fingerprint bits
items.spec: After building the Morgan bit matrix on the training fold, drop columns that are set in fewer than 5 training molecules or in more than 99 percent of them (sklearn.feature_selection.VarianceThreshold with a computed threshold, or boolean masking). Apply the same column mask to the test features. Removing near-constant and very rare bits reduces noise and speeds up the RandomForest split search with no loss of information.

items.title: Target-based feature selection by correlation
items.spec: On the training fold only, compute a Spearman correlation between each fingerprint column and the training labels. Keep the top 512 columns by absolute correlation and fit the RandomForest on those columns for both training and test. Selecting features that are informative about logD reduces the dimension the forest must search and removes columns that are only noise across scaffolds.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, replace the bit-vector output with hashed count vectors: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy, keeping radius 2 and 2048 bits. Everything else (RandomForest settings, fit_predict flow) stays the same. Counts often carry more information than presence bits for logD-type properties.

items.title: Larger Morgan radius
items.spec: Set RADIUS = 3 in the settings block and keep the rest unchanged. Larger radius captures bigger substructures, which can help a lipophilicity model, at the cost of more sparse bits.

items.title: Add Crippen logP and RDKit descriptors
items.spec: In featurize, append a block of RDKit 2D descriptors to each fingerprint row: use rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList, compute each value per molecule, replace NaN/inf with 0, and clip extreme values to the 1st and 99th percentiles seen in training. Concatenate with the Morgan bits. Descriptors such as MolLogP, TPSA and MolWt are strong logD signals that bit fingerprints miss.

items.title: Crippen logP as a single strong feature
items.spec: Compute rdkit.Chem.Crippen.MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors and NumRotatableBonds for every molecule and append these five numbers to the fingerprint matrix. Keep the RandomForest unchanged. This is a small, cheap addition that gives the trees direct access to lipophilicity-relevant physchem values.

items.title: Ionization-state SMARTS counts
items.spec: Add a few count features for groups that are charged or ionized at pH 7.4, which strongly shift logD relative to logP. Define SMARTS patterns for carboxylic acid, tetrazole, acyl sulfonamide, aliphatic amine (primary, secondary, tertiary, non-amide), amidine/guanidine and quaternary nitrogen. Count matches per molecule with Chem.MolFromSmarts and Mol.GetSubstructMatches, and append the counts to the feature matrix.

items.title: MACCS keys features
items.spec: Append 167-bit MACCS structural keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the Morgan bit vector for each molecule, producing a concatenated feature matrix. Keep the RandomForest unchanged. MACCS keys summarise pharmacophore-like functional groups and complement circular fingerprints.

items.title: Feature-class fingerprint variant (FCFP)
items.spec: Use the feature-invariant Morgan generator instead of the standard one: rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Keep counts or bits as-is. FCFP groups atoms by pharmacophore role, which generalises better across unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion fingerprints
items.spec: Compute rdFingerprintGenerator atom-pair count fingerprints (GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048) and topological-torsion count fingerprints (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, fpSize 1024) per molecule and concatenate them with the Morgan features. These encode longer-range topology that Morgan fingerprints truncate.

items.title: Scaffold-agnostic feature pruning
items.spec: Before fitting, drop fingerprint columns that are non-zero in fewer than 5 training molecules or in more than 98% of them. Apply the same column mask to the test features. This removes near-constant bits that add noise and slow the forest without losing information.

items.title: Switch to LightGBM with L1 objective
items.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor using objective='l1' (matching the MAE metric), n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8 with subsample_freq=1, and random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Train on the same featurized matrix.

items.title: CatBoost regressor on fingerprints and descriptors
items.spec: Replace the random forest with catboost.CatBoostRegressor(loss_function='MAE', iterations=1500, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) trained on the feature matrix. CatBoost's ordered boosting often generalises well on small tabular chemistry data.

items.title: XGBoost with pseudo-Huber loss
items.spec: Replace the random forest with xgboost.XGBRegressor(objective='reg:pseudohubererror', n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.04, max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Pseudo-Huber is robust to outlier logD values while staying close to squared loss near zero.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression
items.spec: Compute Tanimoto (Jaccard on binary Morgan bits) similarity matrices between train and train, and between test and train, using numpy dot products: S = (A·B)/(|A|+|B|-A·B). Fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.05) on the training Gram matrix and predict with the test-by-train similarity matrix. Tanimoto kernels are the standard chemistry similarity measure and often beat forests on small datasets.

items.title: Kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Build the Tanimoto similarity matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints as in a Tanimoto-kernel model. Fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.5) to the centered training targets (subtract the training mean, add it back to predictions). Kernel ridge is fast on 3k molecules and gives a smooth similarity-based regressor to ensemble with the forest.

items.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto regressor
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules. For each test molecule take the k=7 most similar training molecules and predict the similarity-weighted mean of their targets (weights = similarity to the power 3). Use this as a standalone predictor or as an ensemble member; it is cheap and interpretable.

items.title: Multilayer perceptron on fingerprints
items.spec: Use sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), alpha=1e-3, learning_rate_init=1e-3, max_iter=300, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, random_state=seed) on the standardised feature matrix (StandardScaler fitted on training data). Predict with the fitted network. A dense net on fingerprints gives a different inductive bias from trees.

items.title: Simple ensemble of forest and gradient boosting
items.spec: Fit the existing RandomForestRegressor and a LightGBM model with objective='l1' on the same features (fit each with the seed). Return the arithmetic mean of their test predictions. Averaging a bagged and a boosted model typically reduces variance more than either alone.

items.title: Stacking of heterogeneous base models
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, make 5 inner folds over the training set (KFold, shuffle, random_state=seed). For each base model (RandomForest, LightGBM L1, Tanimoto-kernel SVR) collect out-of-fold predictions on the training set and predictions on the test set averaged over folds. Fit a non-negative linear regressor (sklearn LinearRegression(positive=True)) on the out-of-fold predictions and apply its weights to the test predictions.

items.title: Predict residual from Crippen logP
items.spec: Compute Crippen logP (rdkit.Chem.Crippen.MolLogP) for train and test molecules. Fit the model on the target residual y - crippen_logp, then add crippen_logp back to the test predictions. Using a physics-style baseline lets the model learn only the correction, which often reduces error on small data.

items.title: Target clipping and winsorising
items.spec: Before fitting, clip the training targets to the 0.5th and 99.5th percentiles of train_y to limit the influence of extreme or noisy measurements. Fit the unchanged model on the clipped targets and predict the test molecules normally. Measured logD values have some outliers that distort tree leaves.

items.title: Clip predictions to training range
items.spec: After prediction, clip the returned test predictions to the interval [min(train_y) - 0.5, max(train_y) + 0.5]. This is a safety step that removes extreme extrapolations from tree or kernel models on unseen scaffolds. Keep the model unchanged.

items.title: Median-of-trees prediction for MAE
items.spec: Instead of the mean over the forest, take the median prediction across individual trees for each test molecule: loop over model.estimators_, stack their predictions, and return np.median along axis 0. Since the metric is MAE, the conditional median is the better point estimate. Keep the forest hyperparameters unchanged.

items.title: Tune forest leaf size and feature fraction
items.spec: Change the RandomForest settings to MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF = 3 and MAX_FEATURES = 0.2 (or sqrt of feature count). Larger leaves smooth predictions and reduce overfitting to scaffold-specific noise, which matters because test folds have unseen scaffolds. Leave all other code unchanged.

items.title: Bootstrap-free forest with max depth limit
items.spec: Set max_depth=14 on the RandomForestRegressor and keep bootstrap=True with max_samples=0.7. Limiting depth and subsampling rows each tree adds regularisation and decorrelates trees, improving generalisation to new scaffolds.

items.title: Shrink boosting learning rate with more trees and early stopping
items.spec: For the LightGBM L1 model, hold out 10% of the training molecules (random, seeded) as a validation set. Train with learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators up to 3000, and lightgbm early_stopping(100) on validation MAE. Refit on all training data with the best iteration count scaled by 1.1. A lower learning rate with tuned tree count is a standard schedule that usually improves boosting accuracy.

items.title: Staged learning-rate decay for MLP
items.spec: For the MLP model, replace the default constant learning rate with a cosine decay: train in epochs via partial_fit (set max_iter=1 per call) for 200 epochs, setting the optimizer learning rate to 1e-3 * 0.5*(1+cos(pi*epoch/200)) each epoch. Use Adam with alpha=1e-4 weight decay. A decaying schedule usually gives a smoother final fit than a constant rate.

items.title: Seed-averaged bagging of the final model
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, train the chosen model 5 times with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 on bootstrap resamples of the training set (sample rows with replacement, same size), and return the mean of their test predictions. Repeated resampling reduces variance from both the data and the random initialisation at 5x the training cost; keep the total job under 10 minutes.

items.title: Subsampled row and column batches for boosting
items.spec: For the LightGBM L1 model, set bagging_fraction=0.7 with bagging_freq=1 (row subsampling per iteration) and feature_fraction=0.4 (column subsampling per tree), plus min_data_in_leaf=20. Smaller random batches per boosting step decorrelate successive trees and regularise against overfitting to training scaffolds.

items.title: Sample weighting by scaffold frequency
items.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) of every training molecule and weight each sample by 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold). Pass these as sample_weight to the model's fit call. This stops heavily represented scaffold families from dominating the fit, which matches the scaffold-split test setting.

items.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors to fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, besides the Morgan bits, compute all RDKit 2D descriptors with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors for each molecule (use Descriptors._descList). Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip values to +/-1e6. Concatenate them to the fingerprint matrix and keep the same RandomForestRegressor. Descriptors such as MolLogP, TPSA and MolWt carry most of the signal for logD.

items.title: Crippen logP as a standalone feature
items.spec: Add a feature column equal to Chem.Crippen.MolLogP(mol), plus MolMR and TPSA, appended to the Morgan bit matrix. Keep the random forest unchanged. logD tracks lipophilicity, so an explicit logP column gives the trees a strong early split that bits alone cannot provide easily.

items.title: Predict residual from Crippen logP
items.spec: Compute x = Crippen MolLogP for train and test molecules. Fit the model on the target r = train_y - x, then return predictions as model.predict(test) + x_test. Use the same fingerprint features and random forest. The baseline lipophilicity is removed so the model learns only the correction.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same Morgan generator, so each feature holds how many times an environment occurs rather than a 0/1 flag. Keep 2048 bits and the random forest. Counts hold more information about repeated groups in larger molecules.

items.title: Larger Morgan radius with feature invariants
items.spec: Try RADIUS = 3 for Morgan count fingerprints and also add FCFP-style features by building a second generator with GetMorganGenerator(..., atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Concatenate the ECFP and FCFP count vectors with 2048 bits each. Keep the random forest.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion fingerprints
items.spec: Build additional count fingerprints with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024) and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=1024). Concatenate them with the Morgan counts and fit the same random forest. These capture different structural pairs and paths than circular environments.

items.title: MACCS keys appended
items.spec: Add the 167-bit MACCS structural keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to numpy) to the Morgan feature matrix. Keep the random forest. MACCS encodes curated functional groups that correlate with ionization and polarity.

items.title: Ionizable-group count features
items.spec: Count SMARTS matches for carboxylic acids, tetrazoles, aliphatic amines (primary, secondary, tertiary, not amides), amidines, and phenols, and append these counts to the features. logD at pH 7.4 depends strongly on ionization, which fingerprints capture poorly. Keep the random forest.

items.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing
items.spec: In featurize, keep the largest organic fragment (rdkit.Chem.SaltRemover or split on '.' and keep the heaviest fragment), neutralize charges with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and then compute fingerprints. Fall back to the unmodified molecule if sanitization fails. This removes counterion and charge noise.

items.title: LightGBM regressor on fingerprints and descriptors
items.spec: Replace the random forest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor(n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Use the same featurization as the baseline with count fingerprints. Gradient boosting often beats bagged trees on tabular chemistry features.

items.title: L1 or Huber objective in gradient boosting
items.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='huber' (alpha about 1.0) or objective='l1' so the loss matches the mean absolute error metric. Keep the other LightGBM settings from a standard setup with 600 trees and learning rate 0.03. Robust losses reduce the influence of outlier logD measurements on the fit.

items.title: XGBoost regressor with pseudo-Huber loss
items.spec: Fit xgboost.XGBRegressor(n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.03, max_depth=6, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_weight=3, objective='reg:pseudohubererror', random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on count fingerprints plus RDKit descriptors. Predict with the fitted model. Pseudo-Huber combines squared error near zero with linear error on outliers.

items.title: CatBoost on RDKit descriptors
items.spec: Compute RDKit 2D descriptors (cleaned of NaN and inf) and fit catboost.CatBoostRegressor(iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, loss_function='MAE', random_seed=seed, verbose=False, thread_count=8). CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are often strong on small tabular datasets, and its MAE loss matches the metric.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression
items.spec: Compute binary Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits). Build the Tanimoto similarity matrix K(A,B) = (A.B)/(|A|^2+|B|^2-A.B) with numpy, and fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on the train-train kernel. Predict with the test-train kernel. Similarity kernels are the standard strong baseline for molecular property prediction.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel kernel ridge regression
items.spec: Build the Tanimoto kernel matrix from binary Morgan fingerprints as in a precomputed kernel. Center the targets by subtracting the training mean, solve (K + lambda*I) alpha = y_centered with lambda = 0.5 using numpy.linalg.solve, and predict test as K_test @ alpha plus the mean. Kernel ridge is a smooth similarity-weighted regressor that complements tree models.

items.title: Ensemble of random forest and LightGBM
items.spec: Train both the random forest (300 trees, max_features 0.3) and a LightGBM regressor on the same features, and return the average of their test predictions with equal weights. Ensembling diverse model families usually lowers the error more than tuning one model.

items.title: Stacking with a ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold KFold (shuffle, random_state=seed) on the training set to produce out-of-fold predictions from the random forest, LightGBM, and kernel ridge. Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy.optimize.nnls or sklearn LinearRegression with positive=True) on these out-of-fold predictions. Apply the fitted base models on all training data and combine their test predictions with the learned weights.

items.title: Random forest with median-of-trees prediction
items.spec: Keep the random forest fit, but predict by taking the median across the per-tree predictions instead of the mean. Use model.estimators_ and np.median over the stacked tree outputs along axis 0. The median is the natural estimator for an absolute-error metric and reduces the influence of a few extreme leaves.

items.title: Extra-trees regressor
items.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) on the same count fingerprint features. Random split thresholds make the trees smoother and often reduce variance on small noisy data.

items.title: Stronger leaf regularization in random forest
items.spec: Set min_samples_leaf to 3 and max_features to 'sqrt' in the random forest, and keep 300 trees. Larger leaves average more molecules per prediction, which reduces noise in the noisy experimental logD labels.

items.title: Remove near-constant fingerprint bits
items.spec: After computing the fingerprint matrix on the training set, drop columns that are nonzero in fewer than 2 training molecules or in more than 99 percent of them. Apply the same column mask to the test features. Keep the random forest. Removing uninformative bits cuts noise and speeds up split search.

items.title: Hyperparameter selection by inner scaffold split
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training set by Murcko scaffold into an inner train and inner validation part (about 20 percent of scaffolds). Try a small grid of LightGBM settings (num_leaves in {15, 31}, learning_rate in {0.03, 0.05}) and keep the one with the lowest validation MAE. Refit on the full training set with the chosen settings. Selecting on scaffold-disjoint data matches the evaluation.

items.title: Early stopping with learning-rate decay in boosting
items.spec: Train LightGBM with up to 3000 trees at learning rate 0.05 and use an inner validation split (10 percent of training molecules, grouped by scaffold) with early_stopping(100). Use a learning-rate schedule via callbacks, reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda i: 0.05 * 0.999**i). Refit or keep the best iteration for the test predictions.

items.title: Row and feature subsampling for bagged boosting
items.spec: Train an ensemble of 5 LightGBM regressors with different seeds (seed + k), each using bagging_fraction=0.7 with bagging_freq=1 and feature_fraction=0.4, and average their test predictions. Stochastic row and column sampling reduces variance of the boosted trees.

items.title: Multilayer perceptron on standardized descriptors
items.spec: Standardize RDKit 2D descriptors (fit the scaler on the training set, clip to plus or minus 5 after scaling, replace NaN with 0). Fit sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 128), alpha=1e-3, learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=500, random_state=seed) on the scaled features and the target. Neural networks on scaled descriptors capture smooth additive trends in logP-like properties.

items.title: Minibatch MLP with cosine learning-rate schedule
items.spec: Train a small PyTorch-free MLP is not allowed, so use sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with solver='adam', batch_size=64, learning_rate_init=1e-3, and set the number of epochs to 300 with warm restarts by refitting twice with warm_start=True and a lower learning_rate_init each round (0.5x). Use standardized descriptors plus count fingerprints as input.

items.title: Stronger weight decay for the MLP
items.spec: On standardized descriptors plus fingerprints, fit sklearn MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(128,), alpha=0.01, solver='adam', max_iter=400, early_stopping=True, random_state=seed). Raising alpha, the L2 penalty, from its default 1e-4 limits overfitting on the small training set. Average predictions over 3 seeds.

items.title: Target transform through a clipped range
items.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to the 1st and 99th percentiles of the training targets to limit the effect of extreme outliers. Fit the baseline random forest on the clipped target. Predict on the test molecules as usual without changing the output scale.

items.title: Bagged random forest over feature subsets
items.spec: Build 4 random forests of 150 trees each. Each uses a different feature view: Morgan radius 2 bits, Morgan radius 3 counts, atom-pair counts, and MACCS keys. Average their test predictions. Views with different structural emphasis give diverse errors that the average cancels.

items.title: Mean-target and noise-aware sample weighting
items.spec: Compute training sample weights as the inverse of the local target noise estimate: for each training molecule, take the standard deviation of train_y among its 5 nearest neighbors by Tanimoto similarity, and set weight = 1 / (0.1 + std). Pass the weights to the random forest fit via sample_weight. This downweights molecules whose neighbors disagree.

items.title: Fingerprint size and chirality change
items.spec: Set N_BITS to 4096 and build the Morgan generator with includeChirality=True. Keep the random forest with count fingerprints. A larger hash space reduces bit collisions, and stereo information can separate isomers that have different measured logD values.

items.title: Add RDKit descriptors to RF
items.spec: Compute all RDKit Descriptors (Descriptors.descList) per molecule, replace NaN/inf with 0 and clip to +-1e6, and concatenate with the Morgan bits as RF input. Keep the rest unchanged.

items.title: Descriptors only RF
items.spec: Use only RDKit 2D descriptors (nan_to_num, clipped) as features for the RandomForest, dropping the fingerprint. Physchem such as TPSA, HBD and logP drive BBB.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors
items.spec: Replace the RF with LGBMClassifier (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed, verbose=-1) on RDKit descriptors plus count Morgan features.

items.title: Count Morgan fingerprint
items.spec: Use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy instead of the bit vector (radius 2, 2048) as RF features.

items.title: ExtraTrees swap
items.spec: Replace RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier (500 trees, max_features 0.3) on the existing features.

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use CatBoostClassifier (iterations=600, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on RDKit descriptors plus MACCS keys.

items.title: MACCS keys addition
items.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys) to the Morgan bits as features.

items.title: Smaller radius Morgan
items.spec: Set RADIUS=1 and N_BITS=1024 to reduce scaffold-specific bits, improving generalization to unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Feature-Morgan with chirality off, FCFP
items.spec: Use a Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen() (functional-class fingerprints), radius 2, counts, in place of ECFP.

items.title: Atom pair and torsion counts
items.spec: Add hashed count atom-pair fingerprints (fpSize 1024) from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator to the features.

items.title: Rank-average ensemble RF+LGBM
items.spec: Train an RF on Morgan+descriptors and a LightGBM on descriptors. Average their predicted probabilities after rank-normalizing (scipy.stats.rankdata) on the test set.

items.title: Balanced class weights
items.spec: Set class_weight='balanced_subsample' in the RF.

items.title: RF min_samples_leaf 2 and more trees
items.spec: Set N_TREES=800, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=2, MAX_FEATURES='sqrt'.

items.title: Logistic regression on scaled descriptors
items.spec: Standardize descriptors (QuantileTransformer or StandardScaler after clipping) and fit LogisticRegression C=0.1; use as a simple model, optionally blended 50/50 with the RF.

items.title: SVM with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Precompute Tanimoto kernel on binary Morgan bits and fit SVC(kernel='precomputed', probability=True, C=1, random_state=seed). Return predict_proba.

items.title: XGBoost on mixed features
items.spec: Use XGBClassifier (n_estimators=500, max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.4, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on descriptors plus Morgan counts.

items.title: Variance feature filter
items.spec: Drop features with fewer than 5 nonzero training molecules (or zero variance) before fitting; fit the mask on training data only.

items.title: Seed-bagged ensemble
items.spec: Train 5 LightGBM models with different seeds and subsample settings on descriptors and average predictions.

items.title: Salt stripping and canonicalization
items.spec: Before featurizing, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), neutralize charges (Uncharger), then compute features.

items.title: Custom BBB rule features
items.spec: Add hand-made features: TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, number of acidic groups (carboxylic acid SMARTS), basic amine count, rotatable bonds, formal charge, and the CNS MPO-like score. Append them to the Morgan features, upweighted by using them alongside descriptors in a GBM.

items.title: Gasteiger charge descriptors
items.spec: Add partial-charge statistics (max, min, and sum of abs Gasteiger charges, polar surface-related PEOE_VSA, SlogP_VSA, and EState VSA) as extra features through the descriptor list.

items.title: Stacked RF + GBM + LR
items.spec: Produce out-of-fold predictions (5-fold inside fit_predict, GroupKFold is not needed) from RF, LGBM and LR, then fit a logistic regression meta-learner and apply it to the test predictions.

items.title: Calibrated sigmoid probabilities
items.spec: Wrap the model in CalibratedClassifierCV (sigmoid, cv=3). AUROC may be slightly affected, so use it mainly with the GBM.

items.title: Scaffold-aware sample weights
items.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and weight samples by 1/sqrt(scaffold count) so large scaffold clusters do not dominate. Pass sample_weight to fit.

items.title: Shallow MLP on descriptors
items.spec: Quantile-transform descriptors and fit an sklearn MLPClassifier (hidden 256,64, alpha=1e-2, early_stopping, random_state=seed). Average 5 seeds and blend with the RF.

items.title: HistGradientBoosting
items.spec: Use HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05, max_iter=300, l2_regularization=1, random_state=seed) on descriptors+MACCS.

items.title: Remove highly correlated descriptors
items.spec: On the training set, drop descriptors with |corr|>0.95 with an earlier one and constant ones, then fit the RF on the remainder plus Morgan bits.

items.title: RF max_features tuning with descriptors
items.spec: On a descriptors+Morgan feature set, set MAX_FEATURES=0.15 and N_TREES=500 for diversity and speed.

items.title: Label smoothing for GBM
items.spec: Convert targets to soft labels 0.05/0.95 and fit LightGBM as a regressor (objective cross_entropy) on descriptors to reduce the effect of noisy labels.

items.title: Add RDKit physchem descriptors
items.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors (Descriptors.descList) computed per molecule, concatenated with the Morgan bits. Replace nan/inf with 0 and clip to ±1e6. Keep the random forest. BBB depends strongly on TPSA, MW, HBD and logP.

items.title: Descriptors only RF
items.spec: Drop the fingerprint and use only the RDKit descriptor matrix (nan-cleaned, clipped) with the RandomForest. Tests whether physchem alone generalizes better across scaffolds.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors
items.spec: Use RDKit descriptors as features with LGBMClassifier (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed, verbose=-1, n_jobs=8).

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors+counts
items.spec: Features are RDKit descriptors plus Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits). Model is CatBoostClassifier(iterations=600, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8).

items.title: Morgan count fingerprints
items.spec: Switch from binary bits to count vectors (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) with the RF, radius 2, 2048 bits.

items.title: Extra trees
items.spec: Replace RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3) on the current features.

items.title: MACCS keys addition
items.spec: Concatenate MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) with the Morgan bits and the RF.

items.title: Rank-average ensemble RF + GBM
items.spec: Fit an RF on Morgan+descriptors and a LightGBM on descriptors. Return the average of their rank-normalized predictions (scipy.stats.rankdata/n).

items.title: Smaller radius, folded counts
items.spec: Use Morgan radius 1 with 1024 count bits plus descriptors; more generalizable substructures for new scaffolds.

items.title: Feature-based Morgan with chirality off, atom-pair FP
items.spec: Add atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048) alongside Morgan bits for the RF.

items.title: Topological torsion + pair fusion
items.spec: Concatenate Morgan counts, atom-pair counts and topological-torsion counts (1024 bits each) and train the RF with max_features='sqrt'.

items.title: RF min_samples_leaf tuning
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=2 and N_TREES=600 to smooth probabilities.

items.title: RF balanced class weights
items.spec: Use class_weight='balanced_subsample' in the RF, since BBB data are imbalanced toward positives.

items.title: Logistic regression on scaled descriptors
items.spec: StandardScaler (after clipping and quantile-clipping to 1-99 percentile) plus LogisticRegression(C=0.1) on descriptors. Use it as a simple model with good extrapolation.

items.title: SVM RBF on descriptors
items.spec: Use a QuantileTransformer then SVC(kernel='rbf', C=1, probability=True, random_state=seed) on descriptors.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count/bit fingerprints between train and test, and fit SVC(kernel='precomputed', probability=True, C=1).

items.title: Small hand-picked BBB descriptors + GBM
items.spec: Use a compact set: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, formal charge, acid/base group counts (carboxylic acid via SMARTS, basic amine SMARTS), aromatic rings, fraction sp3. Train HistGradientBoostingClassifier with strong regularization.

items.title: Acid/base SMARTS features
items.spec: Add counts for carboxylic acid, sulfonamide, quaternary N, basic amines, and phenols as extra features to Morgan+descriptors for the RF.

items.title: XGBoost tuned shallow
items.spec: XGBClassifier(n_estimators=500, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.4, min_child_weight=3, reg_lambda=5, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on descriptors + Morgan counts.

items.title: Seed-bagged LightGBM
items.spec: Average 5 LightGBM models with different seeds derived from seed and bagging/feature fractions of 0.7 on descriptors plus MACCS.

items.title: Stacking RF/GBM/SVM
items.spec: Build a StackingClassifier with RF (Morgan), LightGBM (descriptors) and SVM (descriptors) base models and logistic regression as the final estimator, cv=5.

items.title: Feature selection by variance
items.spec: Remove Morgan bits that are on in fewer than 5 training molecules (or more than 95%) before the RF, and also remove near-constant descriptors.

items.title: Canonical salt stripping
items.spec: Before featurization, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges (Uncharger), so salts do not distort the features.

items.title: ErG and pharmacophore 2D features
items.spec: Add rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint (ErG) features and Gobbi 2D pharmacophore counts to descriptors for the RF/LightGBM.

items.title: Hist GBM with monotone-free tuned params
items.spec: Use HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_depth=5, learning_rate=0.05, max_iter=300, l2_regularization=1.0, random_state=seed) on descriptors+MACCS.

items.title: Pseudo-label self-training
items.spec: Fit the RF, predict test molecules, add test molecules with confidence >0.9 or <0.1 as pseudo-labels, refit, and predict again. Transductive on unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Scaffold-aware sample weights
items.spec: Compute Murcko scaffolds of the training molecules and weight each sample by 1/sqrt(scaffold group size) in RF fit, to reduce dominance by large scaffold families.

items.title: Random-forest on MACCS+descriptors
items.spec: Drop Morgan; use MACCS keys plus RDKit descriptors with RF (max_features=0.3, 500 trees, min_samples_leaf=1).

items.title: Descriptor + Morgan RF with sqrt features
items.spec: Use Morgan bits (1024) with descriptors and set max_features='sqrt', n_estimators=800, to give descriptors a better chance of being selected.

items.title: Small MLP ensemble on descriptors
items.spec: Quantile-transform descriptors, then average 5 sklearn MLPClassifier models (hidden 128,64, alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, random_state=seed+i).

items.title: Add RDKit 2D descriptors
items.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors (about 210 values: TPSA, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, MW, etc.) as features in addition to Morgan bits. Replace NaN/inf with 0 and clip extreme values. Keep the random forest. Descriptors like TPSA are key to BBB penetration.

items.title: Descriptors only RF
items.spec: Drop the fingerprint and use only RDKit 2D descriptors (nan_to_num, clipped to +-1e6) with the RandomForest, to test whether fingerprints help generalization to unseen scaffolds.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors
items.spec: Replace RF with LGBMClassifier (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, subsample 0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) on RDKit descriptors plus Morgan counts.

items.title: ExtraTrees on descriptors+FP
items.spec: Swap RandomForest for ExtraTreesClassifier (500 trees, max_features=0.3) on the descriptors plus Morgan bits concatenated.

items.title: Morgan count fingerprints
items.spec: Use count-based Morgan fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) radius 2 with 2048 bits instead of binary bits, with the RF.

items.title: Add MACCS keys
items.spec: Concatenate MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, 167 bits) to the Morgan bits and the RDKit descriptors for the RF.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion counts
items.spec: Add atom pair and topological torsion count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator, fpSize 1024 each) to the features, in addition to Morgan.

items.title: Feature-based Morgan (FCFP)
items.spec: Use Morgan with the FeatureMorgan atom invariants generator (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen), radius 3, count-based, 2048 bits, which generalizes across scaffolds better than ECFP.

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use CatBoostClassifier (iterations 600, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on RDKit descriptors plus MACCS keys.

items.title: XGBoost small trees
items.spec: Use XGBClassifier (n_estimators 500, max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.4, min_child_weight 2, n_jobs 8) on descriptors plus MACCS.

items.title: RF + GBM rank ensemble
items.spec: Average rank-normalized predictions of an RF on Morgan bits and a LightGBM on descriptors, with equal weights.

items.title: Seed bagging ensemble
items.spec: Train 3 models (RF, ExtraTrees, LightGBM) with different seeds derived from seed on the same descriptor+MACCS features and average probabilities.

items.title: Balanced class weights
items.spec: Set class_weight='balanced_subsample' in the RF, since BBB data are imbalanced toward positives.

items.title: RF min_samples_leaf 3
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=3 and MAX_FEATURES='sqrt' to smooth probabilities and reduce overfitting on unseen scaffolds.

items.title: More trees
items.spec: Increase N_TREES to 1000 and use max_features 0.2 on the existing fingerprint to reduce variance.

items.title: Logistic regression on scaled descriptors
items.spec: Use a pipeline of StandardScaler (after clipping and quantile transform) and LogisticRegression(C=0.1, max_iter=2000) on RDKit descriptors; add as a blend with RF at 0.3 weight.

items.title: SVM RBF on descriptors
items.spec: SVC(kernel='rbf', probability=True, C=3, gamma='scale', random_state=seed) on QuantileTransformed descriptors, blended 50/50 with the RF on fingerprints.

items.title: Tanimoto kernel SVM
items.spec: Compute a Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (minmax kernel) and fit SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1, probability=True) in place of the RF.

items.title: Small physchem feature set
items.spec: Use a hand-picked set of about 15 descriptors (TPSA, MolLogP, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3, charge counts, acid/base group counts, aromatic rings, HeavyAtomCount, LabuteASA) with GradientBoosting or RF, as a low-variance model.

items.title: Acid/base substructure flags
items.spec: Add SMARTS-count features for carboxylic acid, sulfonamide, tertiary/secondary/primary amine, quaternary N, amidine, and phenol, concatenated to descriptors for the tree model.

items.title: Feature selection by variance
items.spec: Remove features with fewer than 5 nonzero training molecules or zero variance before fitting the RF, with the Morgan fingerprint count at 4096 bits.

items.title: Canonicalize and strip salts
items.spec: Before featurization, parse the SMILES, keep the largest fragment, neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize Uncharger, and use these molecules for features.

items.title: Stacking with logistic meta
items.spec: Build out-of-fold predictions inside fit_predict (5-fold GroupKFold by Murcko scaffold) for RF-FP, LGBM-descriptor, and SVM models, then fit a logistic regression meta-learner and apply to test.

items.title: Scaffold-aware sample weights
items.spec: Weight each training molecule by 1/sqrt(size of its Murcko scaffold group) when fitting the RF or LightGBM so large scaffold families do not dominate.

items.title: Gasteiger charge descriptors
items.spec: Add features from Gasteiger partial charges: max, min, sum of absolute charges, and polar surface contributions (PEOE_VSA, SlogP_VSA, SMR_VSA bins) to the descriptor set.

items.title: LightGBM with DART
items.spec: LGBMClassifier with boosting_type='dart', 300 estimators, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15, colsample_bytree 0.5, on descriptors plus MACCS.

items.title: Random Forest on 3D-free MQN descriptors
items.spec: Add rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_ (42 molecular quantum numbers) and CalcNumAmideBonds etc. to the descriptors for the RF.

items.title: MLP on descriptors
items.spec: sklearn MLPClassifier(hidden_layer_sizes=(128,64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, random_state=seed) on quantile-transformed descriptors, averaged over 5 seeds, blended with RF 50/50.

items.title: Calibrated isotonic RF output
items.spec: Wrap the RF with CalibratedClassifierCV(method='sigmoid', cv=3) to rescale probabilities; AUROC may improve via smoother ranking with the descriptors plus Morgan features.

items.title: Morgan radius 3 with chirality off, 1024 bits
items.spec: Use Morgan radius 1 count fingerprints with fpSize 1024 combined with descriptors, as shorter-radius substructures generalize better across scaffolds; use RF with max_features 0.2.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy using the same Morgan generator (radius 2, 2048 bits). Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged. Substructure multiplicity often carries signal that the binary bit vector discards.

items.title: Append MACCS keys to Morgan bits
items.spec: Compute rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule (167 bits) and concatenate it to the existing 2048-bit Morgan vector before fitting the RandomForest. MACCS encodes coarse functional-group presence, which complements the local Morgan environments.

items.title: Append RDKit 2D physchem descriptors
items.spec: Compute all values from rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList for each molecule, replace NaN and inf with 0, clip each column to its 1st and 99th training percentiles, and concatenate the result to the Morgan features. Physicochemical properties such as TPSA, MolLogP, MW and HBD drive blood-brain barrier penetration, so the tree model gets them directly.

items.title: Compact BBB-prior descriptor set
items.spec: Build a small dense feature vector from about 12 descriptors known to govern brain penetration: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, RingCount, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, formal charge, and the count of carboxylic acid groups. Fit a RandomForest on this alone and on the Morgan bits concatenated with it, keeping whichever gives the better cross-validated loss.

items.title: Atom-pair count fingerprints
items.spec: Replace the Morgan generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator (fpSize 2048, default distance range) and use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy for the features. Atom-pair descriptors capture topological distances between functional groups and are a different view of the molecule from circular fingerprints.

items.title: Topological torsion count fingerprints
items.spec: Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator (fpSize 2048) with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy as the feature extractor, and fit the existing RandomForest on it. Torsion paths encode four-atom chains, which describe conformational flexibility and linker shape relevant to membrane permeation.

items.title: Feature-invariant (FCFP-style) Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Create the Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator set to rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), keeping radius 2 and 2048 bits, and use count fingerprints. Mapping atoms to pharmacophoric classes (donor, acceptor, aromatic, acidic, basic) generalizes better across unseen scaffolds than element-identity atoms.

items.title: Larger, wider Morgan fingerprint
items.spec: Set RADIUS = 3 and N_BITS = 4096 so that fewer bits collide and deeper environments are represented. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged. Check whether the extra depth helps or simply adds noise under scaffold-held-out folds.

items.title: Ionization-state group counts
items.spec: Add a small block of counts for ionizable groups, each computed with SMARTS patterns: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, sulfonic or phosphonic acid, primary, secondary and tertiary aliphatic amines, amidine or guanidine, quaternary ammonium, and phenol. Append these counts to the Morgan features. Acids reduce brain penetration and basic amines often increase it, so these counts act as explicit ionization features.

items.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing
items.spec: In featurize, parse each SMILES, take the largest fragment with rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and fall back to the original molecule if sanitization fails. Compute the Morgan features from the standardized molecule. This removes salt counterions and charge-state noise that would otherwise change the fingerprints.

items.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute column sums of the training fingerprint matrix and keep only columns that are set in at least 1% of training molecules. Apply the same column mask to the test features. This removes sparse bits that the forest memorizes from a few molecules and that generalize poorly to new scaffolds.

items.title: LightGBM in place of the random forest
items.spec: Replace RandomForestClassifier with lightgbm.LGBMClassifier using n_estimators 400, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 31, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.5, and random_state=seed. Use the same Morgan features. Gradient boosting usually beats bagged trees on fingerprint classification when the signal is weak.

items.title: XGBoost histogram model
items.spec: Replace the random forest with xgboost.XGBClassifier using tree_method 'hist', n_estimators 400, learning_rate 0.05, max_depth 6, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, and random_state=seed. Keep the Morgan features. Gives a second boosting implementation for comparison against LightGBM.

items.title: CatBoost classifier
items.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostClassifier with iterations 600, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, and thread_count=8 on the Morgan features. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees resist overfitting on small, noisy datasets like this one.

items.title: Standardized logistic regression on descriptors
items.spec: Compute RDKit 2D descriptors for each molecule, replace NaN and inf with 0, clip to training 1st and 99th percentiles, and standardize with a StandardScaler fitted on the training fold. Fit sklearn LogisticRegression with C=0.1 and max_iter 2000. A regularized linear model on physchem properties is a strong baseline for BBB penetration and gives a diverse ensemble member.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM
items.spec: Compute Morgan count fingerprints, then build a MinMax (Tanimoto-style) kernel matrix K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)) between training and test molecules. Fit sklearn SVC with kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, and use decision_function on the test kernel as the score, because AUROC depends only on ranking. Chemical-similarity kernels are well suited to fingerprint data.

items.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour vote
items.spec: Compute Morgan bit fingerprints and Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules. Take the k=10 most similar training molecules and return a similarity-weighted mean of their labels, with weights equal to the Tanimoto values raised to the power 3. A nearest-neighbour score is a non-parametric model that adds diversity to tree-based ensembles.

items.title: Multilayer perceptron on fingerprints and descriptors
items.spec: Concatenate Morgan bits with standardized RDKit descriptors (cleaned as above). Fit sklearn MLPClassifier with hidden_layer_sizes (256, 64), alpha=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.1, max_iter 300, and random_state=seed. Average the predictions of 3 seeds inside fit_predict to reduce variance.

items.title: ExtraTrees classifier
items.spec: Replace RandomForestClassifier with sklearn ExtraTreesClassifier using 1000 trees, max_features 'sqrt', min_samples_leaf 2, and random_state=seed on the same Morgan features. Extremely randomized splits smooth the decision function and often generalize better on small, noisy fingerprint datasets.

items.title: Retuned random forest regularization
items.spec: Keep RandomForestClassifier but set max_features to 'sqrt', min_samples_leaf to 2, max_depth to None, and n_estimators to 1000. Lower-variance trees with a larger ensemble should improve the averaged ranking that AUROC rewards. Only these hyperparameters change.

items.title: Class-balanced weighting
items.spec: Pass class_weight='balanced_subsample' to RandomForestClassifier, or compute scale_pos_weight equal to the ratio of negatives to positives and pass it to the boosting model if one is used. This keeps the minority class from being underweighted during fitting. Only the weighting is changed.

items.title: Stronger LightGBM regularization
items.spec: Use LightGBM with learning_rate 0.03, n_estimators 500, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 30, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.7 with bagging_freq 1, reg_lambda 5.0, and random_state=seed. Heavier regularization limits how strongly individual rare substructures can drive predictions on unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Learning-rate decay schedule for boosting
items.spec: Train LightGBM with 600 rounds and pass a reset_parameter callback that decays learning_rate geometrically from 0.1 to 0.01 over the rounds, using lgb.train with the Dataset API. Use random_state=seed. Decaying shrinkage lets early trees capture coarse structure and later trees refine it.

items.title: Inner early stopping for boosting rounds
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training fold with StratifiedShuffleSplit into 90 percent fit and 10 percent validation using seed. Train LightGBM with up to 2000 rounds at learning_rate 0.03 and early_stopping(100) on the validation split, read best_iteration, then refit on the full training fold with that many rounds. The number of rounds is chosen from data, not fixed by hand.

items.title: Bagged boosting over bootstrap replicates
items.spec: Train 5 LightGBM models, each on a bootstrap sample of the training fold drawn with a seed derived from the base seed, with different random_state values. Average their test probabilities. The averaging reduces variance from any single boosting run.

items.title: Adam MLP with minibatches and weight decay
items.spec: Use a PyTorch-free approach with sklearn MLPClassifier: solver='adam', learning_rate_init=1e-3, batch_size=64, alpha=1e-2 for L2 weight decay, hidden_layer_sizes (512, 128), max_iter 200, early_stopping=True, and random_state=seed. Inputs are Morgan bits concatenated with standardized descriptors. Small minibatches with explicit weight decay give a differently regularized neural model.

items.title: Rank-averaged ensemble of RF, LightGBM and logistic regression
items.spec: Fit three models on the training fold: the existing RandomForest on Morgan bits, a LightGBM on Morgan bits plus descriptors, and a standardized logistic regression on descriptors. Convert each model's test scores to ranks within the test set, average the three rank vectors with weights 0.4, 0.4 and 0.2, and return the average rescaled to [0, 1]. Rank averaging is robust to differences in score calibration between models.

items.title: Stacked meta-learner over base models
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute out-of-fold predictions on the training fold with an inner 5-fold StratifiedKFold for three base models: the RandomForest, a LightGBM, and a logistic regression on descriptors. Fit a LogisticRegression meta-model on these out-of-fold scores, then apply the base models refit on the full training fold to the test set and feed their scores to the meta-model. Stacking learns how much to trust each base model.

items.title: Transductive pseudo-labeling of confident test molecules
items.spec: Fit the baseline RandomForest, predict the test molecules, then add the test molecules whose probability is above 0.8 as label 1 or below 0.2 as label 0 to the training set. Refit the RandomForest on the augmented set and output its predictions for the test molecules. Only the test SMILES are used, not their labels, so the procedure is legitimate. It lets the model adapt to the query scaffolds.

items.title: Out-of-fold similarity-to-class features
items.spec: For each training molecule, compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity to training actives and to training inactives, excluding itself and using 5-fold inner splits so that no label leaks into its own feature. For test molecules, use similarities to all training actives and inactives. Append these two similarity features to the Morgan bits and fit the RandomForest. Nearest-neighbour label evidence is a strong feature for classifying molecules that resemble known examples.

items.title: Add RDKit physicochemical descriptors
items.spec: In featurize, append the full RDKit descriptor set from rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList (MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, RingCount, FractionCSP3, etc.) to the Morgan bit vector. Replace NaN and inf values with 0 and clip extreme values to the 0.001 to 0.999 quantiles of the training set. Keep the RandomForest unchanged otherwise.

items.title: Physchem-only feature set
items.spec: Replace the Morgan fingerprint with a small set of about 12 interpretable descriptors known to govern BBB penetration: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, formal charge, count of carboxylic acids, count of basic amines, aromatic ring count, heavy atom count, and fraction sp3. Train the same RandomForest on these only. Compare to the fingerprint baseline inside the same job.

items.title: Combine fingerprint and physchem features
items.spec: Build the feature matrix as the concatenation of the 2048-bit Morgan count fingerprint (radius 2) and a compact physchem vector (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, charge, acid and base counts). Use the same RandomForest with max_features 0.3.

items.title: Morgan count fingerprints instead of bits
items.spec: Switch from binary Morgan bits to hashed count fingerprints using GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with the same radius and 2048 size. Counts carry more information about repeated substructures. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged.

items.title: Feature-count sweep for Morgan radius and size
items.spec: Vary the Morgan settings inside fit_predict by testing radius 1, 2, and 3 with fpSize 1024, 2048, and 4096. Pick the combination with the best 3-fold inner cross-validated AUROC on the training fold only, then fit on all training data with that setting. Use the seed for any tie-breaking.

items.title: MACCS keys plus Morgan
items.spec: Append the 167-bit MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the Morgan fingerprint. MACCS encodes general pharmacophore-like substructures that complement the local circular environments of Morgan. Keep the RandomForest and its settings unchanged.

items.title: Atom-pair and topological torsion fingerprints
items.spec: Add hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, 1024 bits) and topological torsion counts (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 1024 bits) alongside the Morgan features. Concatenate all blocks into one matrix for the RandomForest.

items.title: RDKit path-based fingerprint block
items.spec: Add the RDKit topological (path-based) fingerprint from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetRDKitFPGenerator with maxPath 6 and fpSize 1024 to the Morgan features. Concatenate and train the same RandomForest. This captures linear fragments that circular Morgan can miss.

items.title: Replace RandomForest with ExtraTrees
items.spec: Use sklearn ExtraTreesClassifier with 500 trees, max_features sqrt, min_samples_leaf 1, n_jobs -1 and random_state=seed on the existing Morgan features. Extra randomized splits often reduce variance on small noisy datasets like this one.

items.title: LightGBM gradient boosting on fingerprints
items.spec: Replace the RandomForest with LightGBM (LGBMClassifier) using 400 estimators, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging_fraction 0.8 with bagging_freq 1, min_child_samples 10, and random_state=seed. Use the existing Morgan features and n_jobs 8.

items.title: CatBoost on fingerprints plus descriptors
items.spec: Use CatBoostClassifier with 800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 3, random_seed=seed, verbose 0, thread_count 8 on the Morgan plus RDKit descriptor features. Gradient boosted symmetric trees handle mixed binary and continuous inputs well.

items.title: XGBoost with histogram trees
items.spec: Use XGBClassifier with tree_method hist, 500 estimators, max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.05, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 2, random_state=seed, n_jobs 8 on the Morgan features. Output predict_proba class 1.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between binary Morgan fingerprints (intersection over union, computed with numpy on the 2048-bit matrices). Train sklearn SVC with kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed. Predict on test-to-train Tanimoto matrix. Similarity kernels are a strong baseline for molecular property prediction.

items.title: Gaussian-process style kernel ridge on Tanimoto
items.spec: Use the min-max (Tanimoto-like) kernel on Morgan count fingerprints, fit sklearn KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed' and alpha 0.5 on labels mapped to plus or minus one, then map predictions to (0,1) with a logistic squash so that ranks are preserved for AUROC.

items.title: Logistic regression on fingerprints with L2
items.spec: Train sklearn LogisticRegression with C=0.1, max_iter 2000, solver liblinear, random_state=seed on standardized RDKit descriptors plus Morgan bits. Linear models provide a different inductive bias to add to tree ensembles later.

items.title: Soft-vote ensemble of RF, ExtraTrees and LightGBM
items.spec: Train three models on the same features: RandomForest, ExtraTreesClassifier, and LGBMClassifier with fixed moderate settings and seed-derived random states. Average their predicted probabilities with equal weights and return the mean. Averaging diverse tree models usually lowers variance.

items.title: Rank-average ensemble of fingerprint and descriptor models
items.spec: Fit one RandomForest on Morgan bits and one gradient boosting model on RDKit descriptors. Convert each model's test probabilities to ranks within the test set, average the ranks, and rescale to (0,1). Rank averaging suits the AUROC metric.

items.title: Multi-seed bagging of the forest
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, train 5 RandomForest models with random_state values derived from seed (seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4), each with 200 trees, and average their predict_proba outputs. This reduces the variance from any single random draw.

items.title: Balanced class weights
items.spec: Set class_weight='balanced' on the RandomForest so that minority-class errors are weighted more heavily. AUROC is sensitive to ranking across classes, so balanced weighting can improve the ordering of the positive class even when the base rate is skewed.

items.title: Limit tree depth and raise leaf size
items.spec: Set min_samples_leaf to 3 and max_depth to 20 on the RandomForest. Stronger leaf regularization smooths probability estimates and can help with the noisy labels and unseen scaffolds in this benchmark.

items.title: Tune max_features on the forest
items.spec: Sweep the RandomForest max_features over sqrt, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5 using a 3-fold stratified inner cross-validation on the training fold only (grouped by Murcko scaffold if easy). Refit using the best value. Keep the seed fixed.

items.title: Calibrated probabilities via isotonic on OOB
items.spec: Use the RandomForest out-of-bag predictions (oob_score=True, bootstrap True) to fit an isotonic regression mapping from raw score to probability, then apply it to test predictions. Monotone mapping leaves AUROC unchanged in principle but corrects tie and ordering artifacts from averaging.

items.title: Scaffold-aware target smoothing via neighbor labels
items.spec: For each test molecule, compute the Tanimoto similarity to all training molecules, take the k=10 nearest neighbors, and blend the forest probability with the similarity-weighted mean of their labels (alpha 0.5). This adds a kNN component that is robust for molecules sharing close analogues.

items.title: Pure kNN with Tanimoto similarity
items.spec: Predict each test molecule's score as the Tanimoto-similarity-weighted average of the labels of its k=7 most similar training molecules on binary Morgan fingerprints. Use the seed only for tie breaking. This nonparametric baseline complements tree models.

items.title: Data augmentation via SMILES canonical variants
items.spec: For each training molecule, add a second representation generated by MolToSMILES with doRandom=True (seeded) and featurize it as an extra training row with the same label. Augmenting with alternative SMILES strings is a cheap regularizer for fingerprint models that otherwise see only one canonical form. Only the Morgan features are affected by SMILES order when using counts, so keep the same featurization.

items.title: Remove unparseable or salt-containing molecules safely
items.spec: Before featurizing, strip salts and counterions by keeping the largest covalent fragment (rdkit.Chem.SaltRemover or sorting fragments by heavy atom count), then compute features. Fallback to the original molecule if parsing fails. Cleaning inputs can make descriptors such as TPSA and logP more consistent.

items.title: Charge-state and neutralization normalization
items.spec: Neutralize charged atoms in each molecule using rdMolStandardize.Uncharger before computing fingerprints and descriptors, falling back to the original molecule on failure. Ionization artifacts (e.g. carboxylates versus acids) otherwise split chemically identical compounds into different feature vectors.

items.title: Stratified bagging with bootstrap resampling of scaffolds
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, draw 10 bootstrap samples of the training set where rows are resampled at the Murcko-scaffold level instead of row level, train a small RandomForest (150 trees) on each, and average predictions. Scaffold-level resampling mirrors the grouped evaluation and reduces overfitting to specific ring systems.

items.title: Add counts of pharmacophore features
items.spec: Compute RDKit Gobbi 2D pharmacophore count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariants from rdReducedGraphs or Gobbi pharmacophore features) and append them to the Morgan bit vector. Pharmacophore features capture donor, acceptor, and ionizable groups relevant to membrane permeation.

items.title: Platt-free probability sharpening via power transform
items.spec: After computing the ensemble probability p, return p raised to a power gamma of 0.8 renormalized to (0,1) by p^gamma/(p^gamma+(1-p)^gamma). This monotone transform keeps AUROC unchanged for a single model but changes how averaged ensembles tie-break; keep it only if it helps in the replicate job.

items.title: Two-stage model: descriptors then residual fingerprint boosting
items.spec: First fit a logistic regression on physchem descriptors (TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, HBD, HBA, charge, acid and base counts) to produce a baseline logit. Then fit a LightGBM model on Morgan bits with the baseline logit added as a feature (or as init_score). Staged modelling lets simple physics-like rules carry the main signal while fingerprints model residuals.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same radius-2, 2048-bit Morgan generator, so each bit holds the number of times that substructure occurs instead of a 0/1 flag. Leave the RandomForest settings unchanged. The rest of fit_predict stays the same.

items.title: Larger Morgan radius and fold size
items.spec: Set RADIUS = 3 and N_BITS = 4096 in the settings block. This keeps the same featurize and RandomForest code. It captures larger substructures and reduces bit collisions.

items.title: Feature-invariant (FCFP-style) Morgan
items.spec: In featurize, build the Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen() so atoms are typed by pharmacophore features (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) rather than exact element identity. Keep radius 2, 2048 bits, and the existing RandomForest.

items.title: Add RDKit physicochemical descriptors
items.spec: Append a small set of interpretable descriptors to each fingerprint vector: MolWt, MolLogP, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, RingCount, NumAromaticRings, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, and total formal charge. Compute them with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors and rdMolDescriptors and hstack them onto the Morgan array. Use the same RandomForest. TPSA and logP are the strongest known BBB penetration correlates.

items.title: Append MACCS structural keys
items.spec: In featurize, compute the 167-bit MACCS keys with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule and hstack them onto the Morgan fingerprint. Keep the rest of the pipeline the same. MACCS keys add coarse, interpretable substructure information.

items.title: Add atom-pair count fingerprints
items.spec: Also compute a 2048-bit atom-pair count fingerprint with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator and GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Concatenate it with the Morgan features so the RandomForest sees both topological views. Keep the same model and seed handling.

items.title: Add topological torsion counts
items.spec: Compute a 1024-bit topological torsion count fingerprint with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator and GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Concatenate it onto the Morgan features before fitting the RandomForest. This adds torsion-path information that Morgan radius-based bits miss.

items.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing
items.spec: Before computing any features, parse each SMILES and strip counter-ions and salts with rdkit.Chem.MolStandardize.rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser, then neutralize charges with Uncharger. Fall back to the raw molecule if parsing fails. Featurize the cleaned molecules with the existing Morgan code. Many BBBP entries contain salts that otherwise dominate the fingerprint.

items.title: BBB-relevant SMARTS functional-group counts
items.spec: Define about ten SMARTS patterns for groups that affect BBB penetration: carboxylic acid, primary, secondary and tertiary amine, quaternary ammonium, sulfonamide, hydroxyl, nitro, amide, and phosphate. For each molecule count the matches with Chem.MolFromSmarts and GetSubstructMatches, and hstack the counts onto the Morgan features. Acids and quaternary cations are known to penetrate the BBB poorly.

items.title: Replace RandomForest with ExtraTrees
items.spec: Swap RandomForestClassifier for sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesClassifier with n_estimators=500, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=-1, and random_state=seed. Keep the Morgan featurization. Extra-trees split randomly and often generalize better on small noisy fingerprint data.

items.title: Class-balanced RandomForest weights
items.spec: Pass class_weight='balanced_subsample' to the RandomForestClassifier constructor, leaving all other settings unchanged. This reweights the minority class in each bootstrap sample. It can change how the ranking of positives and negatives is learned, which matters for AUROC.

items.title: Tuned RandomForest regularization
items.spec: Set MAX_FEATURES to 'sqrt', MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 2, and N_TREES to 1000 in the settings block. Leave the rest of the code unchanged. Larger leaves and a smaller feature subset smooth the probability estimates and can reduce overfitting to the training scaffolds.

items.title: RandomForest with bootstrap subsampling
items.spec: Set bootstrap=True and max_samples=0.6 on the RandomForestClassifier so each tree sees a random 60% of the training rows. Keep the other settings the same. Smaller bootstrap samples decorrelate the trees, which often improves ranking quality on held-out scaffolds.

items.title: LightGBM on fingerprints plus descriptors
items.spec: Replace the RandomForest with LightGBM LGBMClassifier using n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, and random_state=seed, with n_jobs=8. Feed it the Morgan bits plus the physicochemical descriptors from the descriptor idea. Gradient boosting usually beats random forests on tabular fingerprint problems.

items.title: XGBoost binary classifier
items.spec: Use xgboost.XGBClassifier with tree_method='hist', max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.05, n_estimators=500, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, eval_metric='logloss', n_jobs=8, and random_state=seed on the Morgan features. Return predict_proba[:,1]. Shallow boosted trees reduce variance versus deep trees.

items.title: CatBoost on Morgan counts
items.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostClassifier with depth=6, iterations=800, learning_rate=0.05, l2_leaf_reg=3, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=False on the count-based Morgan features. CatBoost's ordered boosting is robust on small datasets and gives well-calibrated scores.

items.title: Inner-validation early stopping for boosting
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training set into 90% and 10% with a stratified split using the seed. Train LightGBM with early stopping on the 10% part (patience 50, logloss) to find the best iteration count. Refit on the full training set with that count (times 1.1) and predict on the test set. This avoids guessing the number of rounds.

items.title: Decaying learning-rate schedule for boosting
items.spec: Train LightGBM or XGBoost with a learning-rate schedule that starts at 0.1 and decays exponentially to 0.01 over the boosting rounds. Implement it with the callback that resets the learning rate each iteration (for example lgb.reset_parameter with a list of decaying values). Use 500 rounds. The decay gives coarse fits early and fine adjustments late.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM
items.spec: Compute the binary Morgan fingerprints for train and test. Build the Tanimoto kernel K(A,B)=sum(min)/sum(max) by matrix products on bit vectors (A·B / (|A|+|B|-A·B)). Fit sklearn.svm.SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed) and predict with the test-by-train kernel. The Tanimoto kernel is the standard similarity measure for molecular fingerprints.

items.title: Weighted Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour model
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules on binary Morgan bits. Take the k=10 most similar training molecules and predict the weighted mean of their labels with weights similarity**3. Return this as the probability. A similarity-based vote captures local SAR that tree models can miss.

items.title: Logistic regression on standardized features
items.spec: Build the descriptor-plus-Morgan feature matrix, standardize it with StandardScaler fitted on the training fold, and fit sklearn.linear_model.LogisticRegression(C=0.1, max_iter=2000). Return predict_proba[:,1]. A strongly regularized linear model is a diverse baseline for blending.

items.title: Regularized MLP on fingerprints
items.spec: Use sklearn.neural_network.MLPClassifier with hidden_layer_sizes=(512,), alpha=1e-3 (L2), learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=300, and random_state=seed. Standardize the Morgan bits and descriptors first. Dropout is not available, so the L2 penalty and early stopping provide the regularization.

items.title: Rank-averaged RF, LightGBM and SVM blend
items.spec: Train three models on the same features: the existing RandomForest, a LightGBM classifier, and the Tanimoto-kernel SVM. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks with scipy.stats.rankdata, divide by the count, and average them with equal weights. Return the averaged rank score in [0,1]. Rank averaging is safe for AUROC and blends diverse learners.

items.title: Stacked ensemble with logistic meta-learner
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on the training set for three base models (RandomForest, LightGBM, and logistic regression on the Morgan bits). Fit a LogisticRegression meta-model on the stacked out-of-fold probabilities. For the test set, average the base models trained on the full training set and pass them through the meta-model. Stacking learns how much to trust each base model.

items.title: Randomized-SMILES augmentation
items.spec: For each training molecule, generate 5 extra SMILES strings with Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True) (use a fixed random seed derived from the seed argument). Featurize the original plus augmented SMILES and train the RandomForest on the enlarged set with the labels copied. At test time, average the predictions over several randomized SMILES of each test molecule. This is a standard test-time augmentation for molecular models.

items.title: Self-training on confident test predictions
items.spec: Fit the RandomForest on the training set, then predict the test set.
