Add test molecules with predicted probability above 0.85 as label 1 or below 0.15 as label 0, and refit on the training set plus these pseudo-labelled molecules. Return the probabilities from the refit model. Pseudo-labelling uses unlabelled test structure and can adapt to new scaffolds.

items.title: Multi-radius RandomForest ensemble
items.spec: Train three RandomForestClassifiers on Morgan features at radius 1, 2 and 3 (2048 bits each), each with a different seed offset from the seed argument. Average their predict_proba[:,1] outputs equally. This ensemble covers local and wider substructure contexts without changing the feature definition itself.

items.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits
items.spec: After featurizing the training set, compute the number of training molecules with each bit set and keep only bits present in at least 3 molecules. Apply the same column selection to the test features. Fit the RandomForest on the reduced matrix. Removing near-empty bits cuts noise, speeds up training, and lowers the chance of spurious splits.

items.title: Capped tree size via max leaf nodes
items.spec: Set max_leaf_nodes=200 and min_samples_leaf=2 on the RandomForestClassifier, with N_TREES=800. Keep the Morgan features and other settings unchanged. Capping the number of leaves limits the complexity of each tree and gives smoother probability estimates, which can help with the held-out-scaffold shift.

items.title: Count Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace binary Morgan bits with count fingerprints: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy (radius 2, 2048 bits) in featurize and keep the random forest. Counts carry more information about substructure multiplicity.

items.title: RDKit 2D descriptors
items.spec: Add all RDKit descriptors (rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList) as features, replacing the fingerprint. Use np.nan_to_num and clip to ±1e6. Keep the RF. Clearance correlates with logP, TPSA and MW, so these should generalize across scaffolds.

items.title: Descriptors + count Morgan concat
items.spec: Concatenate RDKit descriptors (cleaned with nan_to_num and clipping) with count Morgan radius 2 at 1024 bits. Feed to RF with max_features=0.3.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors+counts
items.spec: Replace the RF with LGBMRegressor (n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on descriptors plus count Morgan features.

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor (iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.03, rsm=0.3, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on RDKit descriptors plus MACCS keys.

items.title: MACCS keys added
items.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the feature matrix with Morgan bits. Keep the RF.

items.title: Rank-transform target
items.spec: Train on the rank-transformed target (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n, optionally mapped to normal quantiles with norm.ppf). The metric is Spearman, so this reduces outlier influence. Predictions need no inversion.

items.title: Extra trees
items.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2) on the current features.

items.title: RF min_samples_leaf tune
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=3 and MAX_FEATURES=0.2 with N_TREES=500. Smoother leaves may help noisy clearance data.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion counts
items.spec: Add atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, counts) to the features, alongside Morgan. Use the RF.

items.title: Feature-wise variance filter
items.spec: Drop fingerprint columns that are non-zero in fewer than 5 training molecules (compute on the training set, apply to test). This reduces noise features for the tree model.

items.title: Larger Morgan radius 3 with features
items.spec: Use Morgan radius 3 with counts at 2048 bits, with useFeatures-style invariants (the feature-Morgan atom invariants generator) as an extra block next to the standard one.

items.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Implement a Tanimoto (minmax on counts) kernel matrix in numpy and fit sklearn SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on count Morgan. Use the rank-transformed target.

items.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto
items.spec: Use KernelRidge with a precomputed minmax Tanimoto kernel on count Morgan fingerprints, alpha=1.0. Standardize y first.

items.title: RF + LGBM + SVR ensemble
items.spec: Average the rank-normalized predictions of the RF (descriptors+Morgan), LightGBM, and Tanimoto SVR. Rank each model's test predictions with rankdata before averaging.

items.title: Seed bagging
items.spec: Train 5 models with different seeds derived from seed, and average the predictions. This lowers variance for LGBM or XGBoost.

items.title: XGBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor (n_estimators=600, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3, reg_lambda=5, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on RDKit descriptors plus count Morgan at 1024 bits.

items.title: Huber / absolute-error objective
items.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='huber' (alpha=1.0) on standardized y, or RF with criterion='absolute_error' if fast enough. This is more robust to the skewed clearance values.

items.title: Log-transform target
items.spec: If train_y is positive and skewed, fit on log1p(y - min + 1) when skew > 1; otherwise leave it. Use the RF.

items.title: Crippen/MolLogP-focused small descriptor set
items.spec: Use a curated set of ~20 descriptors: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, RotBonds, rings, aromatic rings, FractionCSP3, charge counts, and halogen counts. Add them to Morgan counts, and weight them by using max_features=0.5 in an RF.

items.title: Scaffold-aware inner early stopping
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out 15% of training molecules grouped by Murcko scaffold. Use them to pick the number of LightGBM iterations by early stopping, then refit on all data with that count.

items.title: Gaussian process on Tanimoto
items.spec: Implement GP regression in numpy with a Tanimoto kernel plus a noise term (1.0 on the standardized y, tuned via a small marginal-likelihood grid over noise in {0.3,1,3}). Predict the posterior mean.

items.title: Dummy-variance: Avalon and ErG fingerprints
items.spec: Add Avalon count fingerprints (rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP, 1024 bits) and ErG fingerprints (rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint) to the feature set. Use the RF.

items.title: Stacked ridge over model ranks
items.spec: Fit RF, LGBM and SVR with 5-fold inner out-of-fold predictions on the training data. Fit a non-negative ridge (positive=True) on the OOF predictions to weight the final ensemble.

items.title: Salt stripping and canonicalization
items.spec: Before featurizing, keep only the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), and neutralize charges with Uncharger. This reduces noise from counter-ions.

items.title: Random-feature subsample ensemble
items.spec: Build a bagged ensemble of 10 LightGBM models, each trained on a random 70% of rows and a random 50% of columns. Average the predictions.

items.title: MLP on descriptors
items.spec: Standardize descriptors with a QuantileTransformer (normal output), then fit sklearn MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256,64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True, random_state=seed). Average over 5 seeds. Blend 50/50 by rank with the RF.

items.title: Morgan fold size 4096 with min-count
items.spec: Use count Morgan at 4096 bits, radius 2, and drop bits seen fewer than 3 times in training. Use the RF with max_features=0.2.

items.title: Sample weighting by scaffold size
items.spec: Compute Murcko scaffolds of the training set and give each sample weight 1/sqrt(scaffold group size). Pass it as sample_weight to the RF fit. This reduces domination by large scaffold series, matching the scaffold-split test.

items.title: Rank-average RF and CatBoost
items.spec: Fit an RF on Morgan counts and a CatBoost on descriptors. Average their rankdata-normalized predictions with equal weights.

items.title: Count Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace binary Morgan bits with count fingerprints: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy (radius 2, 2048) and keep the RF. Counts carry more information about substituent multiplicity.

items.title: RDKit 2D descriptors
items.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors.descList values (about 200) as features, replacing the fingerprint. Use nan_to_num, clip to +-1e6 and keep the RF. Descriptors like logP, TPSA and MW relate to clearance and generalize across scaffolds.

items.title: Descriptors plus count Morgan concat
items.spec: Concatenate RDKit descriptors (cleaned with nan_to_num and clipping) and count Morgan fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits). Fit the RF with max_features 0.3.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors
items.spec: Use LGBMRegressor on RDKit descriptors plus count Morgan. Settings: n_estimators 500, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_samples 10, random_state seed, n_jobs 8.

items.title: CatBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor (iterations 800, depth 6, learning_rate 0.03, l2_leaf_reg 5, random_seed seed, thread_count 8, verbose 0) on RDKit descriptors plus MACCS keys.

items.title: Rank-transform target
items.spec: Convert train_y to normalized ranks (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n, then optionally mapped to normal scores with norm.ppf) before fitting. This matches the Spearman metric and reduces outlier influence.

items.title: ExtraTrees swap
items.spec: Replace RandomForest with ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1). It is often smoother on high-dimensional sparse fingerprints.

items.title: Increase min_samples_leaf
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 3 and N_TREES to 500 to smooth predictions on noisy targets.

items.title: MACCS keys addition
items.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the Morgan bits as extra features.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints
items.spec: Add count atom-pair fingerprints (2048 bits) from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, and concatenate them with Morgan counts. Use the RF.

items.title: Feature-selected RF
items.spec: Drop fingerprint columns that are on in fewer than 5 training molecules or in more than 95% of them. Apply the same mask to the test set. Then fit the RF with max_features 0.5.

items.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Compute a Tanimoto kernel on count or binary Morgan fingerprints and fit sklearn SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1). Predict with the test-by-train kernel.

items.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto
items.spec: Use KernelRidge with a precomputed MinMax/Tanimoto kernel on count Morgan (radius 3) and alpha 1.0. Use rank-normalized targets.

items.title: Gaussian process Tanimoto regression
items.spec: Implement GP regression manually with a Tanimoto kernel: K + noise*I, with noise 0.5, solved by scipy.linalg.solve. Predict the posterior mean on centered targets.

items.title: Ensemble RF + LightGBM + SVR
items.spec: Average the rank-normalized predictions of three models, an RF on Morgan, LightGBM on descriptors and a Tanimoto SVR. Rank-normalize each model's test predictions with rankdata before averaging.

items.title: Log-target transform
items.spec: If the target is skewed and positive, fit on log1p(y - min + 1). Otherwise standardize y. Predictions are only ranked, so a monotone transform of y mainly changes the loss weighting.

items.title: Larger Morgan radius with feature chirality
items.spec: Use radius 3, 4096 bits, and includeChirality via GetMorganGenerator(includeChirality=True). Use count output.

items.title: Functional-group fragment counts
items.spec: Add the rdkit.Chem.Fragments fr_* counts (about 85 functions) to the descriptor set. Combine with descriptors and use LightGBM or the RF.

items.title: Feature-based Morgan (FCFP)
items.spec: Use Morgan with atomInvariantsGenerator=GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 3, counts. Concatenate with the ECFP counts. These pharmacophoric environments generalize better across scaffolds.

items.title: XGBoost with shallow trees
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor (n_estimators 600, max_depth 4, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.7, colsample_bytree 0.3, reg_lambda 5, n_jobs 8, random_state seed) on descriptors plus count Morgan.

items.title: Seed bagging of boosted models
items.spec: Train 5 LightGBM models with different seeds derived from seed and different subsample/colsample draws, then average their predictions. Use descriptors as features.

items.title: Standardize and drop salts
items.spec: Before featurizing, keep only the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges (Uncharger). This removes counterion noise.

items.title: Ridge/PLS on descriptors blend
items.spec: Fit a RidgeCV on StandardScaler-scaled, clipped descriptors, then blend its ranks 30/70 with the RF ranks. A linear model adds diversity on unseen scaffolds.

items.title: MLP on descriptors
items.spec: Use sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden layers 256,64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping, max_iter 500, random_state seed) on QuantileTransformer-scaled descriptors. Average 5 seeds.

items.title: Inner-CV model weighting
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run scaffold-ish GroupKFold (grouped by Murcko scaffold) on the training data for 2-3 candidate models. Then pick blend weights by inner Spearman. Predict with the best weighted mix.

items.title: Max_features tuning for RF on descriptors
items.spec: RF on descriptors plus Morgan counts with max_features 0.2 and min_samples_leaf 2, 500 trees. Also try max_features='sqrt'.

items.title: Crippen/partial-charge descriptors and 3D-free shape
items.spec: Add the MQN, Crippen contributions (rdMolDescriptors.SlogP_VSA, SMR_VSA, PEOE_VSA) and BCUT2D descriptors to the feature set. Fit the RF/LightGBM.

items.title: Sample weighting by scaffold size
items.spec: Weight each training sample by 1/sqrt(size of its Murcko scaffold group) in RF/LGBM fit via sample_weight. This reduces domination by large series.

items.title: Quantile-loss / Huber objective
items.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='huber' (alpha 1.0 on standardized y) to reduce the effect of noisy outliers. Use descriptors plus counts.

items.title: Morgan SVD compression
items.spec: Reduce the count Morgan matrix with TruncatedSVD (100 components, fit on train plus test smiles features, which is unsupervised). Concatenate with descriptors and feed LightGBM.

items.title: Count Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace binary Morgan bits with count fingerprints: use gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy (radius 2, 2048 bits) in featurize. Keep the random forest unchanged.

items.title: RDKit 2D descriptors
items.spec: Add all RDKit Descriptors.descList values (about 200) as features, with nan_to_num and clipping to ±1e6. Train the random forest on descriptors only. Descriptors such as logP, TPSA and MW matter for clearance.

items.title: Descriptors plus counts concat
items.spec: Concatenate RDKit descriptors with Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits) and train the RF on the combined matrix. Set max_features=0.2.

items.title: LightGBM on descriptors+counts
items.spec: Swap the model for LGBMRegressor (n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on descriptors + Morgan counts.

items.title: CatBoost regressor
items.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.03, l2_leaf_reg=5, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on RDKit descriptors + count Morgan features.

items.title: Rank-transform target
items.spec: Convert train_y to normalized ranks (scipy.stats.rankdata/len) before fitting. The metric is Spearman, so rank targets reduce outlier influence. Predictions are used as they are.

items.title: ExtraTrees swap
items.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor (n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=-1) on the same features.

items.title: RF min_samples_leaf and more trees
items.spec: Set N_TREES=800, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=2, MAX_FEATURES=0.2 to smooth predictions for unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Larger radius, feature Morgan
items.spec: Use Morgan radius 3 with 4096-bit counts, and add the chirality flag off. Check whether bigger substructures help.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion counts
items.spec: Add count fingerprints from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator (fpSize 2048) and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator (fpSize 1024). Concatenate them with Morgan and fit the RF.

items.title: MACCS keys add-on
items.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the Morgan bits and fit the RF.

items.title: Feature-based Morgan (FCFP)
items.spec: Use Morgan with the atom invariants generator GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 2048 counts. Concatenate it with ECFP counts.

items.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel
items.spec: Use SVR with a precomputed Tanimoto (min/max) kernel on Morgan count fingerprints (C=5, epsilon=0.1). Compute the kernel in numpy: sum(min)/sum(max) over feature pairs, or the binary version via dot products.

items.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto
items.spec: Use KernelRidge with a precomputed binary Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits (alpha=1.0) on the rank-transformed target. Predict with the test-vs-train kernel.

items.title: Gaussian process Tanimoto
items.spec: Implement a GP regression by hand in numpy: Tanimoto kernel on count fingerprints, noise 0.3, standardized y. Solve with Cholesky and predict the posterior mean.

items.title: RF + LGBM + SVR rank-average ensemble
items.spec: Fit an RF, a LightGBM and a Tanimoto SVR. Rank-normalize each model's predictions on the test set and average them with equal weights.

items.title: Multi-seed bagging
items.spec: Train 5 models with seeds seed..seed+4, each with a different subsample (80% of molecules), and average the predictions to cut variance.

items.title: XGBoost on descriptors
items.spec: Use XGBRegressor(n_estimators=600, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=3, reg_lambda=5, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) on RDKit descriptors only.

items.title: Pseudo-Huber / MAE objective
items.spec: Use a robust loss in LightGBM (objective='huber', alpha=1.0) on descriptors plus counts to limit the effect of noisy clearance outliers.

items.title: Variance filter and feature selection
items.spec: Drop fingerprint bits that are on in fewer than 5 training molecules, and drop near-constant descriptors, before fitting the RF. This reduces noise features.

items.title: Scaffold-aware sample weights
items.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and weight it by 1/sqrt(scaffold group size). Pass the weights as sample_weight to the model so big series don't dominate.

items.title: Log-transform target
items.spec: If y is positive and skewed, fit on log1p(y - min(y) + 1e-3) and invert the transform. Otherwise standardize y. Fit the RF on the result.

items.title: Small MLP on descriptors
items.spec: Use sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden 256,64, alpha=1e-2, early_stopping, max_iter=500) on QuantileTransformer-scaled descriptors. Average 5 seeds.

items.title: PCA/SVD of fingerprint plus descriptors
items.spec: Compute TruncatedSVD (50 components) on Morgan counts, concatenate it with descriptors, and fit the GBM or RF. Fit the SVD on train+test smiles, which is unsupervised.

items.title: Crippen/EState fragment counts
items.spec: Add rdkit.Chem.Fragments fr_* counts and the EState VSA descriptors (EState_VSA, VSA_EstateN, SlogP_VSA, SMR_VSA) as features alongside the Morgan bits, then fit the RF.

items.title: Stacking with ridge
items.spec: Build out-of-fold predictions inside fit_predict (5-fold KFold) from the RF, LGBM and SVR. Fit a non-negative linear regression on them and use it to blend the test predictions.

items.title: Strong LightGBM regularization
items.spec: LightGBM with extra_trees=True, num_leaves=8, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=800, lambda_l2=10, colsample_bytree=0.2, min_child_samples=15. Features are descriptors plus counts.

items.title: Mordred-like 3D-free shape descriptors
items.spec: Add rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors features: BCUT2D, AUTOCORR2D, and CalcNumAmideBonds, plus the Chi and Kappa indices. Concatenate them with the existing descriptors and fit LightGBM.

items.title: Stereo-free salt-stripped standardization
items.spec: Before featurizing, keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), neutralize charges with Uncharger, and canonicalize. This removes salt noise in the features.

items.title: Random-subspace RF on mixed views
items.spec: Train 3 RFs separately on Morgan counts, on descriptors and on atom-pair counts. Average the predictions. This diversifies the views.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints
items.spec: Replace the binary Morgan bit vector with a count vector: use rdFingerprintGenerator's GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with the same radius 2 and 2048 size, keeping the RandomForestRegressor unchanged. Counts keep how often each substructure occurs, which can matter for lipophilicity-driven clearance.

items.title: Append RDKit 2D descriptors to fingerprints
items.spec: In featurize, compute all RDKit Descriptors.descList values for each molecule (wrap each call in try/except and set failures to NaN). Replace NaN and inf with 0, clip each column to its 1st and 99th training percentiles, and horizontally concatenate with the Morgan bits. Keep the RF unchanged. Fit the clip bounds on the training set only.

items.title: Small physicochemical descriptor set only
items.spec: Drop the fingerprints and use a compact set of about 15 interpretable descriptors: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, FractionCSP3, RingCount, HeavyAtomCount, and counts of carboxylic acids, basic amines, and quaternary or formal charges (via SMARTS). Fit the same RandomForestRegressor on this matrix. Low-dimensional physchem often generalizes better to unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Append MACCS structural keys
items.spec: Concatenate the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a numpy array) to the existing 2048-bit Morgan vector. Leave the RandomForestRegressor and its settings unchanged. MACCS keys encode predefined functional groups that complement hashed circular fingerprints.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints
items.spec: Add hashed atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 1024 bits each, count vectors) and concatenate them with the Morgan features. Keep the RF unchanged. These capture longer-range topology than radius-2 circular environments.

items.title: Feature-invariant Morgan (FCFP-style)
items.spec: Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with an atom invariant generator (AllChem.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen or rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen) so the bits encode pharmacophore-like classes (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) instead of exact atom types. Use radius 2 and 2048 bits with the RF unchanged.

items.title: Rank-transform the training target
items.spec: Before fitting, convert train_y to its within-training ranks scaled to [0, 1] (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n). Fit the RF on these ranks, then return the predictions. Since the metric is Spearman correlation, training on ranks aligns the objective with the score and removes the influence of extreme clearance values.

items.title: Log-transform the training target
items.spec: Fit the model on a log-scale target: y' = sign(y) * log1p(|y|) computed from train_y, and return predictions as-is (monotone transforms preserve Spearman rank). Clearance values are typically right-skewed, so this compresses the high tail that would otherwise dominate squared-error splits.

items.title: Winsorize outlier training targets
items.spec: Clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles before fitting, using only the training values. The model then sees a bounded target and is less distorted by measurement outliers. Keep the RF and features unchanged. Predictions are returned unchanged.

items.title: Drop sparse fingerprint bits
items.spec: After featurizing the training set, keep only the fingerprint columns that are set in at least 3 training molecules, and apply the same column mask to test features. This removes noisy, rarely-seen bits that can mislead RF splits and reduces dimensionality and training time.

items.title: LightGBM gradient boosting model
items.spec: Replace the RF with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor on the Morgan features: n_estimators 600, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Boosting often beats bagged trees on small tabular fingerprint problems.

items.title: CatBoost regressor
items.spec: Replace the RF with catboost.CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, 800 iterations, loss RMSE, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on the Morgan bits. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees tend to be strong with small, noisy datasets.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints, i.e. K = (A dot B) / (|A| + |B| - A dot B), for train-train and test-train pairs. Fit sklearn.svm.SVR with kernel='precomputed' (C=5, epsilon=0.05) on the train-train matrix and predict from the test-train matrix. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecules.

items.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour regression
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity between test and training Morgan fingerprints. For each test molecule, take the k=10 most similar training molecules and return the similarity-weighted mean of their targets, with weights = similarity^3. This is a simple nonparametric baseline that works well when test molecules have close analogues in training.

items.title: Ensemble of small MLPs on standardized features
items.spec: Build the Morgan plus RDKit-descriptor feature matrix, standardize it with training-set mean and std, and train 5 sklearn MLPRegressor models (hidden_layer_sizes (256, 64), alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 300, random_state from seed plus index). Average their predictions. Ensembling several seeds reduces variance on small data.

items.title: Adam with strong L2 for the MLP
items.spec: Within the MLP setup (sklearn MLPRegressor with solver='adam'), set learning_rate_init=1e-3, alpha=1e-1 (strong L2 weight decay), batch_size=32, and early_stopping=True with n_iter_no_change=20. Stronger weight decay plus small mini-batches encourage smoother fits that generalize better across scaffolds.

items.title: Cosine learning-rate decay for the MLP
items.spec: Train the MLP with solver='sgd' or 'adam' using a manual outer loop: call partial_fit for a fixed number of epochs (e.g. 200) and set the learning rate each epoch with cosine annealing from 1e-3 down to 1e-5 (use the solver's learning_rate_init attribute updated before each partial_fit). Keep the 5-model seed ensemble from the MLP idea. The schedule helps the optimizer settle into a flatter minimum.

items.title: LightGBM with early stopping on an inner holdout
items.spec: Set aside 15 percent of the training molecules, stratified by target quantile, as an inner validation set. Train LGBMRegressor (learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, colsample_bytree 0.3, up to 2000 trees) with eval_set and early_stopping(100). Then refit on all training molecules using the best iteration count scaled by 1.1. Automatic boosting-round selection avoids both under- and over-fitting.

items.title: Larger RF leaves for smoother ranking
items.spec: Set RandomForestRegressor min_samples_leaf to 3 instead of 1 and keep the other settings. Larger leaves average more molecules per prediction, which reduces variance and gives less jagged predictions across similar molecules. Test whether this helps when test scaffolds are unseen.

items.title: RF with sqrt feature subsampling
items.spec: Set RandomForestRegressor max_features='sqrt' instead of 0.3 (which gives about 45 features per split on 2048 bits, versus about 45 at 'sqrt' 2048 bits, close to 0.02). Keep the other settings. Sparse binary fingerprints usually suit a smaller per-split feature fraction, which decorrelates trees more strongly.

items.title: RF with bootstrap subsampling of molecules
items.spec: Set RandomForestRegressor bootstrap=True and max_samples=0.5, so each tree is fit on a random half of the training molecules. This adds diversity between trees and makes each tree cheaper, which allows more trees in the same budget. Keep the other settings.

items.title: Seed-bagged LightGBM with row subsampling
items.spec: Train 5 LGBMRegressor models with different random_state values (from seed), each on a random 80 percent subsample of rows (subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.3), and average their predictions. Averaging across subsampled datasets reduces the variance of boosting, which is high on small data.

items.title: Huber objective for LightGBM
items.spec: Use LGBMRegressor with objective='huber' and alpha=1.0 (applied to the training targets after standardizing them to zero mean and unit variance using training statistics). Huber loss is less sensitive to large clearance values than squared error, which can reduce the influence of noisy measurements on the learned ranking.

items.title: Rank-average ensemble of RF, LightGBM and SVR
items.spec: Fit the RF on Morgan bits, LightGBM on Morgan plus descriptor features, and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by test count) and return the unweighted mean of the three rank vectors. Rank averaging combines models with different scales without tuning weights.

items.title: Stacking with out-of-fold meta-learner
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run an inner 5-fold KFold on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from the RF (Morgan bits), a Tanimoto kNN, and a ridge model on descriptors. Fit a RidgeCV meta-learner on these out-of-fold predictions and apply it to the test-set predictions of the three base models refit on all training data. Stacking learns how to weight complementary models.

items.title: Inner scaffold-grouped tuning of RF settings
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, evaluate a small grid of RF settings (max_features in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5} and min_samples_leaf in {1, 3, 5}) with an inner GroupKFold (3 folds) where groups are Murcko scaffold SMILES computed from the training molecules. Choose the setting with the highest inner Spearman correlation and refit on all training data. Scaffold grouping keeps the tuning honest for unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Inverse-scaffold-frequency sample weights
items.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and set sample_weight to 1 divided by the number of training molecules sharing that scaffold, normalized to mean 1. Pass these weights to RandomForestRegressor.fit. This prevents large scaffold families from dominating the trees and encourages coverage of the chemical space.

items.title: Salt stripping and neutralization before featurization
items.spec: In featurize, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest covalent fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), and neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Fall back to the original molecule if parsing fails. Use the cleaned molecules for the Morgan fingerprint and the RF. Standardizing the structures removes counterion noise that would otherwise appear as spurious features.

items.title: Multi-radius Morgan RF ensemble
items.spec: Train three RandomForestRegressor models, each on Morgan fingerprints of radius 1, 2 and 3 (2048 bits each, with n_estimators 200 per model, random_state from seed plus index). Average their test predictions. Different radii capture local versus wider environments, and averaging the three models hedges against any one radius being a poor fit.

items.title: Chirality and ring-membership aware Morgan bits
items.spec: Generate Morgan fingerprints with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048) using the atom-invariant and bond options that include chirality (includeChirality=True) and ring membership (includeRingMembership is on by default for the atom environment). Keep the RF unchanged. Stereochemistry and ring context can distinguish metabolically different isomers that plain Morgan bits merge.

items.title: Log-transform the target
items.spec: In fit_predict, train on np.log1p of train_y (clip at 0 first if any values are negative, using log1p(y - min(y) + 1) if needed), then invert with expm1 on the predictions before returning. Keep the RandomForestRegressor and featurization unchanged. Spearman is rank-based, so this only changes how the trees split on skewed clearance values.

items.title: Rank-normal target transform
items.spec: Replace train_y with normal scores: rank the training targets (scipy.stats.rankdata, average ties), map ranks to (rank - 0.5) / n, then apply scipy.stats.norm.ppf. Fit the same RandomForestRegressor on these scores and return its test predictions directly. Only the training target changes; the model and features stay the same.

items.title: Append RDKit 2D descriptor block
items.spec: Compute the full RDKit descriptor set with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors for each molecule (replace NaN and inf with 0, clip values to ±1e6). Hstack these float descriptors with the 2048 Morgan bits before fitting the RandomForestRegressor. Use the same column order for train and test, computed from the same list of descriptor names.

items.title: Curated physicochemical descriptor block
items.spec: Build a small descriptor vector per molecule: molecular weight, Crippen MolLogP, TPSA, H-bond donors, H-bond acceptors, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, Fsp3, heavy atom count, and formal charge count. Concatenate it with the Morgan bits and fit the same random forest. Clearance is driven largely by lipophilicity and size, so these few columns should help the trees split on them directly.

items.title: Morgan count fingerprints instead of bits
items.spec: Replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with the count variant (gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) at radius 2 and 2048 length. Each feature becomes the number of times a substructure occurs, not a 0/1 flag. Keep the random forest unchanged, so the only difference is the feature type.

items.title: Larger radius and hashed size
items.spec: Set RADIUS to 3 and N_BITS to 4096 for the Morgan generator, keeping the same random forest. Larger radius captures bigger substructure contexts and more bits reduce hash collisions. Watch the runtime; 15 fits must stay within the 10 minute limit.

items.title: FCFP feature-invariant Morgan appended
items.spec: Build a second Morgan generator with useFeatures=True (pharmacophoric invariants, FCFP-style) at radius 2 and 1024 bits. Concatenate it with the standard ECFP bits (2048) and fit the same random forest. The two representations capture different aspects of the chemistry, so the trees can use both.

items.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints
items.spec: Add rdFingerprintGenerator atom-pair and topological-torsion generators with count outputs (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), each folded to 1024 bits. Concatenate them with the Morgan bits and fit the same random forest. These encode longer-range atom environments than ECFP.

items.title: MACCS keys appended
items.spec: Compute MACCS structural keys with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule (166 bits) and hstack them onto the Morgan features before fitting the random forest. MACCS keys are a fixed, interpretable substructure dictionary that often complements hashed fingerprints on small datasets.

items.title: Salt stripping and neutralization before featurizing
items.spec: In featurize, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest covalent fragment (rdkit.Chem.SaltRemover or sorting fragments by heavy atom count from Chem.GetMolFrags), and neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. If a molecule still fails to parse, fall back to a zero vector. The same preprocessing applies to train and test molecules.

items.title: ExtraTrees instead of random forest
items.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor with the same n_estimators, max_features, min_samples_leaf, n_jobs=-1, and random_state=seed. Extra-trees use random split thresholds and are often smoother on small noisy datasets, which may help rank correlation on unseen scaffolds.

items.title: LightGBM regressor on fingerprints and descriptors
items.spec: Replace the random forest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Feed it the same Morgan bits. Gradient boosting often outperforms bagged trees on tabular targets.

items.title: CatBoost regressor
items.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostRegressor with iterations=800, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, l2_leaf_reg=3, loss_function='RMSE', random_seed=seed, verbose=False, thread_count=8, on the Morgan bits. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees regularize well on small datasets with many sparse binary features.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression
items.spec: Compute a MinMax (Tanimoto-generalized) kernel on count Morgan fingerprints: K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)) for all train-train and test-train pairs with numpy broadcasting in chunks. Fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, epsilon=0.1) on the train kernel and predict from the test-train kernel. Similarity kernels are a strong default for molecular property prediction.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel ridge regression
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto kernel on binary Morgan fingerprints (K = |A∩B| / |A∪B|, computed by matrix products). Solve the kernel ridge system (K_train + alpha*I) w = y_centered with alpha around 0.5 and predict test values as K_test w plus the training mean. This is a closed-form Gaussian-process-like regressor, no iterative training.

items.title: Similarity-weighted kNN regression
items.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarities between test and train binary Morgan fingerprints. For each test molecule, take the k=10 most similar training molecules and average their targets weighted by similarity raised to the power 3. Fall back to the global training mean if the best similarity is zero. This is a simple nonparametric baseline that exploits nearest-neighbor chemistry.

items.title: Small MLP with dropout and weight decay
items.spec: Train a torch-free MLP is not available, so use sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor on log1p count Morgan features with hidden_layer_sizes=(256,128), alpha=1e-2 (L2 weight decay), learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.15, max_iter=300, random_state=seed. Standardize the targets before fitting and invert after prediction.

items.title: Rank-averaged ensemble of RF, LightGBM and Tanimoto SVR
items.spec: Fit three models on the same training fold: the random forest, a LightGBM regressor on Morgan bits, and the Tanimoto-kernel SVR. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n) and average them with equal weights. Return the averaged rank score. Averaging diverse model families usually lifts rank correlation.

items.title: Stacked blend with out-of-fold ridge weights
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold KFold on the training molecules (shuffle, random_state=seed) to produce out-of-fold predictions from a random forest and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR. Fit a non-negative linear regression (sklearn.linear_model.LinearRegression(positive=True)) on these out-of-fold predictions to find blend weights. Then refit both base models on all training data and return the weighted sum of their test predictions.

items.title: Larger forest with sqrt feature sampling
items.spec: Set N_TREES to 1000 and MAX_FEATURES to 'sqrt' in the random forest. The sqrt rule decorrelates trees more strongly on sparse binary fingerprints than a 0.3 fraction, and the extra trees reduce variance. Keep min_samples_leaf unchanged.

items.title: Random forest with larger leaves
items.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 4 in the random forest, keeping other settings the same. Larger leaves smooth predictions across neighboring molecules, reducing overfitting to noisy measurements from unseen scaffolds.

items.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits
items.spec: After featurizing the training fold, compute the fraction of training molecules having each Morgan bit. Keep only bits present in at least 2 percent and at most 98 percent of training molecules, and apply the same column mask to the test features. Fitting then ignores bits that are almost constant or too rare to generalize across scaffolds.

items.title: Winsorize training targets
items.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles (numpy.percentile). Fit the random forest on the clipped values and return predictions as usual. Extreme clearance values from measurement noise can otherwise pull tree leaves toward outliers.

items.title: Bootstrap subsampling in the random forest
items.spec: Set bootstrap=True and max_samples=0.5 in RandomForestRegressor. Each tree sees only half the training molecules, which decorrelates trees and adds regularization. Use more trees (500) to compensate for the higher per-tree variance.

items.title: Stochastic LightGBM with row and column subsampling
items.spec: Use LightGBM with subsample=0.6 and subsample_freq=1 and colsample_bytree=0.4, with num_leaves=15 and learning_rate=0.05 and n_estimators=300. Random row and feature subsets per boosting round act as mini-batches and reduce overfitting. Seed with random_state=seed.

items.title: Learning-rate decay schedule for boosting
items.spec: Train a LightGBM regressor with 600 boosting rounds and a learning rate that decays from 0.1 to 0.01 using the callback lightgbm.reset_parameter(learning_rate=lambda i: 0.1 * (0.1 ** (i / 600))). Keep num_leaves=15 and subsample=0.8. The decaying step size gives coarse early fits and finer late refinements.

items.title: Early stopping with an inner validation split
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out 15 percent of the training molecules (sklearn train_test_split with random_state=seed). Train LightGBM with n_estimators up to 2000, learning_rate=0.03, and early_stopping(stopping_rounds=50) on the held-out part, recording best_iteration. Refit on all training molecules with best_iteration times 1.1 rounds and predict the test molecules.

items.title: Huber loss for robust boosting
items.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='huber' and alpha=1.0 applied to standardized targets (subtract mean, divide by std of train_y), with num_leaves=15, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=500, subsample=0.8. Huber loss limits the gradient from outlying clearance measurements, which can otherwise dominate squared-error fits.

items.title: Pairwise ranking objective in LightGBM
items.spec: Train lightgbm.LGBMRanker with objective='lambdarank' on Morgan bits. Build integer relevance labels by binning train_y into 10 quantile levels (np.digitize with np.quantile edges), use one query group containing all training molecules, set n_estimators=400 and learning_rate=0.05. Return the ranker's scores as predictions, since Spearman rewards correct ordering.

items.title: Two-stage residual boosting
items.spec: First fit the random forest on Morgan bits and get out-of-bag predictions (oob_prediction_ with oob_score=True, bootstrap=True). Compute residuals on the training molecules as train_y minus the OOB predictions. Then fit a LightGBM regressor (num_leaves=15, learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=300) on the Morgan bits plus the RF OOB prediction as an extra column to predict the residuals. The final prediction is the RF test prediction plus the LightGBM residual prediction for the test molecules, with the RF test prediction as the extra column.

items.title: Log-transform the target
items.spec: Before fitting, replace train_y with log10 of the values (use log10(clip(y, min positive value / 10, None)) if any y is <= 0). Fit the same model on the transformed target and return its raw predictions. Clearance is roughly log-normal, so a log target should give smoother splits. Spearman is rank-based, so no back-transform is needed.

items.title: Normal-score (rank-Gaussian) target
items.spec: Replace train_y with its normal scores: rank each training value, divide by (n+1), and apply scipy.stats.norm.ppf. Fit the model on these scores and return its predictions for the test molecules. This makes the target less sensitive to outliers and matches the rank-based metric. No inverse transform is needed.

items.title: Winsorize extreme training targets
items.spec: Clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles before fitting, leaving test predictions unchanged. This stops a few very high or very low clearance values from dominating the squared-error splits. Use np.percentile on train_y only, so the procedure never sees test labels.

items.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprint
items.spec: Replace the binary Morgan featurizer with the count version: gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) at radius 2 and 2048 bits. Counts keep how many times each substructure occurs, which often helps for property regression. Keep the random forest and all other settings unchanged.

items.title: Radius-3 chiral Morgan fingerprint
items.spec: Use Morgan radius 3 with 2048 bits and useChirality=True in rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator. Larger radius captures bigger local environments, and chirality separates stereoisomers that may have different metabolic rates. Keep the random forest unchanged.

items.title: Add RDKit physchem descriptors
items.spec: Compute all RDKit 2D descriptors with rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors for every molecule. Replace NaN and infinite values with 0 and clip each column to its training 1st and 99th percentiles. Concatenate these roughly 200 values with the Morgan bits and fit the random forest on the combined matrix. Lipophilicity and polarity descriptors are known to drive hepatic clearance.

items.title: MACCS keys fingerprint
items.spec: Featurize each molecule with rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys (167 bits) and use it in place of the Morgan bits. MACCS keys encode broad functional-group presence, which may generalize better across unseen scaffolds. Keep the random forest unchanged.

items.title: Hashed atom-pair count fingerprint
items.spec: Replace the Morgan featurizer with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=2048) and use GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Atom pairs encode topological distances between atoms and are less tied to exact ring environments, so they may transfer across scaffolds. Keep the random forest unchanged.

items.title: Topological torsion count fingerprint
items.spec: Featurize molecules with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=2048) and GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy. Torsion paths describe local flexibility and chain shape, which may relate to enzyme access. Keep the random forest unchanged.

items.title: Feature-invariant (FCFP-like) Morgan
items.spec: Build a Morgan generator that uses pharmacophoric atom invariants: rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Atoms are then grouped by donor, acceptor, aromatic, and similar roles instead of element identity, which gives more generalizable bits across scaffolds. Keep the random forest unchanged.

items.title: Small physchem-only gradient boosting model
items.spec: Ignore fingerprints. Compute about 10 interpretable descriptors per molecule (Crippen logP, TPSA, molecular weight, H-bond donors and acceptors, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, fraction sp3, formal charge, heavy atom count). Fit sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.03, subsample=0.8, random_state=seed). Low-dimensional models can generalize better to unseen skeletons.

items.title: LightGBM on fingerprints and descriptors
items.spec: Build the features as Morgan counts (radius 2, 2048 bits) concatenated with the RDKit 2D descriptors. Fit lightgbm.LGBMRegressor(n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Gradient boosting often beats random forests on tabular fingerprint features.

items.title: CatBoost on fingerprints and descriptors
items.spec: Use the same concatenated Morgan counts and RDKit descriptors as the LightGBM idea. Fit catboost.CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, learning_rate=0.03, depth=6, l2_leaf_reg=5, random_seed=seed, verbose=False, thread_count=8). CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees tend to regularize well on small datasets.

items.title: XGBoost regressor with row and column subsampling
items.spec: Use the Morgan count plus descriptor matrix. Fit xgboost.XGBRegressor(n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.03, max_depth=4, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.4, min_child_weight=3, reg_lambda=2, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, tree_method='hist'). The depth cap and subsampling limit overfitting to individual scaffolds.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression
items.spec: Compute the binary Morgan (radius 2, 2048 bits) Tanimoto similarity matrix: K = (A·B) / (|A| + |B| - A·B) using numpy dot products. Fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.05) on the training Gram matrix and predict with the test-by-train Tanimoto matrix. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecular fingerprints.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel ridge regression
items.spec: Build the Tanimoto Gram matrix on binary Morgan bits as in the SVR idea. Solve for dual coefficients with (K + alpha I) c = y_centered, using alpha=0.5 and np.linalg.solve. Predict test values as K_test @ c plus the training mean. This closed-form kernel model is deterministic and has a single regularization knob.

items.title: Distance-weighted Tanimoto kNN
items.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules on binary Morgan bits. For each test molecule keep the k=8 most similar training molecules and predict the similarity-weighted average of their targets, with weights = similarity raised to the power 3. Nearest-neighbour averaging is a strong baseline for activity-like tasks.

items.title: Extra-trees regressor
items.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=500, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) on the same Morgan bits. Random split thresholds add more smoothing, which can help when test skeletons differ from training skeletons.

items.title: Stronger random forest regularization
items.spec: Keep the random forest on Morgan bits but set min_samples_leaf=3, max_features='sqrt', and max_depth=20. Larger leaves and shallower trees reduce variance from overfit small clusters of similar molecules. Everything else stays the same.

items.title: Ridge regression on standardized descriptors
items.spec: Use the RDKit 2D descriptors, replacing NaN and inf with 0, clipping to training percentiles, and standardizing with training means and stds. Fit sklearn.linear_model.RidgeCV(alphas=np.logspace(-2, 3, 20)) on the standardized matrix. A linear physchem model gives a diverse, low-variance component for ensembling.

items.title: MLP on fingerprints with L2 and early stopping
items.spec: Fit sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 64), alpha=1e-2, learning_rate_init=1e-3, max_iter=500, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, random_state=seed) on the Morgan bits after standardizing the target to zero mean and unit variance. Early stopping and L2 decay keep the network from memorizing the training scaffolds.

items.title: Rank-averaged ensemble of RF, LightGBM and SVR
items.spec: Train the random forest on Morgan bits, a LightGBM regressor on Morgan counts plus descriptors, and the Tanimoto SVR. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks, average the three rank vectors with equal weights, and return the average. Rank averaging keeps models with different output scales from dominating and suits the Spearman metric.

items.title: Stacked ensemble with ridge meta-learner
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold KFold on the training set (shuffle=True, random_state=seed). For each fold, fit the base models (random forest, LightGBM, Tanimoto SVR) on the other folds and record out-of-fold predictions. Fit a non-negative linear regression on the stacked out-of-fold prediction matrix, then refit the base models on all training data and combine their test predictions with the learned weights.

items.title: Inner-CV selection of random forest max_features
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 3-fold GroupKFold-like split on the training set (or plain KFold with shuffle and seed) and score candidate max_features values in {0.05, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5} by Spearman correlation of out-of-fold predictions. Refit the random forest on all training data with the best value and predict the test set. This lets the data choose capacity rather than fixing it by hand.

items.title: Row and column subsampling in gradient boosting
items.spec: In a sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor or LightGBM model on Morgan counts plus descriptors, use row subsampling of 0.6 per tree and column subsampling of 0.3 per tree, with n_estimators=400 and learning_rate=0.05. Stochastic boosting reduces correlated errors among trees and tends to generalize better on small datasets.

items.title: Bagged small trees on bootstrap subsamples
items.spec: Draw 20 bootstrap-like subsamples of 70 percent of the training rows without replacement, using numpy's RandomState(seed + i). For each subsample fit a DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features=0.3) on Morgan bits, and average the 20 test predictions. This is a bagging-style ensemble with explicit control over the row sampling fraction.

items.title: Internal early stopping for boosting rounds
items.spec: Hold out 10 percent of the training rows (chosen with the seed) as an internal validation set. Fit a LightGBM regressor with a large n_estimators=2000, learning_rate=0.03, and early_stopping_rounds=100 on that split, then refit on all training rows using the best iteration count found. Early stopping chooses the number of rounds from the data instead of a fixed guess.

items.title: Two-stage learning-rate schedule for boosting
items.spec: Fit a LightGBM or XGBoost model with a coarse shrinkage of 0.1 for the first 200 trees, then continue training with 0.01 for another 600 trees. In LightGBM, use the init_model argument or train with lgb.train and a learning-rate callback that switches rates at iteration 200. Larger early steps followed by small refinement steps can reach a better fit with fewer total trees.

items.title: Huber loss for robust gradient boosting
items.spec: Train a LightGBM regressor with objective='huber' and alpha=1.0 on the standardized target, using Morgan counts plus descriptors as features. Huber loss limits the influence of outlying clearance values, which can be noisy in measured data, while keeping squared-error behaviour for typical points. Predict in the same standardized units.

items.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weights
items.spec: Compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) of every training molecule. Give each training row weight 1 / sqrt(count of its scaffold) and pass these as sample_weight to the random forest fit. Large scaffold families then do not dominate the trees, which better matches unseen-skeleton testing. Test predictions use the same model.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pairwise distance gradients, wall constraints, r>=0) to the SLSQP call. This removes finite-difference cost so many more restarts or iterations fit in the time budget.

items.title: Increase MAX_ITER and polish
items.spec: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000 for SLSQP with ftol=1e-12 so each run converges fully to a local optimum rather than being cut at 200 iterations. Only valid with the analytic Jacobian, otherwise too slow.

items.title: Two-stage: short screening then polish
items.spec: Run many restarts with maxiter=60, keep the top 3 by sum of radii (after repair), then continue SLSQP from those with maxiter=500 and keep the best. Allocates time to promising basins.

items.title: Structured initialisation: jittered grid
items.spec: Initialise centres on a 5x5 grid plus one extra point (or a 6x5 grid with 4 random points removed) with Gaussian jitter of sd 0.03, and radii 0.08. Known good packings are near-hexagonal/grid-like so starts are closer to good basins.

items.title: Hex-lattice initialisation
items.spec: Initialise centres from a hexagonal lattice with rows of 5,5,6,5,5 (or 6,5,5,5,5) points scaled into the square, with small random jitter and random row-orientation flips. Radii start at 0.09.

items.title: Basin hopping from best
items.spec: After an initial batch of restarts, repeatedly perturb the best solution (move 1-3 random circles to random spots or add Gaussian noise sd 0.02 to all centres), re-run SLSQP, and accept if improved. Replaces pure random restarts for the remaining time.

items.title: Relocate smallest circle perturbation
items.spec: In the basin hopping loop, perturb by removing the smallest-radius circle and re-inserting at the largest empty spot (found from random sample points maximizing distance to the other circles and walls), then re-optimize.

items.title: Use more of the time budget
items.spec: Set TIME_FRACTION to 0.9 and make the loop stop based on estimated duration of the last run so the final run does not overshoot; keep the repair cheap. Yields more restarts.

items.title: Better repair via exact scaling
items.spec: Replace the repair with an iterative pass: clip radii to walls, then for every overlapping pair shrink both proportionally until max overlap <= 0, looping up to 200 times, and use SHRINK=1e-11 plus a final exact check. Loses less radius than the current 50-iteration one with SHRINK 1e-9.

items.title: LP radius refinement
items.spec: After SLSQP, fix the centres and solve an LP with scipy linprog maximizing sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0. This gives the exact optimal valid radii for those centres, replacing the heuristic repair.

items.title: Alternate LP and centre moves
items.spec: Iterate: LP for radii at fixed centres, then a sequential linearised step for centres via LP with trust region 0.02 on centre displacement (linearised distance constraints). Repeat until converged, as a polish after SLSQP.

items.title: Variable initial radii
items.spec: Draw initial radii randomly from uniform(0.03,0.12) per circle instead of constant 0.05, to encourage a diverse mix of large and small circles as in the best packings.

items.title: Wider init range
items.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.05 so centres can start near walls, since optimal packings place many circles touching the boundary.

items.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation
items.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few hundred steps of L-BFGS-B on a smooth penalty objective -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2) with mu increasing from 10 to 1000, then pass the result to SLSQP. Gives feasible-ish starts and fewer SLSQP iterations.

items.title: Sparse neighbour constraints
items.spec: In SLSQP only include pair constraints for pairs whose initial distance is below e.g. 0.4, re-checking and adding violated pairs in a follow-up run. Reduces the 325-pair constraint count and speeds each iteration.

items.title: Trust-constr alternative
items.spec: Use scipy trust-constr with analytic Jacobian and sparse constraints for the polish stage of the top candidates instead of SLSQP, to see whether it converges to tighter optima.

items.title: Symmetry-seeded starts
items.spec: Generate half the starts by sampling 13 circles in half the square and mirroring about x=0.5 (or a diagonal) with jitter, then optimize without symmetry constraints. Best-known packings tend to be near-symmetric.

items.title: Constraint slack safety margin
items.spec: Require pair constraints d - ri - rj >= 1e-12 and wall margins 1e-12 inside SLSQP so the repair needs nearly no shrink, and use SHRINK=1e-12 in repair.

items.title: Ensemble of init types
items.spec: Cycle starts between uniform random, jittered grid, and hex lattice by iteration index mod 3, and keep running per-type best stats; after 10 s allocate remaining restarts to the type with the best average.

items.title: Elite pool recombination
items.spec: Maintain a pool of the top 5 packings. Create children by taking circles from the left half of one parent and right half of another (resolve count to n by dropping or adding at random), then optimize with SLSQP.

items.title: Sort-by-radius radius growth start
items.spec: Start with radii=0.01 for all circles and grow them via a first SLSQP run with maxiter=30, then re-run with the full limit. Gradual growth avoids early bad jams.

items.title: Objective smoothing with distance squared
items.spec: Write pair constraints as squared form (dx²+dy²) - (ri+rj)² >= 0 with analytic Jacobian, avoiding sqrt and non-differentiability at zero distance. Faster and more stable for SLSQP.

items.title: Bounds instead of wall constraints
items.spec: Move the wall and r>=0 constraints into SLSQP bounds: centre coordinates in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5], and keep wall constraints only as c-r>=0 forms, reducing the number of general constraints.

items.title: Early abort of poor runs
items.spec: Run SLSQP in chunks of 40 iterations via repeated minimize calls; after the second chunk abandon the run if the current sum of radii is below 97% of the best so far. Saves time for more restarts.

items.title: Simulated annealing on centres then SLSQP
items.spec: Do a short annealing with random single-circle moves under LP-free proxy (greedy radius estimate from nearest distances) for about 2000 steps, then feed to SLSQP. Provides better-distributed starts.

items.title: Perturb-and-reoptimise radii swap
items.spec: For the best solution, try swapping positions of pairs of circles with notably different radii, re-run short SLSQP, and accept improvements. Explores permutations of the size layout.

items.title: Lloyd-style centre spreading init
items.spec: Sample 26 random points, apply 10 Lloyd (centroid Voronoi) iterations using a dense random sample of the square, and use the result as centres with radii half the nearest-neighbour distance. Yields evenly spread starts.

items.title: Drop repair for LP-valid results
items.spec: If the LP radius refinement returns a result, skip the repair function entirely and only apply a tiny shrink 1e-12 followed by exact validation; fall back to repair if validation fails.

items.title: Final validity guard
items.spec: Before returning, verify exactly in double precision with numpy that all constraints hold with tolerance 1e-10; if not, shrink all radii by a factor of 1-1e-9 until valid. Guards against crashes from any new method.

items.title: Fewer circles of a tiny size bias
items.spec: Add a small random per-run weight vector w_i in [0.95,1.05] to the objective (-sum w_i r_i) for the first SLSQP run, then re-optimize with true weights. This breaks ties and diversifies basins.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radius entries, 0 on centres) and an analytic sparse-built dense Jacobian for the constraints (pair distances, wall constraints, r>=0) to SLSQP. This removes finite-difference cost (about 78 evaluations per gradient) and allows many more restarts and iterations in the same time.

items.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000 with analytic jac
items.spec: After adding analytic Jacobians, set MAX_ITER to 500-1000 so each SLSQP run converges fully instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Keep the repair step.

items.title: Basin hopping from the best solution
items.spec: After a few random restarts, spend the remaining time perturbing the best packing. Jitter all centres by gaussian noise with sd 0.02-0.05, set radii to 0.8 of their values, and re-run SLSQP warm-started. Accept if the sum of radii improves.

items.title: Swap-two-circles perturbation
items.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, perturb by swapping the positions of two circles with very different radii (the radii swap too), then re-optimize with SLSQP. This helps escape arrangements where the size layout is wrong.

items.title: Remove and reinsert smallest circle
items.spec: Perturbation move: delete the smallest circle and reinsert it at a random location or the largest void (the point among random samples with max distance to other circles and walls), with a small radius. Then re-run SLSQP from that start.

items.title: Hex-grid-like initialization
items.spec: Initialize centres on a jittered grid or hex lattice such as rows of 5,5,6,5,5 (26 circles), with noise sd 0.02 and radius 0.08, instead of uniform random. This starts close to the known good structure.

items.title: Jittered square-grid init 5x5+1
items.spec: Start from a 5x5 grid with spacing 0.2 plus one extra circle at a random location. Add jitter with sd 0.03 and set radii to 0.09. Randomize which cell is perturbed.

items.title: Larger initial radii variety
items.spec: Draw the initial radii from uniform(0.03, 0.12) per circle instead of a constant 0.05, so the optimizer sees varied size layouts, which suits the problem's mixed radii.

items.title: Two-stage: fixed radii penalty then SLSQP
items.spec: Stage 1 runs a cheap L-BFGS minimization of a penalty energy (negative sum of radii plus a large weight times squared overlap and wall violation), with the weight increasing 10x across 3 rounds. Stage 2 polishes with SLSQP. This provides better starting points at low cost.

items.title: Use TIME_FRACTION 0.9
items.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9. A single run is short, so there is a margin below the 30 s limit. Make sure the last restart cannot run past the budget, for example by checking the elapsed time against an estimated run duration.

items.title: Exact LP repair of radii
items.spec: After SLSQP, fix the centres and solve an LP with scipy linprog (HiGHS) for the radii that maximize their sum subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0. Subtract 1e-12 for safety. This is optimal for the given centres and better than the greedy shrink.

items.title: Polish best with tight tolerance
items.spec: At the end, take the best packing, run SLSQP again with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter 1000, then the LP repair. Keep the result only if it is valid and better.

items.title: Reduce constraint count via neighbor pruning
items.spec: In the polish stage, include only pair constraints for circles whose centre distance is below r_i+r_j+0.15. This shrinks the QP and speeds up SLSQP iterations. Verify the final packing with the full check.

items.title: Successive restarts with early abort
items.spec: Run SLSQP in short chunks of 40 iterations. After the first chunk, abandon runs whose sum of radii is below 90 percent of the best so far, and continue only promising runs to full convergence. This saves time on poor starts.

items.title: Symmetry-aware init: mirror
items.spec: Generate 13 random circles in the left half and mirror them across x=0.5 as the start (jittered a little). Symmetric starts often lead to good structured packings. Mix 50/50 with fully random restarts.

items.title: Squared-distance constraints
items.spec: Rewrite pair constraints as (dx²+dy²) - (ri+rj)² >= 0 which is smooth, with an easy Jacobian and no sqrt at the contact point. Combine with the analytic Jacobian to improve SLSQP robustness.

items.title: Variable-radius-aware noise annealing
items.spec: In basin hopping, make the perturbation sd cycle through [0.01, 0.03, 0.06] across iterations, or shrink it slowly over time. Use a larger sd at the start for exploration and a smaller one at the end for refinement.

items.title: Population of elites
items.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct packings. Each iteration picks one elite at random, perturbs and re-optimizes it, and replaces the worst elite if the result is better and distinct (by sum differing by more than 1e-6).

items.title: Boundary-biased init
items.spec: Place about 16 circles near the boundary, with centres within 0.1 of the walls, and the rest in the interior. Best packings of this problem have many circles on the walls, so this bias helps.

items.title: Radius-weighted jitter
items.spec: In perturbation, scale the noise on each centre by 1/(r_i+0.02) so small circles move more and big ones stay put. Then re-optimize with SLSQP.

items.title: Cheaper repair with safety margin only
items.spec: Since SLSQP output already satisfies the constraints to about 1e-9, replace the iterative greedy repair with a vectorized one-shot step: compute the max overlap and violation, then subtract that amount from all radii. Pairs that overlap by v need r reduced by v/2 each, and the walls are handled by the clip. Use a final exact check.

items.title: Initial solution via random sequential packing
items.spec: Generate starts by greedy placement: sample 200 random points, pick the one with the largest feasible radius given the placed circles and walls, repeat 26 times. Use these centres and radii as the SLSQP start.

items.title: Trust-constr alternative for polish
items.spec: Run scipy trust-constr as a final polish on the best SLSQP solution with analytic Jacobian and Hessian-free options. Keep the result if it is valid after LP repair and the sum is higher.

items.title: Lower INIT_LOW spread
items.spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.03, so the initial centres cover the full square including near the walls, as optimal packings put circles in the corners. Also try an initial radius of 0.07.

items.title: Corner seeding
items.spec: Force 4 circles to start in the four corners with radius 0.12, and place the rest uniformly. Corner circles are present in nearly all good packings.

items.title: Sort-and-relabel symmetry reduction
items.spec: Before each re-optimization in basin hopping, relabel the circles by sorted centre x coordinate. This keeps the SLSQP variable ordering consistent and helps cache the index arrays. It is a minor change that adds no extra logic.

items.title: Precompute index arrays once
items.spec: Move np.triu_indices and the constraint function out of _solve_once into module-level cached closures keyed by n, so they are not rebuilt on every restart. This slightly raises the number of restarts.

items.title: Shrink-and-regrow perturbation
items.spec: Perturbation: multiply all radii of the best packing by 0.7 and keep the centres, add noise sd 0.01, then run SLSQP. This lets circles slide through a looser configuration and regrow into a different contact graph.

items.title: Simulated-annealing acceptance in hopping
items.spec: In basin hopping, accept a worse result with probability exp(-(delta)/T), with T decaying from 0.01 to 0.0005 over the time budget. Always track the global best separately and return it.

items.title: Final validity guard
items.spec: At the end of solve, run an exact double-precision check, with pairwise distance minus sum of radii and wall margins, on the best result. If any violation exceeds 0, shrink all radii by the max violation plus 1e-12. If SHRINK is raised to 1e-11, the loss is negligible. This protects against crashes from the more aggressive methods.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pairwise distance gradients, wall constraints, r>=0) to SLSQP. This removes finite-difference cost (about 78 variables) and gives many more restarts or iterations in 24 s.

items.title: Increase MAX_ITER to 1000
items.spec: Set MAX_ITER = 1000 so SLSQP converges fully on each restart instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Keep the rest unchanged.

items.title: Basin hopping from best
items.spec: After a few random restarts, switch to perturbing the best solution: add gaussian noise (sd about 0.03) to the centres, set radii to 0.8 of the best, re-run SLSQP, and keep the result if it is better. Use the seeded rng.

items.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle
items.spec: Perturbation move: take the best packing, pick the smallest circle (or a random one) and move it to a random spot, or to the largest empty hole found by sampling points. Then re-run SLSQP from there and keep the result if it improves.

items.title: Grid-based initialisation
items.spec: Initialise centres on a jittered 5x5 grid plus one extra point (26 points) with jitter sd 0.03 and radius about 0.09, instead of uniform random placement. This starts near a good layout.

items.title: Hex-like row initialisation
items.spec: Initialise with rows of 5,5,6,5,5 circles (or 6,5,5,5,5) with jitter, since the best known packings are approximately row-structured. Randomly permute the row counts per restart using the seed.

items.title: Better repair via LP
items.spec: Replace the iterative repair with a linear program (scipy linprog) that maximises the sum of radii with the centres fixed, subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and wall limits. The result is exactly feasible and optimal for the centres. Subtract 1e-12 slack.

items.title: Polish best with LP and SLSQP
items.spec: At the end, take the best packing and run one more SLSQP with a tight ftol (1e-12) and a large maxiter, then LP-repair it. Reserve 15 percent of the time for this.

items.title: Raise TIME_FRACTION to 0.9
items.spec: Set TIME_FRACTION to 0.9, which still leaves a safety margin below 30 s CPU. The last restart must not overrun, so also check the elapsed time before each start.

items.title: Two-stage: penalty then SLSQP
items.spec: Run a cheap L-BFGS minimisation of a penalty objective (-sum r plus mu times squared overlaps) with an analytic gradient from random starts. Then refine with SLSQP only if the penalty result is promising, which screens out bad starts.

items.title: Screen restarts with short SLSQP
items.spec: Run each restart for only 40 SLSQP iterations. Keep the top 10 percent by sum of radii, then continue those to full convergence. This saves time on poor basins.

items.title: Neighbour-only constraints
items.spec: After a short run, keep only the pair constraints for pairs whose distance is below 3 times the mean radius, which shrinks the constraint set. Re-verify all pairs in the final repair.

items.title: Radius init variation
items.spec: Draw the initial radii per restart from uniform(0.03, 0.12) instead of the fixed 0.05. This diversifies starting basins.

items.title: Smaller INIT_LOW
items.spec: Set INIT_LOW = 0.05 so that initial centres cover the whole square, including the border where the many small circles of good packings sit.

items.title: Trust-constr alternative
items.spec: Use scipy trust-constr with analytic Jacobians for the final polish of the best packing. It handles degenerate active sets better than SLSQP.

items.title: Annealed overlap penalty continuation
items.spec: Start from random points and run L-BFGS on -sum r + mu*overlap^2 with mu growing 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4. Then finish with SLSQP and the LP repair. This gives smoother basin selection.

items.title: Weighted random radii init
items.spec: Initialise radii at random in proportion to a random permutation, with 4 large circles (0.13) and the others small (0.07). This mimics the known mix of sizes.

items.title: Symmetry-seeded starts
items.spec: Generate half the points randomly in the left half of the square and mirror them, adding a centre point if n is odd. Use these as starts. Optimal packings are often near-symmetric.

items.title: Swap-size perturbation
items.spec: From the best packing, swap the radii of two neighbouring circles that have different radii, add small noise to the centres, and re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept it if it is better.

items.title: Population of elites
items.spec: Keep the top 5 packings. With 50 percent probability, start the next restart from a perturbed elite (noise sd 0.02) instead of from random. Otherwise start from a random point.

items.title: Looser SLSQP tolerance
items.spec: Set ftol=1e-9 in the SLSQP options to stop early on flat progress, which gives more restarts per run.

items.title: Vectorised constraint speed-up
items.spec: Precompute iu once outside the loop and cache the constraint function. Use squared-distance constraints (d^2 >= (ri+rj)^2) to avoid the sqrt, with an analytic Jacobian.

items.title: Shrunk-bounds variables
items.spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0, 0.25]. This removes the wall and r>=0 constraints from the general set and shrinks the QP.

items.title: Final repair shrink reduction
items.spec: Set SHRINK to 1e-12, since the tolerance is 1e-10 and the checks are exact. Verify the validity inside repair with a final loop that reduces radii by the maximum overlap if any remain.

items.title: Inflate-and-shake
items.spec: After SLSQP converges, jitter the centres by sd 0.005 and re-run SLSQP from the converged radii times 0.95. Repeat 3 times and keep the best. This is a cheap local search.

items.title: Pair-relocation move
items.spec: Pick the two smallest circles in the best packing and re-place them at random points. Set their radii to 0.02 and re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept the result if it improves.

items.title: Seed-diverse restarts per phase
items.spec: Spend the first 40 percent of the time on random restarts, then the remaining 40 percent on perturbing the best 3 packings. Use a phase switch based on the elapsed time.

items.title: Border-biased init
items.spec: Place 12 of the 26 initial centres near the border (one coordinate within 0.08 of an edge) and the rest in the interior. Optimal packings have many circles touching walls.

items.title: Active-set polish via Newton
items.spec: Identify the active constraints (gap below 1e-7) of the best packing. Solve the KKT or equality system with Newton steps using least squares to tighten them to machine precision. Then LP-repair, which gains the last 1e-6 or so.

items.title: Multi-start with lower n then add
items.spec: Optimise 25 circles first, then insert a 26th circle at the largest hole with a small radius. Re-optimise all with SLSQP. Mix this with random restarts at 50 percent.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Pass a jac argument to scipy minimize (SLSQP) for both the objective and the constraint vector. The objective gradient is -1 on the radius entries and 0 on the centre entries. The constraint Jacobian has one row per constraint: for each pair (i,j) the derivatives of sqrt(|ci-cj|^2) - ri - rj with respect to ci, cj, ri, rj; for each boundary constraint the unit derivatives with respect to the relevant centre coordinate and radius; and for r>=0 an identity row.
