Build it with numpy using the triu index arrays and scatter-add into a dense matrix. This removes finite-difference cost and lets SLSQP take more iterations within the time budget.

items.title: Raise SLSQP iteration cap and tighten tolerance
items.spec: Increase options maxiter from 200 to 1000 and set options ftol to 1e-12 in the SLSQP call inside _solve_once. Most restarts currently stop early at the iteration cap before converging, so a larger cap should give better local optima for the same number of restarts. Keep everything else unchanged.

items.title: Second SLSQP polish after repair
items.spec: After _repair produces valid radii for the best candidate, run one more SLSQP solve starting from the repaired centres and radii, with the same pair, boundary and nonnegativity constraints. Accept the polished packing only if it passes an exact validity check and has a larger radius sum than the repaired one. This recovers the radius sum lost to the shrink step.

items.title: Trust-constr final polish
items.spec: For the final candidate only, refine the packing with scipy.optimize.minimize using method trust-constr, starting from the best SLSQP result. Use the same pair and boundary inequality constraints, with an analytic or finite-difference Jacobian. Keep the result only if it validates and improves the radius sum. Otherwise return the pre-polish packing.

items.title: Greedy coordinate radius inflation
items.spec: After repair, do a coordinate-ascent pass over circles in random order (rng from seed). For each circle i, set its radius to the largest value allowed by the box walls and by the current radii of all other circles, which is min(distance to walls, distance to each neighbour centre minus that neighbour's radius). Repeat for a few sweeps until no radius changes by more than 1e-12. This never creates overlaps and often increases the sum slightly.

items.title: Proportional global scale repair
items.spec: Replace the pairwise shrink loop in _repair with a single global rule. Compute the scale factor s = min over all pairs of d_ij/(r_i+r_j) and over all wall constraints of the feasible ratio, and multiply all radii by min(1, s) minus SHRINK. This keeps the relative radius structure of the optimizer solution instead of shrinking only the worst pair, and it is a single vectorised step.

items.title: Basin hopping on the best packing
items.spec: After an initial batch of random restarts, repeatedly perturb the current best packing rather than restarting from scratch. Each perturbation moves 1 to 3 randomly chosen circles to uniform random positions inside the square, with radii reset to a small value, then re-runs SLSQP from that point. Accept the new packing if its validated radius sum is at least the current one, else keep the old. Use the seed for all draws.

items.title: Remove-and-reinsert hole filling
items.spec: Perturb the best packing by removing the circle with the smallest radius and reinserting it at the point in a fine random sample of the square that maximises the distance to the nearest wall or circle boundary, i.e. the largest empty hole. Then run SLSQP from this configuration and validate. This targets the common defect of a tiny rattler circle and is applied as one move inside a basin-hopping loop.

items.title: Hexagonal and grid-perturbed initialisation
items.spec: Replace the uniform random start in _solve_once with a structured start for half of the restarts. Lay out roughly n points on a hexagonal or square lattice that fits the unit square with random row counts and a random offset, then add Gaussian jitter of scale 0.02 drawn from rng. Keep the uniform start for the other restarts so the search mixes both kinds of initial point.

items.title: Random initial radii instead of fixed radius
items.spec: Initialise the radii in _solve_once from a uniform draw in [0.02, 0.12] using rng, rather than a constant INIT_RADIUS of 0.05. Different start radii lead SLSQP to different contact graphs, which diversifies the restarts without changing the algorithm.

items.title: Two-stage continuation with inflated radii
items.spec: Run SLSQP in two stages. Stage one solves the problem with each radius lower bound raised to a fixed fraction of the target and the objective unchanged, which pushes the centres apart. Stage two removes the lower bound and runs SLSQP to convergence. Each restart uses both stages from the same random start, and only the final stage output is validated and compared.

items.title: Penalty continuation with L-BFGS-B
items.spec: Replace the constrained solve in the first part of each restart with an unconstrained penalty problem solved by L-BFGS-B. Minimise minus the radius sum plus mu times the squared overlaps and boundary violations, where mu starts at 10 and is multiplied by 10 for each of five stages. Warm start each stage from the previous centres and radii. Finish with one SLSQP call from the last stage to enforce exact feasibility.

items.title: Use more of the time budget
items.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 so that roughly 27 of the 30 seconds of CPU time go to restarts. The repair and final return are cheap, so the total stays well below the 45 second cap. This adds roughly 12 percent more restarts for the same code.

items.title: Successive halving over restarts
items.spec: Run many short restarts first, with SLSQP maxiter of about 50. Keep the top quarter by radius sum after repair, then rerun those candidates from their current state with maxiter of 500. Repeat once more with the top few. The total time is spent on the most promising basins rather than on uniform full-length runs. Track time with time.process_time and stop when the budget is reached.

items.title: Decaying perturbation schedule in basin hopping
items.spec: Within the basin-hopping loop, scale the perturbation of each circle centre by a Gaussian with standard deviation that decays geometrically from 0.15 to 0.01 over the time budget, measured by process_time. Large early perturbations explore new basins and small late ones refine the current one. Validate and accept as in plain basin hopping.

items.title: Adaptive restart pool with early pruning
items.spec: Run each restart's SLSQP in chunks of 60 iterations. After each chunk, compare the current radius sum with the median of all completed restarts at the same chunk index, and abandon the restart if it is below the median minus 0.05. Only completed or pruned runs that are still promising go on to the next chunk. This frees time from hopeless starts.

items.title: Mini-batch subsystem optimisation
items.spec: Each SLSQP call optimises only a random subset of about 8 circles, selected with rng, while all other circles are held fixed as obstacles. Iterate over several random subsets, accepting each update only if the full validated radius sum does not drop. This block-coordinate scheme cuts the size of each QP and lets SLSQP run quickly on larger local neighbourhoods.

items.title: Vectorised multi-start batch
items.spec: Stack the constraint and objective evaluation for a batch of, say, 16 random starts into a single numpy computation with a leading batch axis, and run a simple batched projected gradient ascent on the radius sum with overlap penalties. Keep the best few batch members and finish each with a single SLSQP call. This is a batch-level speedup for the pre-polish phase.

items.title: Population with elite crossover
items.spec: Maintain a population of the best 8 validated packings. Each new candidate is made by taking the centres of one parent for circles with index below a random split and the other parent's centres for the rest, with the radii copied from the same source. Run a short SLSQP from the child, validate, and insert into the population if it beats the worst member. Use rng for all choices.

items.title: Penalise radius variance early
items.spec: Add a small regularisation term to the SLSQP objective during the first half of each restart, equal to minus 0.01 times the sum of log radii, which discourages a few circles from collapsing to zero. Remove the term for the second half and run SLSQP to convergence with the pure radius-sum objective. This is a soft regulariser that keeps the early search away from degenerate local optima.

items.title: Margin-tightened constraints
items.spec: Inside the SLSQP constraints, require a small safety margin in all pair and wall inequalities, for example d_ij minus ri minus rj minus 1e-9 and the wall terms minus 1e-9, so the optimiser returns packings that are strictly feasible in double precision. Then reduce SHRINK in _repair to 1e-12 because repair should rarely need to act. This keeps the exact harness check from being tripped by rounding.

items.title: Minimum radius floor during search
items.spec: Lower bound each radius at 0.01 inside the SLSQP call through the bounds argument, rather than only constraining r to be nonnegative through the inequality. Bounds are handled natively by SLSQP and give it cleaner gradients. After the solve, the usual repair and validation still apply, and any radius at the floor is treated as a rattler and shrunk to zero if it causes overlap.

items.title: Randomised constraint ordering and pair pruning
items.spec: Build the pair constraint list only for pairs whose initial centre distance is below 0.5, then add the remaining pairs back lazily if any violate. This shrinks the constraint vector and speeds each SLSQP iteration. Pick the pair set using the random start, so different restarts see different active sets.

items.title: Symmetry-broken seeded starts
items.spec: For a fraction of restarts, start from a packing where circles are placed in concentric rings with the innermost ring of a random count, using rng to choose ring counts. Add jitter of about 0.03 and run the normal SLSQP. Structured rings produce contact graphs that uniform random starts rarely reach, and the validated best is compared as usual.

items.title: Circle removal and re-solve augmentation
items.spec: From the best packing with n circles, remove one random circle and optimise the remaining n-1 circles with SLSQP. Then insert the removed circle at the largest hole found on a grid sample and re-optimise all n circles. Accept the result if its validated sum is larger. This augments the search with a different topology each iteration.

items.title: Gradual slack-to-tight annealing
items.spec: Use a slack parameter eps that starts at 0.02 and decays to zero across the restarts. Within each restart, the pair constraints are d_ij >= ri + rj minus eps, so early packings are allowed to overlap slightly and the optimiser can reorganise freely. In the final SLSQP call of each restart, eps is zero. Repair then removes any remaining overlap.

items.title: Adaptive restart count from timing probe
items.spec: Before the main loop, time one restart with process_time and estimate how many restarts fit in the budget. Use this estimate to split the budget into a fixed number of equal slices, so that the randomised search is spread evenly over time instead of being cut mid-run at an arbitrary point. Keep the best packing across all slices.

items.title: Mirror and rotation symmetric search
items.spec: For a random half of restarts, constrain the packing to be symmetric about the diagonal of the square by generating only half the centres and mirroring them, with radii duplicated. Solve the reduced problem with SLSQP and then release the symmetry for a final unconstrained SLSQP call from the mirrored solution. Symmetric starts reach a different set of basins than generic ones.

items.title: Two-phase global then local search
items.spec: Use a global phase of random restarts with a coarse penalty objective evaluated on a grid of starting configurations, selecting the 3 most promising by radius sum after a short SLSQP. Then run a local phase that perturbs and re-solves only those 3 packings for the rest of the budget. Architecture is a coarse-to-fine pipeline with separate phases.

items.title: Shrink-aware final validation loop
items.spec: After repair, run a validation loop that checks the packing with exact double-precision pair distances and boundary checks at tolerance 1e-12, and if any violation remains, shrink only the offending circles by a factor of one minus the violation divided by the sum of their radii. Repeat until valid, then return. This guarantees harness validity without over-shrinking good packings.

items.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent
items.spec: After the first random SLSQP start, keep the best packing found so far. Each later iteration perturbs that incumbent: add Gaussian noise (sigma about 0.02) to all centres, clip to [0,1], shrink radii to the repaired values, re-run SLSQP from the perturbed point, and accept the result only if its repaired sum is larger. Use the remaining time budget for these hops, with random restarts as a fallback every so often.

items.title: Remove-smallest and reinsert into largest hole
items.spec: In each local search step, take the incumbent packing, delete the circle with the smallest radius, and reinsert it at the point that maximises the distance to the nearest circle edge. Find that point by sampling about 2000 uniform candidates in the square with numpy and evaluating min over circles of (distance to centre minus radius, and distance to the walls). Re-optimise with SLSQP and keep the result if the repaired sum improves.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Pass a jac argument to scipy minimize that supplies the exact gradient of the constraint vector and of the objective. The pairwise-distance block has derivatives with respect to both centres and both radii, and the wall constraints are simple linear terms. Build the Jacobian with numpy indexing over the upper-triangular pair list. This removes finite-difference cost, so each SLSQP call becomes much faster and more restarts fit in the time budget.

items.title: Squared-distance pair constraints
items.spec: Replace the non-smooth constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - ri - rj >= 0 with the equivalent dx^2+dy^2 - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0 whenever ri+rj >= 0, which is smooth at coincident centres and well conditioned for SLSQP. Keep the wall constraints and the r >= 0 bound as they are. Check the repair step still runs on the true distances so the final packing is valid.

items.title: Bounds instead of wall inequality constraints
items.spec: Move the box constraints into the bounds argument of scipy minimize. Centre coordinates get bounds [0,1] and radii get bounds [0, 0.5]. Remove the four wall inequality blocks from cons, so SLSQP handles only the pairwise overlap constraints plus any remaining explicit constraints. This shrinks the constraint matrix and speeds each SLSQP iteration.

items.title: Prune pair constraints to near neighbours
items.spec: Build the list of overlap constraints only for pairs whose centres are closer than a threshold, for example the sum of the two current radii plus 0.15, when the SLSQP call starts. Pass only those pairs into cons. Rebuild the pair list between SLSQP calls in the basin hopping loop. Fewer constraints give faster iterations, and the final repair still checks all pairs so validity is kept.

items.title: Higher iteration cap with a warm restart
items.spec: Set SLSQP maxiter to 1000 instead of 200 and set ftol to 1e-12. If the first call reports not converged, call SLSQP again from its last iterate until convergence or until a fixed number of chunks, so long runs are continued instead of truncated. Keep the same random-restart outer loop.

items.title: Two-phase penalty then SLSQP polish
items.spec: For each start, first minimise a smooth penalty with L-BFGS-B: minus the sum of radii plus mu times the sum of squared positive parts of the overlap and wall violations. Use mu = 10, then 100, then 1000 with warm starts. Finish with one SLSQP polish from the penalty solution. The penalty stage is cheap and gives a good initial basin.

items.title: Augmented Lagrangian for overlap constraints
items.spec: Solve the packing with an augmented Lagrangian loop. The inner problem is an unconstrained L-BFGS-B minimisation of minus the radius sum plus the augmented penalty terms for each overlap and wall constraint. After each inner solve, update the multipliers as max(0, lambda + rho*g) and increase rho by a factor of 2 when violations do not shrink. Polish the final result with SLSQP.

items.title: Elite population with crossover
items.spec: Maintain a population of the 6 best packings found so far. New candidates are formed by taking circles from one parent on one side of a random line through the square and circles from the other parent on the other side, fixing the count to 26 by moving any surplus or missing circles to random positions. Each child is locally optimised with SLSQP. Replace the worst population member when the child beats it.

items.title: Perturbation scale schedule
items.spec: In the basin hopping loop, draw the perturbation sigma from a log-uniform range and anneal the upper bound over the time budget, from about 0.1 at the start down to about 0.005 near the end. Large early moves explore different structures and small late moves refine the best basin. Accept worse solutions with a small probability that decreases with time, as in simulated annealing.

items.title: Adaptive time allocation across starts
items.spec: Run a fixed short SLSQP for each random start, for example with maxiter 60. Keep only the top quarter of starts by repaired sum and continue optimising those with the full iteration cap. Repeat this successive-halving style in rounds until the time budget is spent, then return the best. This spends the budget on promising basins instead of finishing every start.

items.title: Raise the time fraction
items.spec: Change TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so that solve uses about 27.9 s of the 30 s process-time budget, staying well below the 45 s void threshold. Keep every other part of the algorithm unchanged. This gives a few more restarts or hops at no complexity cost.

items.title: Better repair that keeps the radius sum
items.spec: Replace the current repair, which scales both circles of an overlapping pair by the same factor, with a greedy repair. For the most violated pair, shrink only the circle with the smaller radius by the overlap amount, and then clip to the walls. Repeat until no pair overlaps. This keeps larger radii on the more constrained circles and should recover a larger radius sum from the same centres.

items.title: LP radius polish with fixed centres
items.spec: After SLSQP and the repair, freeze the centres and maximise the sum of radii with a linear program from scipy linprog. Use linearised constraints ri + rj <= current distance dij, with the gradient of the distance at the current centres, plus wall bounds ri <= distance to walls. Keep the solution only if the true repaired packing is valid and its sum is larger. Iterate this two or three times.

items.title: Symmetric initial layouts
items.spec: Add a family of starting configurations that impose a symmetry, for example a mirror about the vertical line x = 0.5 or a 180-degree rotation about the centre. Generate half of the centres at random and mirror or rotate them to get the other half, with an odd count handled by placing one circle on the axis. Use these starts for part of the random restarts so the search covers symmetric basins that uniform random starts rarely reach.

items.title: Hexagonal and row-based seeds
items.spec: Add structured initial layouts to the restart pool. Choose a row pattern, for example 5, 6, 5, 5, 5 circles per row, or 4, 5, 6, 5, 6, and place the centres evenly across each row with alternating offsets, which gives a near-hexagonal arrangement. Add small random jitter, then optimise with SLSQP. Mix these seeds with the uniform random starts, alternating between the two kinds.

items.title: Radius-initialisation from a greedy pack
items.spec: Initialise the radii for each start by greedily packing circles. Place centres one at a time at random points, and for each new centre set its radius to the largest value that fits without overlap or leaving the square. Use these greedy radii as the starting point for SLSQP rather than the constant 0.05. Random centres still come from the seed, so the diversity of the starts is kept.

items.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning
items.spec: Scale the optimisation variables so that positions and radii have similar magnitudes. Set the decision vector to be the centres divided by 1 and radii multiplied by 10, so that a unit step in each entry corresponds to a comparable change in geometry. Adjust the objective and the constraint functions accordingly, and undo the scaling before the repair step. This can reduce the number of SLSQP iterations needed to converge.

items.title: Gradient-free polishing with Nelder-Mead on the worst circle
items.spec: After each SLSQP result, repeatedly pick the circle with the smallest radius and try to move it to a new random point in its neighbourhood, or to a point in a large empty region. Re-run SLSQP with the moved circle, and keep the change if the repaired sum improves. This targets the weakest circle, which is the one that limits the packing.

items.title: Soft radius growth from the incumbent
items.spec: Start each local search from the incumbent with all radii set to 0.9 times their current values and centres unchanged. Run SLSQP with the sum-of-radii objective so the packing relaxes outwards from a feasible-looking state. This inflation-style warm start often lands in a nearby better basin more reliably than a fresh random start.

items.title: Regularised radius objective early in the run
items.spec: Add a small bonus term to the SLSQP objective, minus the sum of radii plus lambda times the sum of the squared radii, with lambda starting at 0.05 and decaying to 0 over the first few calls. A penalty on the spread of radii discourages early collapse of small circles and keeps the search exploring. Once lambda reaches zero, the objective is the true radius sum again.

items.title: Noise on centres as regularisation during hops
items.spec: During basin hopping, add zero-mean Gaussian noise to the centres of the incumbent with a sigma chosen per hop, and clip the noisy centres to a margin of 0.02 inside the square. This keeps all perturbed circles away from the walls, which otherwise make SLSQP start from infeasible wall positions and waste iterations. Use the same repair as before.

items.title: Mini-batch of starts for parallel-style selection
items.spec: Generate a batch of 8 random starts per round. Run SLSQP on each in turn with a moderate iteration cap, then keep the top 2 by repaired sum and run a full-length SLSQP on those. Repeat rounds until the time budget is used, and return the best packing found in any round. Batching the selection step gives a cheap filter on the many starts.

items.title: Shuffle circle identity to escape local minima
items.spec: Between hops, randomly permute the labels of circles that have similar radii, that is, swap the centres and radii of two circles whose radii differ by less than 0.02. Re-optimise from the swapped configuration. Label swaps do not change the packing itself, but they change the starting geometry for SLSQP and let the optimiser reach different local optima.

items.title: Vectorised overlap computation for repair and check
items.spec: Rewrite the repair loop so that it computes the full pairwise distance matrix once per iteration with numpy broadcasting and handles all overlapping pairs in one vectorised update, instead of picking one pair per iteration with unravel_index. Allow up to 500 iterations so that the repair always reaches a valid packing. This removes the risk that 50 iterations leave a small overlap that the harness rejects.

items.title: Stochastic restart bias towards the incumbent
items.spec: Each restart is a random draw. With probability 0.3 start from a perturbed copy of the incumbent, with the perturbation drawn from a small Gaussian. With probability 0.7 start from a fresh uniform random layout. This mixes exploitation and exploration in one loop and keeps the code change to a few lines.

items.title: Lower the initial radius and widen the start box
items.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.01 and INIT_LOW to 0.02 so that random starts begin with small circles spread across most of the square, instead of medium circles clustered near the middle. Small starts give SLSQP more room to move each circle into a good position before the overlap constraints bind. Keep everything else the same.

items.title: Batch-size independent restart cap
items.spec: Track the number of SLSQP iterations used across all calls and stop each individual call when it exceeds a per-call budget that is a fixed fraction of the total time, so that no single bad start consumes most of the budget. Use process_time to decide the per-call cap at the start of each call. This keeps the restart count stable across seeds and reduces variance of the 3-seed mean.

items.title: Global-scale repair instead of pairwise shrink
items.spec: Replace the pairwise shrink loop in _repair with a single global factor. Compute the minimum over all pairs of d_ij/(r_i+r_j) and over boundary slacks, then multiply all radii by min(1, that factor) minus SHRINK. This removes the 50-iteration loop and keeps the relative radius profile intact, so the repaired sum is closer to the SLSQP optimum. Keep the final validity check so no overlap can reach the harness.

items.title: Final SLSQP polish of the best packing
items.spec: After the random-restart loop picks the best (c, r), run one more SLSQP call started from that packing with maxiter about 500 and ftol 1e-12, using the same constraints. Accept the polished result only if it is valid after repair and has a larger radius sum than the current best. This recovers the small slack that the repair step gives up.

items.title: Use more of the time budget
items.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9. The harness voids a job only above 45 s CPU, and the limit is 30 s, so the loop can safely use about 27 s. Leave the rest of the code unchanged.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Pass a jac argument to minimize that returns the exact gradient of the constraint vector with respect to the 3n variables. Pair-distance derivatives are unit vectors scattered into the centre and radius columns; boundary derivatives are simple +-1 entries. Analytic gradients make each SLSQP iteration much cheaper, so more restarts fit into the budget.

items.title: Sparse neighbour constraints
items.spec: Only include pair constraints for pairs whose centres are closer than a threshold such as r_i+r_j+0.15 at the start of each restart. Build the pair index once per restart from the initial geometry. This shrinks the constraint vector from 325 pairs to a few dozen, speeding up SLSQP. Re-check all pairs in the repair step so validity is still guaranteed.

items.title: Higher iteration cap with tighter tolerance
items.spec: Set MAX_ITER to 1000 and pass options ftol 1e-12 to the SLSQP call. Many restarts currently stop at 200 iterations before converging, so the reported radius sums are below their local optima. Keep everything else the same.

items.title: Penalty-continuation pre-stage
items.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise a smooth penalty with L-BFGS-B: minus the sum of radii plus weight times the squared overlap and boundary violations. Start the weight at 10 and multiply it by 10 for each of 4 stages, warm-starting each stage from the previous one. Pass the resulting near-feasible configuration to SLSQP. This gives a better-conditioned start than uniform random centres.

items.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent
items.spec: After an initial batch of random restarts, repeatedly perturb the best packing by adding Gaussian noise with sigma 0.03 to all centres, clip to the square, and re-run SLSQP from there. Accept the new result if its repaired radius sum improves on the incumbent, otherwise keep the incumbent. Spend roughly half of the remaining time on this loop.

items.title: Remove and reinsert the smallest circle
items.spec: On each perturbation step of the search, take the circle with the smallest radius in the incumbent, move it to a uniformly random position inside the square, give it radius 0.01, and re-run SLSQP. Accept if the repaired radius sum improves. This is a targeted move that lets the packing reorganise around the weakest circle.

items.title: Relocate rattler circles into the largest hole
items.spec: After SLSQP, identify rattlers as circles with no active contact (slack above 1e-6 to all neighbours and walls). Move each rattler to the grid point that maximises the distance to all other centres and walls (search a 200 by 200 grid), set its radius to that clearance, and re-optimise. This uses the wasted space that rattlers hold in the incumbent.

items.title: Annealed perturbation size
items.spec: In the perturbation search, start with Gaussian sigma 0.1 on the centres and multiply it by 0.9 after every rejected step, with a floor of 0.005. Reset it to 0.1 after each accepted improvement. Large early moves explore distant basins and small late moves refine the incumbent.

items.title: Metropolis acceptance in the perturbation chain
items.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, accept a worse packing with probability exp(-(old - new)/T) where T starts at 0.01 and decays geometrically to 1e-4 over the search. Always keep track of the best packing seen separately from the current chain state. This allows the search to escape local optima of the radius sum.

items.title: Elite crossover between packings
items.spec: Keep an elite pool of the 5 best distinct packings found so far. For each new start, pick two elites, take the centres with x below 0.5 from the first and the rest from the second, and fix the count to n by dropping or adding random points. Start SLSQP from that child. This recombines good spatial structure from different basins.

items.title: Farthest-point sampling initialisation
items.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres with a max-min (farthest-point) sample. Draw 2000 candidate points in [0.05, 0.95]^2 from the seeded generator, then greedily pick n of them, each time choosing the candidate farthest from all already chosen points. The starts are spread out evenly, which gives SLSQP a better initial spacing.

items.title: Hexagonal-lattice starts with jitter
items.spec: Build a starting set from a hexagonal lattice with spacing chosen so about 30 points fit in the square, select n of them at random, add uniform jitter of 0.02, and clip to the square. Alternate these starts with uniform random starts so both kinds of basin are explored. The lattice gives a near-dense start that SLSQP can refine into the good packings.

items.title: Boundary-ring initialisation
items.spec: For each restart, place a random number k between 10 and 16 of the circles evenly along the four edges of the square with a random offset, and scatter the other n-k uniformly in the interior. Use a shared initial radius of 0.05. Boundary-first starts favour the layouts in which large circles hug the walls.

items.title: Successive halving over restarts
items.spec: Run many cheap restarts with SLSQP maxiter set to 40, keep the best 20 percent by repaired radius sum, and run full SLSQP with maxiter 1000 only on those. Use the seeded generator for all draws. This spends more of the budget on the starts that look promising while still sampling many basins.

items.title: Staged SLSQP with checkpoint restarts
items.spec: Run SLSQP in stages of maxiter 60, restarting from the last iterate each time, and stop the restart early if the repaired radius sum after a stage is below 0.9 times the incumbent. Hopeless starts are cut short and the time goes to the rest. Keep the final best selection unchanged.

items.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning
items.spec: Scale the variables so the optimiser works with x_scaled = x times 10 for the radii and the centres unchanged, or equivalently scale the radius variables and objective by a fixed factor. Rescale back before the repair step. Better-conditioned variables and constraints usually give fewer SLSQP line-search failures.

items.title: Trust-constr polish of the final packing
items.spec: After the best packing is chosen, run scipy minimize with method trust-constr on the same constraints, starting from the SLSQP result, with a 2 second cap. Keep the result only if it is valid after repair and has a larger radius sum. Trust-region methods can refine solutions where SLSQP stalls on degenerate contacts.

items.title: Symmetric first-stage optimisation
items.spec: For half of the restarts, impose mirror symmetry about the line x = 0.5 by optimising only the left-half centres and radii, with the right half set as reflections, and the circles on x=0.5 constrained. Run SLSQP on this reduced problem, then unfreeze all variables and run a final SLSQP on the full problem from the symmetric solution. Symmetric packings are a common structure among good solutions.

items.title: Radius-variance regularisation early on
items.spec: Add a term lambda times the variance of the radii to the SLSQP objective, with lambda starting at 0.5 and set to zero for the final solve. The term pushes the early optimisation toward equal radii, which smooths the landscape and avoids collapsing small circles. Anneal it with the outer restart loop.

items.title: Jitter regularisation of centres during the search
items.spec: At each restart, after SLSQP converges, add small Gaussian noise of sigma 0.005 to the centres and run SLSQP again, repeated 3 times, keeping the best result. Repeated small kicks help the optimiser leave shallow local optima without destroying the basin.

items.title: Batched penalty optimisation of many starts
items.spec: Generate 64 random starts at once as a batch array and minimise the overlap penalty for all of them together with a vectorised numpy gradient step loop (for example 2000 steps of gradient descent with decaying step size). Pick the 4 best by penalty-free radius sum and run SLSQP only on those. Batching explores far more starts per second than a serial SLSQP loop.

items.title: Random direction swap of ambiguous circles
items.spec: After each SLSQP result, pick two circles with the most similar radii and swap their radii and centres with probability 0.5, then re-run SLSQP. This discrete move changes which circle sits in which slot and is cheap to test. Accept only if the repaired radius sum improves.

items.title: Clip before repair
items.spec: Before calling _repair, clip the centres to [r_i, 1 - r_i] per circle, then set r_i to min(r_i, distance to the nearest wall) so the boundary constraints hold exactly. Only then run the pairwise repair. This reduces how much the repair must shrink radii, giving a higher final sum without changing the search.

items.title: Adaptive restart count from time used
items.spec: Track the average CPU time of one SLSQP restart and the fraction of restarts that improve the incumbent. Stop starting new restarts when the last 20 restarts have produced no improvement, and use the remaining time for the basin hopping loop instead. This shifts effort from exploration to exploitation based on observed returns.

items.title: Mixed initial radius distribution
items.spec: Instead of the fixed initial radius 0.05, sample initial radii per restart from a uniform distribution on [0.02, 0.12], with the sample drawn from the seeded generator. Diverse starting sizes lead SLSQP to different contact graphs. Keep the repair step as before.

items.title: Fewer, bigger starts with restart reuse
items.spec: Use only 4 to 6 long SLSQP runs per solve, each with maxiter 1000, and seed each run from the best packing of the previous run after a random perturbation of 0.02 on the centres. Chaining long runs replaces many short independent restarts with a deeper search on the best basin.

items.title: Pool-level weight decay on the centre cloud
items.spec: Add a small quadratic penalty on the distance of each centre from the square centre (weight 1e-4) to the SLSQP objective during the first half of the time budget, then remove it. The mild pull toward the middle reduces circles pinned to the boundary early and encourages compact layouts before boundary contacts form.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and a vectorised analytic Jacobian for the constraints (pair distance gradients, wall constraints). Removes finite-difference cost (about 129 evals per gradient), so many more restarts or iterations fit in the time budget. Build the Jacobian as a dense array using the triu indices.

items.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000
items.spec: Set MAX_ITER=1000 (used together with the analytic Jacobian) so SLSQP converges fully rather than stopping at 200 iterations. Also add ftol=1e-12 in options.

items.title: Use full time fraction 0.92
items.spec: Change TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.92. Make sure the last restart cannot overrun: track the longest restart time and stop if the remaining time is less than that.

items.title: Hex-grid perturbed init
items.spec: Instead of uniform random starts, initialise centres on a jittered hexagonal/staggered grid (rows of 6,5,6,5,6,4 etc. or a generic grid with about 32 sites) with noise sd 0.03, radii 0.08. Gives better starting basins than uniform random.

items.title: Basin hopping from best
items.spec: After a few random restarts, spend the remaining time perturbing the best solution: move 2-4 random circles (or the smallest ones) to random locations or add Gaussian noise sd 0.02 to all centres, re-run SLSQP from there, and accept if the sum improves. Keep the best.

items.title: Remove smallest circle and reinsert
items.spec: Perturbation move: take the best solution, delete the circle with the smallest radius, and place it in the largest empty hole (found by sampling 2000 random points and picking the one with max distance clearance). Re-optimise with SLSQP from the result.

items.title: Smaller initial radii
items.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS=0.03 and INIT_LOW=0.05 so that starts have fewer initial overlaps and the optimisation spreads centres over the whole square.

items.title: Two-phase: cheap short runs then polish
items.spec: Run many restarts with MAX_ITER=60, keep the top 5 by sum of radii, then polish each with MAX_ITER=500 and take the best. Splits time 50/50.

items.title: Squared-distance constraints
items.spec: Rewrite the pair constraints as smooth squared form: (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, avoiding the sqrt nondifferentiability at zero distance. Supply analytic Jacobian if possible.

items.title: Better repair via exact LP
items.spec: Replace the iterative repair with a linear program (scipy linprog) which fixes the centres and maximises sum of radii subject to ri+rj<=dij-1e-12 and wall limits. Gives optimal radii for the given centres and always valid. Verify validity afterwards and shrink by 1e-12 if needed.

items.title: Smaller SHRINK
items.spec: Set SHRINK=1e-11 in the repair step (tolerance is 1e-10), recovering about 3e-8 per circle. Only do this after an exact validity check that subtracts any residual overlap.

items.title: Trust-constr/ other polish
items.spec: After the best SLSQP result, run a final SLSQP with tighter ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=300 starting from the best solution with analytic Jacobian to squeeze the last digits.

items.title: Sparse neighbour constraints
items.spec: In the polish phase, include only pair constraints for pairs with distance less than ri+rj+0.15, reducing the constraint count from 496 to about 150 and speeding each SLSQP iteration. Check the full validity at the end via repair.

items.title: Radii-size-mixed init
items.spec: Initialise radii randomly from uniform(0.03,0.12) rather than constant, to encourage diversity of big and small circles, which the best known packings have.

items.title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation
items.spec: Before SLSQP, run 100 steps of gradient descent on a soft overlap penalty energy with growing radii starting from random centres, to get a feasible-ish start. Then SLSQP.

items.title: Symmetric initial layouts
items.spec: For half the restarts, generate 16 random circles in the left half and mirror them across x=0.5 for the init (with noise 0.01). SLSQP then breaks the symmetry if beneficial.

items.title: Lloyd/Voronoi init
items.spec: Init centres by running 5 Lloyd iterations of random points in the unit square (using a sampled grid of 4000 points and nearest-centre assignment), giving evenly spread starts; radii set to 0.5 of nearest-neighbour distance.

items.title: Boundary-biased init
items.spec: Place about 12 of the circles near the walls and corners (uniform along the perimeter, offset 0.06 inwards) and the rest uniformly inside, mimicking the best packings having many wall-touching circles.

items.title: Variable-fixing scaling
items.spec: Scale the variables, e.g. optimise in coordinates for 2*c-1 and radii *2, to improve SLSQP conditioning. Minor change; compare against baseline.

items.title: Accept-worse annealed hopping
items.spec: In basin hopping, accept worse solutions with probability exp(-delta/T), T decaying from 0.005 to 0.0005 over the time budget, while tracking the global best separately.

items.title: Swap-two-sizes move
items.spec: Perturbation: swap the positions of a big circle and a small circle (by radius ranking) in the best solution, scale radii to the swapped spots, and re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept if improved.

items.title: Parallel-free multi-start with early abort
items.spec: Run each restart with MAX_ITER=40 first; if sum of radii (after cheap repair) is below the best-so-far minus 0.05, discard it; otherwise continue with 300 more iterations from that state.

items.title: Skip repair, check validity
items.spec: Instead of the 50-iteration pairwise repair, use vectorised scaling: compute for each circle the max overlap, shrink radii by half of the max overlap at each pair vectorised until none remain. Faster and less lossy.

items.title: Seed with known structure by computation
items.spec: Generate starts from a computed square-lattice layout of 6x6 minus 4 removed random circles (36-4=32) with radius 1/12, jittered by noise 0.02. Lattice-like starts are near the good basins.

items.title: Cluster-move perturbation
items.spec: Perturb the best solution by picking a random centre point and displacing all circles within distance 0.25 by Gaussian noise sd 0.04, then re-run SLSQP. Accept on improvement.

items.title: Increase radius objective weighting via continuation
items.spec: First solve maximising the sum of squared radii-adjusted objective with a small term pushing all radii equal, then switch to the true sum objective starting from the result. Smooths early landscape.

items.title: Constraint margin during search
items.spec: Use pair constraint d >= 1e-9 margin in SLSQP so that the result is nearly feasible and the repair loses almost nothing.

items.title: Final random-jiggle polish of best
items.spec: In the last 10 percent of the time, repeatedly add tiny noise (sd 0.003) to the best centres and re-run SLSQP with the analytic Jacobian, keeping improvements.

items.title: Weighted choice of restarts from elite pool
items.spec: Keep a pool of the top 5 solutions; each iteration pick one at random and perturb 3 circles' positions, re-optimise, and replace the worst pool member if better and distinct (sum differs by more than 1e-6).

items.title: Lower-time per-restart cap
items.spec: Use MAX_ITER=100 with analytic Jacobian to maximise restart count, and pick the best 3 for a full-length polishing at the end.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Supply jac= for the objective (gradient: zeros for centres, -1 for radii) and a analytic constraint Jacobian (sparse-structured but dense array) for cons. This makes each SLSQP run much faster than finite differences, allowing many more restarts in 24 s. Build the Jacobian with numpy for the pair, wall and r>=0 constraints.

items.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000 with early exit
items.spec: Set MAX_ITER=600 so SLSQP converges fully rather than stopping at 200 iterations; combine with analytic Jacobian if present. Keep the repair step.

items.title: Two-phase: best-of-restarts then polish
items.spec: Use 60% of time for short SLSQP runs (maxiter 100) from random starts, keep the top 3 results, then spend the remaining time polishing them with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-15. Return the best repaired result.

items.title: Perturb-and-reoptimize basin hopping
items.spec: After finding the best packing, repeatedly perturb it: jitter all centres by gaussian sd 0.02, or move one or two smallest circles to random positions, shrink radii by 0.5, and re-run SLSQP warm-started. Accept if the sum of radii improves. Use remaining time on this instead of pure random restarts.

items.title: Hex-grid-like initialisation
items.spec: Initialise centres on a jittered hex or square lattice (rows of 6/5 alternating, about 32 points) with noise sd 0.03 and radius 0.08, instead of uniform random. Randomise row counts by seed.

items.title: Smaller initial radius
items.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS=0.02 so the starting point is feasible, letting SLSQP begin from a valid configuration and grow circles.

items.title: Random initial radii
items.spec: Draw initial radii uniformly from [0.03,0.12] so the optimiser finds mixed-size configurations that the best known packings have.

items.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle
items.spec: In the improvement loop, take the best packing, delete the circle with smallest radius, place it at the point of largest empty-circle (sample 2000 random points, pick max distance to the circle boundaries and walls), set its radius small, and re-run SLSQP. Accept if improved.

items.title: Increase TIME_FRACTION to 0.9
items.spec: Use TIME_FRACTION=0.9 but stop starting a new run when the elapsed time plus the longest run time observed exceeds 0.95*time_limit, to stay safe under the CPU limit.

items.title: Better repair via LP
items.spec: Replace the iterative repair with an LP: fixing centres, maximise sum of radii s.t. r_i+r_j<=d_ij*(1-1e-12), r_i<=wall distance, r>=0, solved with scipy linprog highs. This recovers the optimal radii for the centres and gives guaranteed validity; subtract 1e-10 afterwards.

items.title: LP polish of the centres
items.spec: After SLSQP, alternate: LP for radii given centres, then sequential linearised update of centres with trust region. Or simply re-run SLSQP from the LP solution with tight ftol. Apply to the best few candidates.

items.title: Use trust-constr-free penalty pre-stage
items.spec: Before SLSQP, run a few hundred steps of L-BFGS-B on penalty objective -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2) with mu increasing 10,100,1000. Then pass to SLSQP. Gives better basins than raw SLSQP from random.

items.title: Constraint pruning for speed
items.spec: Only include pair constraints for pairs whose centre distance in the start is below 0.5, since far pairs cannot overlap. Recompute and verify afterwards, falling back to repair. This reduces constraint count from 496 to about 150 and speeds each SLSQP call.

items.title: Squared-distance constraints
items.spec: Use constraints (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0 with analytic Jacobian, avoiding sqrt and its non-smoothness at zero distance. Add r>=0 bounds via bounds argument.

items.title: Use bounds for the box
items.spec: Pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5], and keep only wall constraints c-r>=0 etc. Reduces ill-conditioning and removes the r>=0 constraints.

items.title: Seed from symmetric configurations
items.spec: With probability 0.3 per restart generate 16 points randomly in half of the square and mirror them across x=0.5 (or a diagonal), then optimise; symmetric starts may reach better packings.

items.title: Annealed jitter restarts from elite pool
items.spec: Maintain an elite pool of the top 5 packings. Each restart picks one at random, adds noise with sd uniform in [0.005,0.05] to centres, sets radii to 0.8 of their values and runs SLSQP. Mix 30% fully random starts.

items.title: Swap two circles of different radii
items.spec: Perturbation move: choose two circles with markedly different radii in the best packing, swap their centres, shrink all radii by 30%, re-optimise with SLSQP, accept if better.

items.title: Short screening runs
items.spec: For each random start run SLSQP with maxiter=40 first; only continue (warm-started, maxiter 300) if the interim sum of radii is within 3% of the best interim seen. Saves time on poor basins.

items.title: Tighter ftol
items.spec: Set options ftol=1e-12 in SLSQP so converged runs reach the true local optimum to more digits, and combine with maxiter 500.

items.title: Sorted-size initial radii by region
items.spec: Initialise larger radii (0.1) for centres near the middle and smaller (0.05) near edges and corners, since optimal packings tend to put small circles in corners. Centres still random.

items.title: Boundary-biased centres
items.spec: Draw initial centres from a Beta(0.7,0.7) distribution per coordinate so more circles start near the walls, with INIT_LOW removed; known best packings have many circles touching the border.

items.title: Final high-precision repair
items.spec: Make SHRINK adaptive: compute the maximum violation after clip and subtract only needed amounts (e.g. SHRINK=1e-11 with verification that the exact check passes, else 1e-9). Recovers about 1e-9 per circle; marginal but free.

items.title: Multi-stage radius growth
items.spec: Run SLSQP first with the objective maximising sum of r but with radii upper-bounded at 0.09, then rerun without the bound from that solution. Limiting the largest circles early encourages more uniform arrangements.

items.title: Vary circle-count of start then add circles
items.spec: Optimise 31 circles from random start, then insert the 32nd at the largest hole with tiny radius and re-optimise with all 32. Repeat with different seeds.

items.title: Lloyd-style spread init
items.spec: Initialise centres by sampling 32 points with a few Lloyd (centroid) relaxation iterations over 5000 random sample points, producing well-spread centres; radius starts at 0.06.

items.title: Quasi-random Sobol starts
items.spec: Use scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol seeded by the seed to produce centre starts rather than uniform random for better coverage of the space across restarts.

items.title: Early termination of runs by time guard
items.spec: Add a callback to SLSQP raising an exception when time exceeds the budget, and keep the last iterate through repair, so the final run is not wasted and no overrun occurs.

items.title: Remove overlaps through SLSQP final feasibility pass
items.spec: After the main solve, run a short SLSQP with constraints scaled by (1-1e-9) margin so the solution is exactly feasible, instead of the lossy pairwise shrink; then apply the standard repair as a safety net.

items.title: Move smallest-radius circles randomly
items.spec: Each hop: pick the k=3 smallest circles of the best packing, relocate them uniformly at random, set their radii to 0.01, reoptimise with SLSQP maxiter 200. Accept only if the sum improves; do this for the last 70% of time.

items.title: Parallel-free diversified restarts by radius scale
items.spec: Cycle INIT_RADIUS through [0.03,0.05,0.07,0.09] across restarts and INIT_LOW through [0.05,0.1,0.2], so the restart distribution is more diverse.

items.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Supply jac for the objective (gradient -1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pairwise distance derivatives, wall terms, r>=0) to SLSQP via the constraints dict 'jac'. This removes finite-difference cost so many more restarts or iterations fit in 30 s.

items.title: Raise MAX_ITER to 1000
items.spec: Set MAX_ITER=1000 so SLSQP converges fully instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Keep the rest unchanged.

items.title: Basin hopping from best
items.spec: After a few random restarts, spend the remaining time perturbing the best solution: move 2-4 random circles to new random positions with small radii, or jitter all centres by sd 0.02, then re-run SLSQP from there. Accept if the sum of radii improves.

items.title: Hex-grid-like initialisation
items.spec: Initialise centres on a jittered hexagonal or staggered grid with rows of 5-6 circles (32 points), with radius about 0.08, instead of uniform random. Add noise sd 0.02 from the seeded rng.

items.title: Two-stage screening
items.spec: Stage 1: run SLSQP with few iterations (50) on many random starts. Stage 2: take the top 3 by sum of radii and run SLSQP to full convergence (maxiter 500). This allocates time to promising starts.

items.title: Varied initial radii
items.spec: Draw the initial radii from uniform(0.03, 0.12) per circle instead of a constant 0.05, so starts have varied radii mixes. Use the rng.

items.title: Wall-wide init range
items.spec: Set INIT_LOW=0.03 so initial centres cover the whole square including near walls, since optimal packings have circles touching the walls.

items.title: Use time fraction 0.92
items.spec: Set TIME_FRACTION to 0.92, with a guard that estimates the duration of the last restart and stops if another would exceed the limit. More restarts fit within the limit.

items.title: LP radius polish
items.spec: After SLSQP, fix the centres and solve the radii via scipy.optimize.linprog (highs): maximise sum r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij and wall constraints, r>=0. This gives the optimal radii for the given centres and replaces the greedy _repair shrinking. Keep a final tiny shrink of about 1e-12 for validity.

items.title: Squared-distance constraints
items.spec: Give SLSQP the constraint form d^2 - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0 (with r>=0 enforced) to avoid the sqrt singularity at d=0, ideally with an analytic Jacobian.

items.title: Coarse then fine tolerance
items.spec: Solve first with ftol=1e-4 and maxiter 100, then refine with ftol=1e-10 from the result only if the sum of radii is within 2% of the best so far.

items.title: Tighter ftol
items.spec: Pass ftol=1e-10 in SLSQP options so the final iterations converge to a tight KKT point before the repair, which reduces repair loss.

items.title: Relocate smallest circle to largest gap
items.spec: In a basin-hopping loop, pick the smallest-radius circle and relocate it to the best of 200 random candidate points (maximising min distance to other circles minus their radii), then re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept if better.

items.title: Mirror-symmetric starts
items.spec: Half the restarts initialise a mirror-symmetric configuration (16 random circles plus their reflections x->1-x), with the optimiser free to break the symmetry.

items.title: Vectorised repair
items.spec: Replace the greedy pairwise repair with: for every violating pair compute s_ij=d_ij/(r_i+r_j), scale r_i by the min s over its violating pairs, and iterate until valid. Faster and less lossy when SLSQP is near-feasible.

items.title: Skip repair when nearly valid
items.spec: Check the SLSQP result first; if max overlap < 1e-12, just subtract 1e-11 from the radii; otherwise run the repair. This avoids needless 1e-9 shrinkage per circle.

items.title: Early abort of poor starts
items.spec: Run SLSQP in chunks of 40 iterations. After the first chunk discard the start if its sum of radii is below 90% of the best final sum so far, saving time for good starts.

items.title: Prune distant pair constraints
items.spec: Only include pair constraints for pairs whose initial distance is under 0.4, then check all pairs after the solve and re-solve with the full set if violated. Makes SLSQP faster per iteration.

items.title: Trust-constr final polish
items.spec: Use method trust-constr with a sparse analytic Jacobian instead of SLSQP for polishing only the best candidate near the end.

items.title: Penalty L-BFGS pre-stage
items.spec: Before SLSQP, run L-BFGS-B on a penalty objective -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2 + wall violation^2) with mu going 10,100,1000, using analytic gradients. Use the result as the SLSQP start.

items.title: Mixed-size init
items.spec: Initialise with 4 large circles (r=0.15) and 28 small ones (r=0.06) at random positions to encourage mixed-size packings.

items.title: Elite pool restarts
items.spec: Keep the top 5 solutions found. After 30% of the time, each new start is an elite member perturbed by gaussian noise sd 0.03 on centres, radii times 0.8, then SLSQP.

items.title: Annealed perturbation size
items.spec: In basin hopping, make the perturbation sd decay linearly from 0.05 to 0.005 over the time budget.

items.title: Remove and reinsert small circles
items.spec: Remove the 2 circles with the smallest radii from the best solution, reinsert them at random positions with radius 0.02, then SLSQP. Accept if better.

items.title: Iteration budget by phase
items.spec: Use MAX_ITER 100 for the first half of the time (screening) and 400 for the second half, with the second half restarting from the best solution perturbed.

items.title: Sobol initial centres
items.spec: Draw initial centres from scipy.stats.qmc.Sobol scrambled with the seed, for better-spread starts than iid uniform.

items.title: Ring-structured init
items.spec: Initialise about 12 circles around the perimeter at 0.07 from the walls and the remaining 20 randomly in the interior, matching typical optimal structure.

items.title: Final long polish
items.spec: Reserve the last 15% of the time to re-run SLSQP on the best solution with maxiter 2000 and ftol 1e-12, then repair; keep it only if the valid sum improves.

items.title: Cache constraint index arrays
items.spec: Precompute the triu indices once outside _solve_once and use preallocated arrays in cons. A pure speed-up that gives more restarts.

items.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent
items.spec: After the first random SLSQP restart, keep the best packing. Each further iteration perturbs it: pick 1-3 random circles, relocate them to uniform random centres, optionally jitter all centres by N(0, 0.02), then re-run SLSQP from that point. Accept the new packing if its repaired radius sum is higher (greedy). Keep the same time loop and return the best packing.

items.title: Remove-smallest and reinsert into largest hole
items.spec: From the incumbent packing, remove the circle with the smallest radius. Estimate the largest free hole by sampling 5000 random points in the square and picking the point maximising the distance to all remaining circle boundaries (min over j of dist - r_j, and the wall distance). Place the removed circle there with that radius, then re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept if the repaired sum improves.

items.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP
items.spec: Pass a jac argument to minimize. The objective gradient is -1 on the radius block. For the constraint function, write the analytic Jacobian: for each pair row, d/dc of the distance term is the unit vector (c_i - c_j)/dist, d/dr_i and d/dr_j are -1; wall rows are simple +-1 entries on the centre and radius columns. Build it as a dense (m, 3n) array with vectorised indexing. This removes the finite-difference cost and allows many more restarts within the 24 s budget.

items.title: Sparse neighbour-pair constraints
items.spec: Instead of all n(n-1)/2 pair constraints, build the candidate pair list once per SLSQP call from the current centres, keeping only pairs with centre distance below r_i + r_j + 0.15. Rebuild the list after each outer round (run SLSQP in 3 rounds of maxiter 70 each). This shrinks the constraint matrix and speeds each iteration while keeping all near contacts.

items.title: Hexagonal-lattice perturbed initialisation
items.spec: For some restarts, initialise centres from a hexagonal or square lattice with spacing chosen so that about n points fit in [0.05, 0.95]^2, pick the n points nearest a random offset, and add N(0, 0.03) jitter. Mix these with the uniform random starts in a fixed ratio of 1 lattice to 2 uniform starts. Radii start at a small value.

items.title: Greedy sequential insertion initialisation
items.spec: Generate initial centres by sequential greedy packing: repeatedly sample 2000 random candidate points, choose the one with the largest clearance (min of wall distance and distance to existing centres minus their radii) and add it with that clearance as radius (capped at 0.3). Do this for n circles, then pass centres and radii to SLSQP as the start. This gives a feasible-ish start with varied radii.

items.title: Two-phase penalty then SLSQP polish
items.spec: Phase one: minimise a penalised objective -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2) over (c, r) with L-BFGS-B, using bounds 0 <= r and 0 <= c <= 1 and mu = 10. Phase two: take the output and run SLSQP with the exact constraints for the remaining budget. Penalty gradients are cheap to write analytically, and the penalised stage gives smoother starting points than raw random SLSQP.

items.title: Continuation on penalty weight
items.spec: Optimise a soft-overlap objective with L-BFGS-B, starting with a small penalty weight mu = 1 and multiplying it by 4 after each round, for about 6 rounds. Use warm starts between rounds. Finish with an SLSQP run on the exact constraints. The schedule drives the packing from loose to feasible without the hard-constraint solver getting stuck early.

items.title: Elite pool with mutation
items.spec: Maintain a pool of the 5 best distinct packings found so far (by repaired radius sum). Each restart either draws a fresh uniform start (probability 0.3) or picks a random pool member and applies a mutation: move 2 random circles to random positions and jitter the rest by N(0, 0.01). Run SLSQP on the mutated start and insert the result into the pool if it qualifies.

items.title: Cheap screening then full optimisation
items.spec: Run many short SLSQP restarts with maxiter 40 to screen starts quickly. Keep only the top 10% by repaired radius sum and run them to maxiter 300 for the final refinement. This spends most of the budget on many cheap starts and reserves the expensive solve for the promising ones.

items.title: Early abandonment of weak restarts
items.spec: Wrap the SLSQP objective with a callback that records the current objective each iteration. If after 30 iterations the objective (negated radius sum, feasibility ignored) is worse than the incumbent's sum by more than 0.3, abort the restart. SciPy SLSQP does not allow abort directly, so raise a custom exception inside the constraint or objective function and catch it. Only completed restarts are repaired and compared.

items.title: Warm-start chaining across restarts
items.spec: Instead of always starting from uniform random points, alternate between fresh starts and a warm start: take the last accepted packing, scale its radii by 0.9, and add N(0, 0.02) to centres before SLSQP. Accept each result as the new chain state only if it is at least 99% of the incumbent's sum, otherwise restart the chain from the incumbent.

items.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP conditioning
items.spec: Optimise over scaled variables z = (c, r) / s, with s = 0.5 for centres and s = 0.1 for radii, so that all decision variables are of order one. Map back before the repair step. Also divide each constraint by its typical scale (for example, 2 * 0.1) so that SLSQP's step tolerance is comparable across constraint types.

items.title: Trust-constr polish
items.spec: After SLSQP returns, run scipy.optimize.minimize with method trust-constr on the same objective and constraints, starting from the SLSQP solution, with maxiter 200. Keep whichever of the two results has the larger repaired radius sum. The interior-point style method can converge further on the active set, typically adding a few thousandths.

items.title: Active-set Newton polish
items.spec: After SLSQP, identify the contacts: pairs with gap below 1e-6 and walls with slack below 1e-6. Solve the system of active equalities (pair distances equal r_i + r_j, wall contacts equal r) with Gauss-Newton or least squares starting from the SLSQP solution, which is usually very close. Accept the refined packing only if all constraints remain satisfied within 1e-12, otherwise keep the SLSQP result.

items.title: LP radius refinement at fixed centres
items.spec: Replace the pairwise-shrink repair with an exact LP. With the centres fixed, maximise sum(r) subject to r_i >= 0, r_i <= wall distance, and r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, using scipy.optimize.linprog with the HiGHS method. Subtract a tiny margin (1e-12) from the result to satisfy the strict tolerance. This recovers radius sum lost by the crude shrink step.

items.title: Smarter overlap repair
items.spec: Replace the greedy max-overlap repair with a sweep: for each circle in order of increasing radius, shrink it to the largest value that clears all current neighbours and the walls, then repeat the sweep until no overlap remains. Keep the final SHRINK margin. This wastes less radius than scaling the pair jointly, so each restart's score is more accurate.

items.title: Adaptive time allocation
items.spec: Track how many restarts have produced a new incumbent. Start with 2 seconds per restart. If the last 10 restarts did not improve the incumbent, double the SLSQP maxiter and the time per restart, up to the total budget. Return to the short setting after an improvement. This shifts effort toward the more difficult start regime when progress stalls.

items.title: Noise schedule on incumbent perturbation
items.spec: Once an incumbent exists, perturb it each iteration by Gaussian noise on centres with standard deviation that decays geometrically from 0.05 to 0.001 across the time budget, then re-run SLSQP. Accept if the repaired sum improves. Large early perturbations explore, and small late perturbations refine.

items.title: Radius-first initialisation
items.spec: Sample initial radii from a Beta distribution with shape parameters (2, 5) scaled to a maximum of 0.12, and sample centres uniformly in the square respecting the walls. Start SLSQP from these, so that the initial packing has a broad size spread instead of uniform radii. Varying the start distribution across restarts adds diversity without changing the optimiser.

items.title: Log-barrier on radii to avoid collapse
items.spec: Add a regularisation term to the SLSQP objective: minus sum(r) minus 1e-4 * sum(log(r)) to discourage circles from shrinking to zero during early iterations, where SLSQP can get stuck with degenerate tiny circles. Use a small weight so the final optimum is almost unchanged; anneal the weight to zero over the first half of the SLSQP run.

items.title: Symmetric initialisation
items.spec: For half of the restarts, build initial centres in mirror-symmetric pairs about the line x = 0.5 (generate n/2 random points in the left half and reflect them, with one centre on the axis if n is odd). Run SLSQP on the full unconstrained problem. The symmetric starts land in different basins from uniform random starts, which broadens the search.

items.title: Jittered restart with fixed seeds per restart
items.spec: Derive a separate numpy generator for each restart from the base seed and the restart index, using np.random.SeedSequence(seed).spawn, so that each restart's random draws are independent of how many restarts ran before. This makes the search stable under time-limit variation and easier to replicate across the three seeds.

items.title: Tighter SLSQP tolerances and more iterations
items.spec: Set SLSQP ftol to 1e-12 and maxiter to 500 for the final restart only, keeping MAX_ITER = 200 for the screening restarts. Also raise the TIME_FRACTION so the full 30 s budget is used safely, leaving a 5 s margin for the repair step. Extra iterations let SLSQP converge fully on the best starts.

items.title: Dropout of constraints in early SLSQP
items.spec: Run the first SLSQP round with only the pair constraints whose centre distance is below 0.4 and the wall constraints, then add all pair constraints for a second round. Early rounds then operate on a smaller constraint set and move faster. The second round enforces the full feasibility conditions.

items.title: Batch the random starts through a vectorised objective
items.spec: Evaluate many random starts together by computing the constraint violation and radius sum for a batch of candidate packings in one vectorised numpy call, and choose the 5 starts with the largest feasible-looking radius sum to send to SLSQP. Batch scoring of starts is cheap compared with a full SLSQP run, so this filters poor starts without optimiser cost.

items.title: Boundary-biased random starts
items.spec: Sample a fraction (about 40%) of initial centres near the walls, with coordinates drawn from a distribution that places mass at 0.05 to 0.2 and 0.8 to 0.95, and the rest uniform in the interior. Good packings for this problem put many circles along the edges, so this biases the starts toward the right structure.

items.title: Random number reuse for convergence check
items.spec: Track the repaired radius sum across restarts. Stop early once the incumbent has not improved for 40 consecutive restarts and at least 50% of the time budget has been spent, then return the incumbent. This releases unused time and avoids wasting budget on exhausted search, though the time limit is still respected.

items.title: Regularised random restarts with weight decay on radii
items.spec: Add a small quadratic penalty 1e-3 * sum((r - r_mean)^2) to the SLSQP objective to discourage a few large circles dominating and to spread radii more evenly before the final polish. Remove the penalty in the last 20% of the SLSQP iterations by running a second SLSQP call with only the true objective, starting from the first result.

items.title: Analytic constraint Jacobian for SLSQP
items.spec: Pass a jac argument to scipy minimize (SLSQP) giving the gradient of the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and the Jacobian of cons, built in vectorised numpy from the iu pair indices: for each pair row, the partial derivatives of the centre distance and of the two radii; boundary rows are simple unit fills. This replaces finite differencing of a 500+ row constraint vector, so each iteration is much cheaper and more restarts fit in the budget.

items.title: Raise SLSQP iteration cap and tighten tolerance
items.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 and pass options ftol=1e-12. Many restarts currently stop at the iteration cap before converging, so the comparison between basins is noisy. Letting each local solve reach a true local maximum makes the best restart reliable; leave the time loop unchanged.

items.title: Final SLSQP polish of the incumbent
items.spec: After the restart loop selects the best (c, r), run one more SLSQP solve starting from that configuration instead of a random start, with ftol=1e-12 and a few hundred iterations, reserving about 10 percent of the time budget for it. Then clip and repair as before. This recovers radius sum lost to optimiser slack and to the repair shrink.

items.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent
items.spec: Replace most fresh random starts with perturbations of the current best packing. Each step copies the incumbent centres, adds Gaussian noise of scale 0.05 to 3 to 6 randomly chosen circles, resets those radii to 0.05, runs the same SLSQP and repair, and accepts the new packing only if its radius sum is larger. Keep a small fraction of fresh random starts for diversity.

items.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle
items.spec: After each local solve, identify the circle with the smallest radius, delete it, and reinsert it at the point of the unit square farthest from all other centres (sampled on a 200 by 200 grid, maximising distance to the nearest centre minus its radius). Re-run SLSQP from this configuration. Accept if the radius sum improves. This moves wasted circles into holes.

items.title: Iterated local search over the k weakest circles
items.spec: Perturb the incumbent by removing k circles, k drawn from 2 to 4, chosen with probability proportional to their small radii, and reinserting them at random positions with radius 0.02. Re-optimise with SLSQP and repair. Keep the change only if the radius sum improves, otherwise revert. Stop when the time budget is spent.

items.title: Hexagonal lattice initialisation with jitter
items.spec: Add a second class of starting points: a hexagonal or square-ish lattice of 32 points inside [0.1, 0.9]^2 chosen at random among a few row counts, with uniform jitter of 0.03 added. Alternate between these lattice starts and the uniform random starts, using the seed to select. Lattice starts often land in better basins for equal-sized packings.

items.title: Greedy max-min-distance seeding
items.spec: Generate initial centres by farthest-point sampling: the first centre is random, and each further centre is placed at the candidate point (a random sample of 2000 points in [0,1]^2) that maximises its distance to the nearest existing centre. Give the resulting centres initial radii equal to half their nearest-neighbour distance, clipped to the box. This gives well-spread starts instead of uniform random ones.

items.title: Randomised initial radii
items.spec: Replace the constant INIT_RADIUS starting radii with independent uniform draws from [0.01, 0.12] per circle, using rng. Varied radii break the symmetry of the start and let the optimiser assign size to circles that have room, which can lead to different local maxima than equal starts.

items.title: Successive halving over restarts
items.spec: Run a batch of 24 short random restarts with MAX_ITER set to 60. Keep the best quarter by radius sum, then re-run those survivors with MAX_ITER 400 from their last iterate. Repeat once more for the best few. Budget the time so each round uses roughly equal CPU, and return the best final packing after repair.

items.title: Adaptive time fraction
items.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9, keeping the total CPU use under the 45 s limit with margin. Measure the CPU time of each local solve and stop starting new restarts when the next one would exceed the 0.9 budget. This uses more of the allowed time without risking a voided job.

items.title: Penalty continuation before SLSQP
items.spec: Before each SLSQP solve, run an unconstrained L-BFGS-B minimisation of the penalised objective: minus radius sum plus mu times the squared overlap and boundary violations, with mu increasing geometrically from 10 to 1e6 over five stages. Feed the result to SLSQP as the start. The smooth penalty landscape guides circles into a good arrangement before the hard constraints are imposed.

items.title: Annealed position jitter during restarts
items.spec: Within one local solve, run SLSQP several times in sequence. Between runs, add Gaussian noise to centres with standard deviation decreasing from 0.03 to 0.001 over the rounds, then re-solve. Keep the best. This is a cheap annealed search over nearby basins, using the same rng for reproducibility.

items.title: Soft minimum gap regularisation
items.spec: Add a small penalty term to the early SLSQP or L-BFGS objective that rewards large pairwise gaps, for example minus epsilon times the log-sum-exp of negative pair slacks, with epsilon set to 1e-3 and decayed to zero in the final stage. This keeps circles spread out at the start so that they do not jam into a poor arrangement, while the final stage optimises the true sum.

items.title: Shrink-factor slack during optimisation
items.spec: Impose the pair constraints in SLSQP with a margin, requiring distance at least r_i plus r_j plus 1e-7 and boundary margins of 1e-7. Then the output needs no repair shrink and is strictly valid. This removes the repair step's loss while keeping the harness tolerance of 1e-10 satisfied with a comfortable margin.

items.title: Sparse neighbour pair constraints
items.spec: Build the pair constraint set from only pairs whose centre distance is below 0.35 at the start of each local solve, instead of all 496 pairs. Recompute the active pair list after each SLSQP call and re-solve if any excluded pair now overlaps. This shrinks the constraint matrix and speeds up each SLSQP iteration.

items.title: Bound constraints instead of boundary inequalities
items.spec: Express the box constraints as scipy bounds on the centre variables: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, 0.5] as bounds, and keep only the pair constraints as nonlinear inequalities. Boundary rows of the constraint vector are then removed, which shrinks the SLSQP problem and reduces its per-iteration linear algebra cost.

items.title: Symmetric parametrisation
items.spec: Optimise over a quarter of the circles and mirror them across the vertical and horizontal midlines to form the full packing, with circles on the axes handled as their own parameters. Many best-known equal-radius packings are symmetric, so the reduced problem is smaller and easier to search. Fall back to the full problem as one of the restart types.

items.title: Alternating radii and centre optimisation
items.spec: Alternate between two subproblems: with centres fixed, maximise the radius sum with a linear program in the radii subject to pair and boundary linear constraints (scipy linprog); with radii fixed, move centres by a short SLSQP or gradient step to increase the minimal slack. Repeat until the radius sum stops improving. This decouples the nonconvex coupling into simpler steps.

items.title: Sequential linear programming with trust region
items.spec: Linearise the pair distance constraints around the current centres and radii, solve the resulting linear program maximising the radius sum with variable steps bounded by a trust radius of 0.05 (scipy linprog with highs), accept the step if the true radius sum improves and the packing stays valid, and otherwise halve the trust radius. Iterate until the trust radius is below 1e-7.

items.title: Smoothed objective with log-sum-exp
items.spec: For the L-BFGS-B stage, replace the hard pair constraints by a smooth penalty built from the log-sum-exp of the negative slacks with a temperature that decreases over the run. Minimise minus radius sum plus the penalty using analytic gradients, then finish with SLSQP. Smooth gradients make each stage much cheaper than SLSQP alone.

items.title: Sigmoid parametrisation of centres
items.spec: Parametrise centres as 0.5 + 0.5 tanh(u) for unconstrained u, and radii as softplus of unconstrained values, so the box constraints hold by construction. Then run L-BFGS-B on the penalised overlap objective, followed by SLSQP only on the pair constraints. This removes the boundary constraints from the active optimiser.

items.title: Elite pool with crossover
items.spec: Maintain a pool of the 5 best packings found so far. For each new start, pick two parents at random, take the centres of the left half of one and the right half of the other, fill any missing circles with random points, and set radii to 0.05. Run SLSQP and repair. This recombines good partial structures across restarts.

items.title: Parallel batch of restarts with shared start
items.spec: Generate a batch of 8 starting configurations per round from the same seed stream, solve each locally with SLSQP at a reduced MAX_ITER of 150, and keep the best 2 for a full-length solve. Process the batch sequentially in one thread with process_time accounting. Batching the early screen spends less time on hopeless starts.

items.title: Stronger repair by iterative pairwise scaling
