items.spec: Replace the 50-pass repair with iterated full sweeps: for every overlapping pair in index order, scale both radii by the ratio distance over radius sum, and repeat until no pair overlaps, with a cap of 1000 sweeps. This converges to a valid packing that keeps more of the radius sum than the current single-worst-pair loop, which stops at 50 passes.

items.title: Exact feasible radii via min-ratio LP
items.spec: After the centres are fixed, compute the largest feasible radii by solving a linprog maximising the radius sum subject to r_i + r_j <= distance_ij and r_i <= boundary distance for each circle. The LP gives the exact optimum for those centres in double precision, avoiding the heuristic repair entirely. Then subtract 1e-12 from every radius for safety.

items.title: Shrink-factor tuned to tolerance
items.spec: Replace the SHRINK constant of 1e-9 by a final global scale of the radii, multiplying all radii by (1 - 1e-10) after repair, and verify validity with an exact pairwise check before returning. This keeps the reported radius sum as large as possible while the harness tolerance of 1e-10 remains respected.

items.title: Multi-scale seed schedule
items.spec: Start with a coarse search using 16 random restarts and MAX_ITER 100, then take the best 4 and run one full MAX_ITER 1000 solve for each with random perturbation scale 0.02, then polish the best. Allocate the time as 50, 30 and 20 percent across the three stages. This concentrates effort on promising basins rather than uniform restarts.

items.title: Monotonic basin hopping from the incumbent
items.spec: After the first random SLSQP start, keep the best packing found so far. For each later iteration, copy the incumbent, add Gaussian noise (sd about 0.02) to all centres, re-draw the radii as 0.9 times the incumbent radii, run _solve_once-style SLSQP from that point, repair, and accept only if the repaired sum of radii improves. Fall back to a fresh random start every 50 iterations without improvement. Keep the seed-driven rng for all draws.

items.title: Relocate the smallest circle into the largest hole
items.spec: Perturbation move for basin hopping: take the incumbent packing, remove the circle with the smallest radius, and place it at the point of a 200x200 grid over [0,1]^2 that maximises the distance to all other circle boundaries (largest empty space, clipped to the square). Re-optimise with SLSQP, repair, and accept if the sum of radii improves.

items.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP
items.spec: Supply the constraint Jacobian and objective gradient to minimize() via the jac argument for the constraints dict, instead of letting SLSQP finite-difference the 496 pair constraints. Pair-distance derivatives are (c_i - c_j)/d with respect to centres and -1 with respect to both radii; boundary constraints are simple unit entries. This reduces per-iteration cost and lets more restarts fit in the time budget.

items.title: Sparse neighbour-list constraints
items.spec: Only include pair non-overlap constraints for pairs whose centres are closer than a threshold (for example 2.4 times the mean radius of 0.09 plus margin), rebuilding the pair list at the start of each SLSQP call. Far-apart pairs cannot overlap in a nearby solution, so dropping them shrinks the constraint vector and speeds each iteration. Re-check all pairs in the final repair step so validity is unchanged.

items.title: Use bounds instead of boundary constraints
items.spec: Pass box bounds to SLSQP through the bounds argument: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. Keep only the pair-overlap inequalities as constraints, and keep the boundary-containment inequalities c_i - r_i >= 0 and 1 - c_i - r_i >= 0 as constraints too, since bounds alone do not enforce containment. This removes the redundant r >= 0 constraints and trims the constraint count by 4n.

items.title: Two-phase equal-then-free optimisation
items.spec: In each restart, first solve a sub-problem where all radii are tied to a single variable r (maximise r subject to non-overlap and containment), which is a smaller and better conditioned problem. Use its centres as the starting point for the full problem where each radius is free, so the free solve starts near a good basin rather than from random radii.

items.title: Quadratic penalty continuation
items.spec: Replace the hard constraints with a penalty objective: minimise minus the sum of radii plus mu times the sum of squared positive violations, using L-BFGS-B with box bounds. Start mu at 10 and multiply by 10 each stage for 5 stages, warm-starting each stage from the last. Finish with one SLSQP call on the true constraints to certify a feasible local optimum before repair.

items.title: Tighter SLSQP tolerance and iteration budget
items.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 500 and pass options ftol=1e-12 to SLSQP so each local solve converges fully instead of stopping early. Use the extra budget per restart only when the previous restart finished with status 0 to avoid wasting time on diverged runs.

items.title: Use more of the time budget safely
items.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 so the restart loop uses about 27 s of the 30 s CPU budget. The harness kills calls above 45 s, so this leaves a wide margin. Also check time before each restart, not only at the loop head, so a long SLSQP call cannot push the total past the target.

items.title: Stagnation-triggered early stop and reset
items.spec: Track the number of consecutive restarts or basin-hopping steps that fail to improve the incumbent. When this count reaches 30, reset to a fresh random start and keep the global best unchanged. This frees time from stuck basins into new ones instead of spending the whole budget on the same local optimum.

items.title: Gradually shrinking perturbation scale
items.spec: In basin hopping, set the centre perturbation sd to start at 0.05 and decay geometrically by a factor of 0.97 each accepted-or-rejected step, floored at 0.005. Large early kicks explore basins; small late kicks refine the best one. Reset the scale to 0.05 whenever a new incumbent is found.

items.title: Log-parameterised radii
items.spec: Optimise log-radii instead of radii, so radii r = exp(s) stay strictly positive without a r >= 0 constraint. Apply the chain rule to any analytic gradients. This removes the nonnegativity constraints and avoids SLSQP stepping into negative radius values that the repair step then has to clip.

items.title: Repulsive regularisation in the first solve
items.spec: Add a soft repulsion term, sum over pairs of 1/(d_ij squared plus eps), with a small weight (for example 1e-3) to the objective of the first SLSQP solve only. This spreads circles apart early and steers the solve away from jammed configurations. Drop the term for the final polishing solve so the reported objective is the true sum of radii.

items.title: Random jitter of radii between solves
items.spec: After each local solve, multiply every radius by a factor uniform in [0.8, 1.0] and re-run SLSQP from those centres and radii. This shakes the packing out of the current constraint set so the next solve can find a different contact graph. Keep the best repaired result across all jitter steps.

items.title: Shrink margin before final polish
items.spec: After the repair step, run one more SLSQP solve from the repaired packing with each radius reduced by 1e-7 as a safety margin, then repair again. The repair step typically shrinks many radii by a larger amount than needed; a final constrained solve recovers part of that loss while preserving strict feasibility under the harness tolerance.

items.title: Replace repair with a targeted fixer
items.spec: Replace the worst-pair loop in _repair with a pass that, for every overlapping pair, shrinks the two radii in proportion to their overlap (scaling each by the share of the total excess they cause), iterated until no overlap exceeds 1e-12. This converges in fewer steps and loses less total radius than repeatedly scaling only the single worst pair.

items.title: Over-provision then drop
items.spec: Solve for 33 circles instead of 32 in each restart, then delete the circle with the smallest radius and run a short SLSQP polish on the remaining 32 starting from those centres and radii. Extra circles give the optimiser slack that helps escape jammed contact graphs, and the deletion keeps the output size at n.

items.title: Grow the packing incrementally
items.spec: Start with 20 circles and optimise them. Insert each new circle into the largest available hole (grid search as in the relocation move), re-optimise the full set, and repeat until n circles are placed. The incremental build produces better starting contact graphs than uniform random placement at n equal to 32.

items.title: Uniform random starts replaced by Latin hypercube
items.spec: Generate initial centres with a Latin hypercube sample over [0.05, 0.95]^2 instead of independent uniform draws, using the seeded rng. Stratified starts cover the square evenly and reduce the chance that several restarts share the same clustered initial layout.

items.title: Farthest-point initial centres
items.spec: Initialise each restart's centres with farthest-point sampling: draw 2000 random candidates, then greedily pick 32 points each maximising the minimum distance to those already chosen. Use these as starting centres with radius 0.05 and run SLSQP. Well-spread starts give SLSQP a feasible-ish starting point with fewer overlaps to resolve.

items.title: Varied initial radius per restart
items.spec: Draw the initial radius for each restart uniformly from [0.02, 0.12] using the seeded rng instead of the fixed INIT_RADIUS of 0.05. Different starting sizes push SLSQP toward different contact graphs, widening the set of basins that the restarts reach.

items.title: Ring and grid seeded starts
items.spec: Alternate restart types: half the restarts use a random layout as before, and the other half start from a jittered rectangular grid of about 6x6 cells with 32 of the cells chosen at random, with radii 0.08. Structured starts reach the dense lattice-like basins that random starts rarely hit at this n.

items.title: Elite pool crossover
items.spec: Keep the top 5 distinct packings found so far. For each new restart with probability 0.5, build a child by taking the centres from the left half (x below 0.5) of one elite and the right half from another, fill any count mismatch by re-sampling random points, and run SLSQP on the child. Otherwise start from a fresh random layout.

items.title: Successive halving over candidate starts
items.spec: Generate 16 random starts, run each for a short SLSQP budget (MAX_ITER 40), keep the best 4 by sum of radii, and continue only those to full MAX_ITER. Repeat the population budget across the time limit. Spending short runs on many candidates focuses compute on promising basins.

items.title: Parallel-style batched restarts with shared time
items.spec: Group the restart loop into batches of 4 starts. Within each batch, run all four to the same iteration cap, then continue only the best one to completion. This keeps the number of concurrently open problems bounded and stops the time from being spent fully finishing weak starts.

items.title: Trust-constr as an alternative local solver
items.spec: Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method trust-constr on the same constraints (with analytic sparse Jacobian) for the final polish of the best packing found. Trust-constr handles degenerate active sets differently from SLSQP and can improve the last digits of the sum of radii, after which the existing repair step guarantees validity.

items.title: Symmetric initial layouts
items.spec: For half the restarts, initialise centres in mirror-symmetric pairs across the diagonal x = y (generate 16 random points and add their swapped copies, with the 32nd point at a random diagonal position). Symmetric starts reduce the effective search dimension and frequently land on symmetric high-density packings.

items.title: Simulated annealing on radii weights
items.spec: Between SLSQP solves, perturb the relative radius profile by multiplying each radius by exp(N(0, T)) with temperature T starting at 0.1 and decaying geometrically to 0.001 over the time budget, then re-optimise the centres. Accept the new packing with Metropolis probability on the repaired sum of radii. This explores which circles are large and which are small.
